1.A.8.1.1.description: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF. Transports various polyols with decreasing rates as size increases ( Heller et al. 1980 ); also transports arsenite (As(III) and antimonite (Sb(III)) ( Meng et al ., 2004 ). Oligomerization may play a role in determining the rates of transport ( Klein et al. 2019 ). AQP water permeability through GlpF can be regulated by lipid bilayer asymmetry and the transmembrane…
1.A.8.1.1.name: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF.

1.A.8.1.2.description: Aqp1 of 270 aas and 6 TMSs. Induced by NH 3 but not CO 2 , but transports both gases. Aqp1 is found in the plasma membrae as well as the ER/chloroplast. Aqp1 may be involved in photoprotection. It may facilitate the efflux of NH3, preventing the uncoupling effect of high intracellular ammonia concentrations ( Matsui et al. 2018 ).
1.A.8.1.2.name: Aqp1 of 270 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.1.description: Tonoplast intrinsic protein, TIPA or Tip3.1, of 268 aas and 6 TMSs. Phylogenetic distribution, structure, transport dynamics, gating mechanism, sub-cellular localization, tissue-specific expression, and co-expression of TIPs have been reviewed to define their versatile role in plants ( Sudhakaran et al. 2021 ). Based on the phylogenetic distribution, TIPs are classified into five distinct groups…
1.A.8.10.1.name: Tonoplast intrinsic protein, TIPA or Tip3.1, of 268 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.10.description: Aquaporin TIP2-1 (Delta-tonoplast intrinsic protein) (Delta-TIP) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein 2-1) (AtTIP2;1) ( Daniels et al. 1996 ). Transports water and ammonia, and can be activated by mercury ( Kirscht et al. 2016 ). The 3-d structure is known to 1.2Å resolution ( Kirscht et al. 2016 ). It may participate in vacuolar compartmentation and detoxification of ammonium.
1.A.8.10.10.name: Aquaporin TIP2-1 (Delta-tonoplast intrinsic protein) (Delta-TIP) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein 2-1) (AtTIP2;1).

1.A.8.10.11.name: Probable aquaporin TIP-type alpha (Alpha TIP) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein alpha)

1.A.8.10.15.description: The Aquaporin-8 (Aqp8) transporter is permeable to water, NH 3 , formamide and H 2 O 2 , and it is present in the inner membrane of mitochondria and the plasma membrane ( Bienert et al ., 2007 ; Saparov et al ., 2007 ; Soria et al. , 2010 ). Cholesterol, via sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) transcription factors, activates or represses genes involved in its hepatic biosynthetic…
1.A.8.10.15.name: The Aquaporin-8 (Aqp8) transporter is permeable to water, NH 3 , formamide and H 2 O 2 , and it is present in the inner membrane of mitochondria and…

1.A.8.10.16.description: Aqp8a.1 of 260 aas and 6 TMSs. The spaciotemporal pattern of induction of three aquaporins during embyonic development in Zebrafish has been determined, and all three, Aqp8a.1, Aqp8a.2 and Aqp8b, show distictive patterns ( Koun et al. 2016).
1.A.8.10.16.name: Aqp8a.1 of 260 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.17.description: Aquaporin of 250 aas and 6 TMSs. It is a water channel required to facilitate the transport of water across membranes; it is involved in osmotolerance ( Ghosh et al. 2006 ).
1.A.8.10.17.name: Aquaporin of 250 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.18.description: Aqp0a of 263 aas and 6 TMSs. Zebrafish optical development requires regulated water permeability by Aquaporin 0 ( Safrina et al. 2024 ). Localization and expression of Aquaporin 0 (AQP0) in the Tissues of the Spiny Dogfish have been reported ( Cutler et al. 2026 ).
1.A.8.10.18.name: Aqp0a of 263 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.2.name: Tonoplast intrinsic protein-a

1.A.8.10.3.description: Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1.1 of 251 aas and probably 6 TMSs. TIPs control water trade among cytosolic and vacuolar compartments and can also transport glycerol, ammonia, urea, hydrogen peroxide, metals/metalloids, and several amino acids ( Liu et al. 2003 ). Additionally, TIPs, which can be responsive to nitrogen availability and salt sensitivity, are engaged with different abiotic stress…
1.A.8.10.3.name: Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1.1 of 251 aas and probably 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.4.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) NH 3 channel, TIP2;3 ( Loque et al ., 2005 ). [Tip2;2 of wheat is also an NH 3 /H 2 O channel ( Bertl and Kaldenhoff, 2007 )].
1.A.8.10.4.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) NH 3 channel, TIP2;3. [Tip2;2 of wheat is also an NH 3 /H 2 O channel].

1.A.8.10.5.description: Endoplasmic reticulum Small and Basic Intrinsic Protein; (SIP1;1) water channel (present in all plant tissues except seeds) ( Ishikawa et al. , 2005 ) May play a role in gas and water exchange between the plant and its environment via stromata (turgor-driven epidermal valves) and the hydathode pore ( Pillitteri et al ., 2008 ).
1.A.8.10.5.name: Endoplasmic reticulum Small and Basic Intrinsic Protein; (SIP1;1) water channel (present in all plant tissues except seeds) May play a role in gas…

1.A.8.10.6.description: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin, Tip1;3 ( Soto et al. 2008 )
1.A.8.10.6.name: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin, Tip1;3

1.A.8.10.7.description: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin. Tip5;1 ( Soto et al. 2008 ) An aquaporin specifically targeted to pollen mitochondria; probably involved in nitrogen remobilization ( Soto et al. , 2010 ).
1.A.8.10.7.name: The pollen-specific water/urea aquaporin.

1.A.8.10.8.description: Aquaporin-B, AqpB of 294 aas and 6 TMSs. Tyr216 in loop D is a key residue in gating, possibly involving phosphorylation. Mutation of Tyr216 to aspartate or glutamate initiated water permeability. The truncated, permanently open AqpB yielded cells with reduced capability to cope with hypotonic stress ( von Bülow et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.10.8.name: Aquaporin-B, AqpB of 294 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.10.9.description: Aquaporin TIP1-2 (Gamma-tonoplast intrinsic protein 2) (Gamma-TIP2) (Salt stress-induced tonoplast intrinsic protein) (Tonoplast intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtTIP1;2)
1.A.8.10.9.name: Aquaporin TIP1-2 (Gamma-tonoplast intrinsic protein 2) (Gamma-TIP2) (Salt stress-induced tonoplast intrinsic protein)

1.A.8.11.10.description: Pip2-4 of 291 aas with 6 TMSs. In tobacco plants, overexpression of the NtPIP2;4 gene can enhance drought resistance ( Luo et al. 2025 ).
1.A.8.11.10.name: Pip2-4 of 291 aas with 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.11.11.description: PIP2-4 water channel of286 aas and 6 TMSs. The PIP2;4 aquaporin water channel, primarily expressed in roots of rice, mediates both water and nonselective Na + and K + conductance ( Tran et al. 2025 ).
1.A.8.11.11.name: PIP2-4 water channel of286 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.11.2.description: The plasma membrane aquaporin, NtAQP1 (H 2 O and CO 2 permeable; important for photosynthesis, stomatal opening and leaf growth) ( Uehlein et al ., 2003 ; Uehlein et al ., 2008 )
1.A.8.11.2.name: The plasma membrane aquaporin, NtAQP1 (H 2 O and CO 2 permeable; important for photosynthesis, stomatal opening and leaf growth)

1.A.8.11.3.description: Plasma membrane aquaporin 1, PIP1, PIP1;2, PIP1b, of 286 aas and 6 TMSs (Törnroth- Horsefield et al ., 2006 ). Transports H 2 O, H 2 O 2 ( Dynowski et al ., 2008 ), O 2 and CO 2 ( Zwiazek et al. 2017 ) . Forms active heterotetramers with PIP2;1 (1.A.8.11.4); down regulated under drought stress ( Najafabadi et al ., 2008 ); plays a role in salt tolerance ( Li et al. 2018 ). Gated by H + , Ca 2+…
1.A.8.11.3.name: Plasma membrane aquaporin 1, PIP1, PIP1;2, PIP1b, of 286 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.11.5.description: Probable aquaporin PIP2-6 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-6) (AtPIP2;6) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2e) (PIP2e). In the radish ( Raphaus sativus ), there are 61 genes encoding aquaporins, and RsPIP2-6 is induced with high NaCl, and is involved in the salt stress response ( Yi et al. 2022 ). The plasma membrane intrinsic protein OsPIP2;6 is involved in root-to-shoot arsenic…
1.A.8.11.5.name: Probable aquaporin PIP2-6 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-6) (AtPIP2;6) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2e) (PIP2e).

1.A.8.11.6.description: Aquaporin PIP2-8 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-8) (AtPIP2;8) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 3b) (PIP3b). This protein as well as 1.A.8.11.4 are possibly orthologous to spinach PIP1;2 for which the crystal structure is available (PDP# 4JC6) ( Berny et al. 2016 ).
1.A.8.11.6.name: Aquaporin PIP2-8 (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 2-8) (AtPIP2;8) (Plasma membrane intrinsic protein 3b) (PIP3b).

1.A.8.11.7.description: Aquaporin PIP2;5 (PIP2-5) of 285 aas. Transports water and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) ( Bienert et al. 2014 ; ). PIP1;2 doesn't transport H 2 O 2 . TMS3 contains an LxxA motif that targets the protein to the plasma membrane from the ER. While PIP2s are in the plasma mebrane, PIP1s are retained in the ER; this motif only partly explains the difference ( Chevalier and Chaumont 2015 ). PIP1;2 AND…
1.A.8.11.7.name: Aquaporin PIP2;5 (PIP2-5) of 285 aas.

1.A.8.11.8.description: Aqp2 of 297 aas and 6 TMSs. Induced by both NH 3 and CO 2 , and transports both gases. Aqp2 is found in the plasma membrane and may be involved in photoprotection. It may facilitate the efflux of NH3, preventing the uncoupling effect of high intracellular ammonia concentrations ( Matsui et al. 2018 ).
1.A.8.11.8.name: Aqp2 of 297 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.11.9.description: Water channel, Aqp2-3 or Aqp2;3 or PIP2C of 285 aas and 6 TMSs. Ectopic expression of CrPIP2;3, a plasma membrane intrinsic protein gene from the halophyte, Canavalia rosea , enhanced drought and salt-alkali stress tolerance in Arabidopsis ( Zheng et al. 2021 ). The Arabidopsis ortholog is presented here.
1.A.8.11.9.name: Water channel, Aqp2-3 or Aqp2;3 or PIP2C of 285 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.12.1.description: Nodulin-26 aquaporin and glycerol facilitator, NIP ( de Paula Santos Martins et al. 2015 ). Transports NH 3 5-fold better than water in Hg 2+ -sensitive fashion ( Hwang et al. , 2010 ).
1.A.8.12.1.name: Nodulin-26 aquaporin and glycerol facilitator, NIP.

1.A.8.12.10.description: Arsenite export pore, AqpS ( Yang et al ., 2005 )
1.A.8.12.10.name: Arsenite export pore, AqpS

1.A.8.12.13.description: Rice NIP2.1 (NIP2-1; NIP2;1) of 295 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs. It transports metaloids such as arsenous acid (arsenic) and silisic acid (silicon). The 3-D structure has been determined ( Sharma et al. 2023 ). This protein is most similar to TC# 1.A.8.12.2 within TCDB.
1.A.8.12.13.name: Rice NIP2.1 (NIP2-1; NIP2;1) of 295 aas and 6 or 7 TMSs.

1.A.8.12.2.description: The silicon (silicic acid) (undissociated form) transporter, Lsi1 ( Ma et al ., 2007a , b; Mitani et al ., 2008 ). The barley orthologue Lsi1 (also called NIP2-1) is also a silicon (silicic acid) uptake channel ( Chiba et al. , 2009 ). Rice Lsi1 also transports arsenite and pentavalent mono and dimethyl arsenite ( Li et al. , 2009 ). In addition to silicon (Si), selenite (Se) uptake is mediated…
1.A.8.12.2.name: The silicon (silicic acid) (undissociated form) transporter, Lsi1.

1.A.8.12.3.description: The boric acid channel protein, NIP5;1 (expressed in the root elongation zone and root hairs in response to boron deficiency) ( Takano et al ., 2006 ). Borate is an essential nutrient in plants. The ortholog in Brassica napus ( XP_013652160.1 ) is 301 aas in length with 6 TMSs and is 90% identical to the A. thaliana protein. Synthesis of the B. napus protein is induced in roots and shoots by a…
1.A.8.12.3.name: The boric acid channel protein, NIP5;1 (expressed in the root elongation zone and root hairs in response to boron deficiency).

1.A.8.12.4.description: The root-expressed MIP transporter of lactic acid, NIP2;1 (Nod26-like MIP-4; NLM4) (induced by water logging and anoxic stress; shows minimal water and glycerol transport). It may play a role in adaptation to lactic fermentaion under anaerobic stress ( Choi and Roberts, 2007 ). Lactic acid transport is induced by anoxic stress ( Choi and Roberts, 2007 ).
1.A.8.12.4.name: The root-expressed MIP transporter of lactic acid, NIP2;1 (Nod26-like MIP-4; NLM4)

1.A.8.12.5.description: The silicon (silicic acid) transporter, Nip2-2 (Nip2;2) ( Mitani et al ., 2008 ). Also transports arsenite ( Li et al. , 2009 ).
1.A.8.12.5.name: The silicon (silicic acid) transporter, Nip2-2 (Nip2;2).

1.A.8.12.6.description: Nip7;1 arsenite and borate channel ( Isayenkov and Maathuis, 2008 ; Li et al. , 2011 )
1.A.8.12.6.name: Nip7;1 arsenite and borate channel

1.A.8.12.7.description: Aquaporin NIP1-2 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtNIP1;2) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 2) (NodLikeMip2) (Protein NLM2). Selectivity filters play roles in determining aluminum transport by AtNIP1;2 ( Wang et al. 2021 ).
1.A.8.12.7.name: Aquaporin NIP1-2 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-2) (AtNIP1;2) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 2) (NodLikeMip2) (Protein NLM2).

1.A.8.12.8.description: Aquaporin NIP1-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-1) (AtNIP1;1) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 1) (NodLikeMip1) (Protein NLM1). NIP-like aquaporins transport water, but also arsenic, boric acid, sliicon, glycerol, urea, lactic acid and ammonia ( Mitani-Ueno et al. 2011 ; Hwang et al. 2010 ). The grape ortholog appears to transport the same molecules including water and glycerol, but also…
1.A.8.12.8.name: Aquaporin NIP1-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 1-1) (AtNIP1;1) (Nodulin-26-like major intrinsic protein 1) (NodLikeMip1) (Protein NLM1).

1.A.8.12.9.description: Aquaporin NIP6-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 6-1) (AtNIP6;1). The grape ortholog is impermeable to water, but permeable to glycerol ( Sabir et al. 2020 ).
1.A.8.12.9.name: Aquaporin NIP6-1 (NOD26-like intrinsic protein 6-1) (AtNIP6;1).

1.A.8.13.2.description: Hg 2+ -inhibitable aquaporin, AqpM (transports both water and glycerol as well as CO 2 ) ( Kozono et al ., 2003 ; Araya-Secchi et al. , 2011 ). Its 3-d structure has been determined to 1.7 Å. In AqpM, isoleucine replaces a key histidine residue found in the lumen of water channels, which becomes a glycine residue in aquaglyceroporins. As a result of this and other side-chain substituents in the…
1.A.8.13.2.name: Hg 2+ -inhibitable aquaporin, AqpM (transports both water and glycerol as well as CO 2 ).

1.A.8.13.3.description: Putative aquaporin, GlpF5, of 216 aas; probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.13.3.name: Putative aquaporin, GlpF5, of 216 aas; probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone.

1.A.8.13.4.description: Aquaporin, Aqp, of 222 aas and 6 TMSs. It functions in hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) export from the cell, relieving oxidative stress ( Tong et al. 2019 ). It is an H 2 O 2 -inducible bacterial "peroxiporin".
1.A.8.13.4.name: Aquaporin, Aqp, of 222 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.13.5.description: Aquaporin, Aqp9, of 231 aas and 6 TMSs. This protein co-localizes with the vacuolar proton pyrophosphatase to acidocalcisomes and the contractile vacuole complex ( Montalvetti et al. 2004 ) which are involved in osmoregulation ( Rohloff et al. 2004 ). Acidocalcisomes function as storage sites for cations and phosphorus, participate in PPi and poly P metabolism as well as volume regulation and are…
1.A.8.13.5.name: Aquaporin, Aqp9, of 231 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.2.12.description: Aquaglyceroporin, AagP, of 298 aas and 6 TMSs. This protein transports water, glycerol and H 2 O 2 . It catalyzes H 2 O 2 efflux during glycerol uptake and contributes to virulence in mice ( Zhu et al. 2023 ).
1.A.8.2.12.name: Aquaglyceroporin, AagP, of 298 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.2.2.description: Mixed function glycerol facilitator/aquaporin, GlpF ( Froger et al. 2001 ).
1.A.8.2.2.name: Mixed function glycerol facilitator/aquaporin, GlpF.

1.A.8.2.4.description: GlpF1; transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.2.4.name: GlpF1; transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid.

1.A.8.2.5.description: GlpF2. Transporter of water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.2.5.name: GlpF2.

1.A.8.2.6.description: GlpF3. Transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.2.6.name: GlpF3.

1.A.8.2.7.description: GlpF4. Transports water, dihydroxyacetone and glycerol as well as D,L-lactic acid ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.2.7.name: GlpF4.

1.A.8.2.8.description: Putative aquaporin, GlpF6. Probably transports water, glycerol and dihydroxyacetone ( Bienert et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.2.8.name: Putative aquaporin, GlpF6.

1.A.8.2.9.description: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF, of 248 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.2.9.name: Glycerol facilitator, GlpF, of 248 aas and 6 TMSs

1.A.8.3.1.description: Aquaporin Z water channel ( aqpZ gene expression is under sigma S control; induced at the onset of stationary phase) ( Mallo and Ashby, 2006 ). The high resolution 3-d structure is available (PDB 1RC2) revealing two re-entrant coil-helix domains from the selectivity filter ( Savage et al. 2003 ). Coupled mutations enabled glycerol transport ( Ping et al. 2018 ).
1.A.8.3.1.name: Aquaporin Z water channel ( aqpZ gene expression is under sigma S control; induced at the onset of stationary phase).

1.A.8.4.1.description: Intracellular endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized Aquaporin 11 (Aqp11, AqpX1) water channel (important for the development of kidney proximal tubules; disruption produces neonatally fatal polycystic kidneys ( Ishibashi 2006 ). Has a positively charged C-terminal amino acid cluster similar to the di-lysine motif (-KKXX) for ER retention ( Nozaki et al. , 2008 )). In the horse, AQP3 and AQP11 are…
1.A.8.4.1.name: Intracellular endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized Aquaporin 11 (Aqp11, AqpX1) water channel

1.A.8.4.3.description: Aquaporin 10, Aqp10 of 259 aas and 6 TMSs
1.A.8.4.3.name: Aquaporin 10, Aqp10 of 259 aas and 6 TMSs

1.A.8.4.4.description: Aquaporin of 263 aas and 7 TMSs ( Stavang et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.4.4.name: Aquaporin of 263 aas and 7 TMSs.

1.A.8.4.5.description: Aquaporin of 256 aas with 6 TMSs in a 3 (N-terminus) + 3 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement ( Zhou et al. 2018 ).
1.A.8.4.5.name: Aquaporin of 256 aas with 6 TMSs in a 3 (N-terminus) + 3 TMS (C-terminus) arrangement.

1.A.8.4.6.description: Aquaporin of 261 aas and 6 TMSs. Aquaporins may not play major roles in adapting to longterm survival in brackish water or they be regulated by non-transcriptional mechanisms like post-translational modifications ( Misyura et al. 2020 ).
1.A.8.4.6.name: Aquaporin of 261 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.5.1.description: FPS1 glycerol efflux facilitator. It is important for maintaining osmotic balance during mating-induced yeast cell fusion and for tolerating hypoosmotic shock; it also transports arsenite and antimonite). FPS1 is a homotetramer ( Beese-Sims et al. , 2011 ). It is important for osmo-adaptation by regulating intracellular glycerol levels during changes in external osmolarity. Upon high osmolarity…
1.A.8.5.1.name: FPS1 glycerol efflux facilitator.

1.A.8.5.2.description: Fps1 hyperactive orthologue of the S. cerevisiae Fps1 (1.A.8.5.1) ( Geijer et al. , 2012 ).
1.A.8.5.2.name: Fps1 hyperactive orthologue of the S. cerevisiae Fps1 (1.A.8.5.1).

1.A.8.6.1.description: Aqy1, aquaporin (mediates H 2 O efflux during sporulation) (spore maturation) ( Sidoux-Walter et al ., 2004 )
1.A.8.6.1.name: Aqy1, aquaporin (mediates H 2 O efflux during sporulation) (spore maturation)

1.A.8.6.2.description: Aquaporin-2 Aqy2 (plays a role in reducing surface hydrophobicity promoting cell dispersion during starvation and reproduction)
1.A.8.6.2.name: Aquaporin-2 Aqy2 (plays a role in reducing surface hydrophobicity promoting cell dispersion during starvation and reproduction)

1.A.8.6.3.description: Aquaporin, Aqy1 (PIP2-7 7). The subangstron (0.88Å) structure is available ( Kosinska Eriksson et al. 2013 ). the H-bond donor interactions of the NPA motif''s asparagine residues to passing water molecules are revealed. A polarized water-water H-bond configuration is observed within the channel. Four selectivity filter water positions are too closely spaced to be simultaneously occupied…

1.A.8.6.4.description: Water and CO 2 permeable aquaporin, AQP1, of an edible mycorhizal fungus (desert truffles) ( Navarro-Ródenas et al. 2012 ).
1.A.8.6.4.name: Water and CO 2 permeable aquaporin, AQP1, of an edible mycorhizal fungus (desert truffles).

1.A.8.7.1.description: Tobacco X-intrinsic protein (XIP1-1-β). Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water ( Bienert et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.7.1.name: Tobacco X-intrinsic protein (XIP1-1-β).

1.A.8.7.2.description: Potato X intrinsic protein, XIP1. Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water ( Bienert et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.7.2.name: Potato X intrinsic protein, XIP1.

1.A.8.7.3.description: Morning glory XIP-1-1-α. Transports glycerol, urea and boric acid, but not water ( Bienert et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.7.3.name: Morning glory XIP-1-1-α.

1.A.8.7.5.description: Aquaporin F (AqpF) of 321 aas and 6 TMSs. It transports water and glycerol, but additionally transporters hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) for signaling purposes ( Laothanachareon et al. 2023 ). It may be the only aquaporin capable of H 2 O 2 transport and signalling.
1.A.8.7.5.name: Aquaporin F (AqpF) of 321 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.1.description: Aquaporin 1 (CO 2 -, O 2 -, H 2 0 2- and nitrous oxide-permeable, water-selective, and monovalent cation (Li + . Na + and K + ) permeable) ( Zwiazek et al. 2017 ; Varadaraj and Kumari 2020 ; Nourmohammadi et al. 2024 ). Aquaporin-1 tunes pain perception by interacting with Na v 1.8 Na + channels in dorsal root ganglion neurons ( Zhang and Verkman, 2010 ). It is upregulated in skeletal muscle in…
1.A.8.8.1.name: Aquaporin 1 (CO 2 -, O 2 -, H 2 0 2- and nitrous oxide-permeable, water-selective, and monovalent cation (Li +. Na + and K + ) permeable).

1.A.8.8.10.description: Water and urea transporting aquaporin (cockroach) ( Herraiz et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.8.10.name: Water and urea transporting aquaporin (cockroach).

1.A.8.8.11.description: Water channel, Aqp1; inhibited by HgCl 2 and tetraethylammonium. Plays a role in water homeostasis during blood feeding and humidity adaptation of A. gambiae , a major mosquito vector of human malaria in Africa ( Liu et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.8.11.name: Water channel, Aqp1; inhibited by HgCl 2 and tetraethylammonium.

1.A.8.8.12.description: Aquaporin, Aqp1 in the gall fly. Transports water but not glycerol or urea. Promotes freeze-tolerance ( Philip et al. , 2011 ).
1.A.8.8.12.name: Aquaporin, Aqp1 in the gall fly.

1.A.8.8.13.description: The Drosophila melanogaster integral protein, DRIP ( Ishida et al. , 2012 ).
1.A.8.8.13.name: The Drosophila melanogaster integral protein, DRIP.

1.A.8.8.15.description: Mercury-sensitive whitefly aquaporin-1 of the specialized filter chamber of the alimentary tract ( Mathew et al. 2011 ).
1.A.8.8.15.name: Mercury-sensitive whitefly aquaporin-1 of the specialized filter chamber of the alimentary tract.

1.A.8.8.16.description: Aquaporin-1 or Aquaporin1, Aqp1, of 258 aas and 6 TMSs. Three Aqp1 isoforms are differentially regluated by the function of the vasotocin (AVTR) and isotocin (ITR) receptors ( Martos-Sitcha et al. 2015 ). Aqp1aa, one of two isoforms in teleosts, may play a role in spermatogenesis in Cynoglossus semilaevis ( Guo et al. 2017 ).
1.A.8.8.16.name: Aquaporin-1 or Aquaporin1, Aqp1, of 258 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.17.description: Aquaporin-3, Aqp-3 of 271 aas. Transports water, glycerol, hydrogen peroxide and urea ( Geadkaew et al. 2015 ). AQP3 induces the production of chemokines such as CCL24 and CCL22 through regulating the amount of cellular H 2 O 2 in M2 polarized alveolar macrophages, implying a role of AQP3 in asthma ( Ikezoe et al. 2016 ).
1.A.8.8.17.name: Aquaporin-3, Aqp-3 of 271 aas.

1.A.8.8.18.description: Aqp-x2 water channel in the luminal epithelium of urinary bladder cells and lungs. Responsive to Vasotocin (AVT) ( Shibata et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.8.18.name: Aqp-x2 water channel in the luminal epithelium of urinary bladder cells and lungs.

1.A.8.8.19.description: Contractile vacuole aquaporin of 295 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp. Shown to transport water, accounting for the high water permeability of the contractile vacuole ( Nishihara et al. 2008 ).
1.A.8.8.19.name: Contractile vacuole aquaporin of 295 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp.

1.A.8.8.21.description: Aquaporin x5 of 273 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp-x5. The sequence reveals a mercurial-sensitive cysteine and a putative phosphorylation motif site for protein kinase A at Ser-257 ( Kubota et al. 2006 ). A swelling assay using Xenopus oocytes revealed that AQP-x5 facilitated water permeability. Expression of AQP-x5 mRNA was restricted to the skin, brain, lungs and testes. Immunofluorescence and…
1.A.8.8.21.name: Aquaporin x5 of 273 aas and 6 TMSs, Aqp-x5.

1.A.8.8.22.description: Aqp-1A of 258 aas and 6 TMSs, DRIP1. Transports water but not glycerol or urea. Functions in water homeostasis in many tissues and stages of development ( Lu et al. 2018 ). An aquaporin in the beet armyworm, Spodoptera exigua, (79% identical to the one in Chilo suppressalis , mediates cell shape change required for cellular immunity ( Ahmed and Kim 2019 ).
1.A.8.8.22.name: Aqp-1A of 258 aas and 6 TMSs, DRIP1.

1.A.8.8.23.description: Aqp-2A of 269 aas and 6 TMSs, PRIP2. It transports water and urea but not glycerol or trehalose. It functions in water homeostasis in many tissues and stages of development ( Lu et al. 2018 ). Its production in various tissues and stages of growth have been examined ( Lu et al. 2021 ).
1.A.8.8.23.name: Aqp-2A of 269 aas and 6 TMSs, PRIP2.

1.A.8.8.24.description: Big brain-like protein of 309 aas and 6 probable TMSs, BibL1 ( Lind et al. 2017 ).
1.A.8.8.24.name: Big brain-like protein of 309 aas and 6 probable TMSs, BibL1.

1.A.8.8.25.description: Aquaporin 1, AQP1, of 261 aas and 6 TMSs, which selectively transports water ( Lind et al. 2017 ).
1.A.8.8.25.name: Aquaporin 1, AQP1, of 261 aas and 6 TMSs, which selectively transports water.

1.A.8.8.26.description: Aquaporin (Aqp) of 458 aas, 6 N-terminal TMSs and a 200 aa hydrophilic C-terminal domain.
1.A.8.8.26.name: Aquaporin (Aqp) of 458 aas, 6 N-terminal TMSs and a 200 aa hydrophilic C-terminal domain.

1.A.8.8.27.description: Aquaglyceroporin, Glp1, of 269 aas and 6 TMSs. Transports glycerol and water ( Tsujimoto et al. 2017 ).
1.A.8.8.27.name: Aquaglyceroporin, Glp1, of 269 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.28.description: Aquaporin-2, Aqp2, of 275 aas and 6 TMSs.It is subject to hyperosmotic stimulation in Chick Kidney ( Sugiura et al. 2008 ). It is highly similar to the quail ( Coturnix coturnix ) ortholog which has been studied and shown to be a mercury-inhibited, vasotocin-sensitive water channel in the kidney ( Yang et al. 2004 ).
1.A.8.8.28.name: Aquaporin-2, Aqp2, of 275 aas and 6 TMSs.It is subject to hyperosmotic stimulation in Chick Kidney.

1.A.8.8.29.description: Aquaporin/glycerol transporter of 294 aas and 6 TMSs. Tandem duplication (TD) was the major mechanism of gene expansion in echinoderms and hemichordates, which, together with whole genome duplications (WGD) in the chordate lineage, continued to shape the genomic repertoires in craniates. Molecular phylogenies indicated that Aqp3-like and Aqp13-like channels were the probable stem subfamilies in…
1.A.8.8.29.name: Aquaporin/glycerol transporter of 294 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.3.description: The Big Brain, BIB aquaporin of 696 aas and 6 TMSs, transports ions by a channel mechanism involving E71 in TMS1) ( Yool, 2007 ). BIB expressed in Xenopus oocytes is a monovalent cation channel modulated by tyrosine kinase signaling. BIB conductance shows voltage- and dose-dependent block by extracellular divalent cations Ca 2+ and Ba 2+ but not by Mg 2+ in wild-type channels ( Yanochko and Yool…
1.A.8.8.3.name: The Big Brain, BIB aquaporin of 696 aas and 6 TMSs, transports ions by a channel mechanism involving E71 in TMS1).

1.A.8.8.30.description: Aquaporin-A, AqpA of 249 aas and 6 TMSs. Aquaporins may not play major roles in adapting to longterm survival in brackish water or they be regulated by non-transcriptional mechanisms like post-translational modifications ( Misyura et al. 2020 ).
1.A.8.8.30.name: Aquaporin-A, AqpA of 249 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.31.description: Aqp1 of 250 aas and 6 TMSs. Aqp1 localizes on the contractile vacuole complex in Paramecium multimicronucleatum ( Ishida et al. 2021 ).
1.A.8.8.31.name: Aqp1 of 250 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.8.4.description: Aqp6 aquaporin (also transports NO 3 - and other anions at acidic pH or in the presence of Hg 2+ ) ( Ikeda et al ., 2002 ). AQP6 flicker rapidly between closed and open states. Two well conserved glycine residues: Gly-57 in TMS 2 and Gly-173 in TMS 5 reside at the contact point where the two helices cross. Mammalian orthologs of AQP6 have an asparagine residue (Asn-60) at the position…
1.A.8.8.4.name: Aqp6 aquaporin (also transports NO 3 - and other anions at acidic pH or in the presence of Hg 2+ ).

1.A.8.8.5.description: Aquaporin-4 (AQP4) is the major water channel in the central nervous system and plays an important role in the brain's water balance, including edema formation and clearance. There are 6 splice variants; the shorter ones assemble into functional, tetrameric square arrays; the longer is palmitoylated on N-terminal cysteyl residues) ( Suzuki et al. , 2008 ). The longest, Aqp4e, has a novel…
1.A.8.8.5.name: Aquaporin-4 (AQP4) is the major water channel in the central nervous system and plays an important role in the brain's water balance, including edema…

1.A.8.8.6.description: Aqp1 water channel of the sleeping chironomid (functions in water removal during anhydrobiosis, Kikawada et al., 2008 ).
1.A.8.8.6.name: Aqp1 water channel of the sleeping chironomid.

1.A.8.8.7.description: Aqp2 water channel of the sleeping chironomid (functions in water homeostasis during anhydrobiosis ( Kikawada et al. , 2008 ).
1.A.8.8.7.name: Aqp2 water channel of the sleeping chironomid

1.A.8.8.8.description: Vasopressin-sensitive aquaporin-2 (Aqp2) in the apical membrane of the renal collecting duct ( Fenton et al ., 2008 ). Controls cell volume and thereby influences cell proliferation ( Di Giusto et al. 2012 ). It plays a key role in concentrating urine. Water reabsorption is regulated by AQP2 trafficking between intracellular storage vesicles and the apical membrane. This process is tightly…
1.A.8.8.8.name: Vasopressin-sensitive aquaporin-2 (Aqp2) in the apical membrane of the renal collecting duct.

1.A.8.8.9.description: Aquaporin 5 (x-ray structure at 2.0 Å resolution (PDB# 3D9S) is available) ( Horsefield et al. , 2008 ). Aqp5 is a marker for proliferation and migration of human breast cancer cells ( Jung et al. , 2011 ). Plays a role in chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases (COPD) ( Zhao et al. 2014 ). Its expression is regulated by androgens ( Pust et al. 2015 ). As in humans, the chicken ortholog, Aqp5, is…
1.A.8.8.9.name: Aquaporin 5 (x-ray structure at 2.0 Å resolution (PDB# 3D9S) is available).

1.A.8.9.1.description: Aquaporin 3. 95% identical to the human orthologue. Poorly permeable to water, but more permeable to glycerol and arsenic trioxide ( Palmgren et al. 2017 ). It is expressed in the plasma membrane of basal epidermal cells in the skin; loss of function prevents skin tumorigenesis and epidermal cell proliferation ( Hara-Chikuma and Verkman, 2008 ). The human orthologue also transports both water and…
1.A.8.9.1.name: Aquaporin 3.

1.A.8.9.10.description: Aqp9 or Aqp-h9 of 294 aas. Takes up glycerol as well as water, and thereby contributes to freeze tolerance ( Hirota et al. 2015 ). An almost identical orthologue, HC-9 in Dryophytes chrysoscelis (gray treefrog), similarly facilitates glycerol permeability. Both the transcriptional and translational levels of HC-9 change in response to thermal challenges, with a unique increase in liver during…
1.A.8.9.10.name: Aqp9 or Aqp-h9 of 294 aas.

1.A.8.9.11.description: Aqp1 of 304 aas and 6 TMSs; the most abundant transmembrane protein in the tegument of Schistosoma mansoni. This protein is expressed in all developmental stages and seems to be essential in parasite survival since it plays a crucial role in osmoregulation, nutrient transport and drug uptake ( Figueiredo et al. 2014 ).
1.A.8.9.11.name: Aqp1 of 304 aas and 6 TMSs; the most abundant transmembrane protein in the tegument of Schistosoma mansoni.

1.A.8.9.12.description: Basolateral Aqp3 of 292 aas and 6 TMSs in the frog urinary bladder ( Shibata et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.9.12.name: Basolateral Aqp3 of 292 aas and 6 TMSs in the frog urinary bladder.

1.A.8.9.13.description: Aquaglycerolporin, Aqp (high permeability to ammonium, methylamine, glycerol and water) ( Beitz et al ., 2004 ) NH 4 + /NH 3 + CH 3 /glycerol/water transporter ( Zeuthen et al ., 2006 ).
1.A.8.9.13.name: Aquaglycerolporin, Aqp (high permeability to ammonium, methylamine, glycerol and water) NH 4 + /NH 3 + CH 3 /glycerol/water transporter.

1.A.8.9.14.description: Glycerolaquaporin 9, Aqp9 of 295 aas and 6 TMSs. Transports water, glycerol and arsenic trioxide, As 2 O 3 ( Palmgren et al. 2017 ) as well as urea and lactic acid (but not lactate) ( Geistlinger et al. 2022 ). Primary APL cells express AQP9 significantly (2-3 logs) higher than other acute myeloid leukemia cells (AMLs), explaining their exquisite As 2 O 3 sensitivity ( Leung et al. 2007 ). AQP-7…
1.A.8.9.14.name: Glycerolaquaporin 9, Aqp9 of 295 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.15.description: Aquaporin 9, Aqp9, small solute channel 1 of 296 aas and 6 TMSs ( Wang and Ye 2016 ).
1.A.8.9.15.name: Aquaporin 9, Aqp9, small solute channel 1 of 296 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.17.description: Glycerol-aquaporin of 332 aas and 6 TMSs ( Stavang et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.9.17.name: Glycerol-aquaporin of 332 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.18.description: Aquaporin of 341 aas and 7 TMSs ( Ben Amira et al. 2018 ).
1.A.8.9.18.name: Aquaporin of 341 aas and 7 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.19.description: AQP2 (AQP9) of 312 aas and 6 TMSs; transports water, glycerol and urea as well as the drugs, melarsoprol and pentamidine ( Schmidt et al. 2018 ) . CCCP and gramicidin but not nigericin inhibit Trypanosoma brucei Aquaglyceroporins Aqp2 and Aqp3 at neutral pH ( Petersen and Beitz 2020 ). The structures of drug-bound TbAQP2 represent a novel paradigm for drug-transporter interactions and provide a…
1.A.8.9.19.name: AQP2 (AQP9) of 312 aas and 6 TMSs; transports water, glycerol and urea as well as the drugs, melarsoprol and pentamidine.

1.A.8.9.2.description: Aquaporin-9 (Aqp9) (permeable to glycerol, urea, polyols, carbamides, purines, pyrmidines, nucleosides, monocarboxylates, pentavalent methylated arsenicals and the arsenic chemotherapeutic drug, trisenox ( McDermott et al. , 2009 ). It is poorly permeable to water and not permeable to β-hydroxybutyrate ( Carbrey et al ., 2003 ). (Regulated by CFTR and NHERF1 in response to cyclic AMP ( Pietrement…
1.A.8.9.2.name: Aquaporin-9 (Aqp9)

1.A.8.9.20.description: Aquaporin of 274 aas and 6 TMSs. See Zhou et al. 2018 for its identification.
1.A.8.9.20.name: Aquaporin of 274 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.21.description: Aquaporin 3, Aqp3, of 304 aas and 6 TMSs. CCCP and gramicidin but not nigericin inhibit Trypanosoma brucei Aquaglyceroporins Aqp2 and Aqp3 at neutral pH ( Petersen and Beitz 2020 ).
1.A.8.9.21.name: Aquaporin 3, Aqp3, of 304 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.22.description: Aquaporin-3-like protein, Aqp10b, of 374 aas and 6 TMSs ( Santos et al. 2004 ).
1.A.8.9.22.name: Aquaporin-3-like protein, Aqp10b, of 374 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.24.description: Aqp3 of 292 aas and 6 TMSs. It is a water channel required to promote glycerol permeability and water transport across cell membranes ( Roudier et al. 2002 , Gotfryd et al. 2018 ). It acts as a glycerol transporter in skin and plays an important role in regulating the stratum corneum and epidermal glycerol content. It is involved in skin hydration, wound healing, and tumorigenesis, and it…
1.A.8.9.24.name: Aqp3 of 292 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.3.description: Major aquaglyceroporin, LmAQP1: transports water, glycerol, methylglyoxal, trivalent metalloids such as arsenite and antimonite, dihydroxyacetone and sugar alcohols. Also takes up the activated form or the drug, pentostam. It localizes to the flagellum of the Leishmania promastigotes and is used to regulate volume in response to hypoosmotic stress; it functions in osmotaxis ( Figarella et al…
1.A.8.9.3.name: Major aquaglyceroporin, LmAQP1: transports water, glycerol, methylglyoxal, trivalent metalloids such as arsenite and antimonite, dihydroxyacetone and…

1.A.8.9.4.description: Aquaporin 1 (permeable to water, glycerol, dihydroxyacetone and urea) ( Uzcategui et al ., 2004 )
1.A.8.9.4.name: Aquaporin 1 (permeable to water, glycerol, dihydroxyacetone and urea)

1.A.8.9.5.description: Aquaporin 10 of 301 aas and 6 TMSs. Cell- and tissue-specific expression of AQP-0, AQP-3, and AQP-10 in the testis, efferent ducts, and epididymis has been demonstrated ( Hermo et al. 2019 ). It is also present in keratinocytes and the stratum corneum ( Jungersted et al. 2013 ).
1.A.8.9.5.name: Aquaporin 10 of 301 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.8.9.6.description: Glycerol/water/urea/arsenic trioxide-transporting channel protein, aqaporin 7 or Aqp7, but water is a poor substrate ( Palmgren et al. 2017 ). Present in adipose tissue where it allows glycerol efflux. Defects result in increased accumulation of triglycerides, obesity and adult onset (type 2) diabetes ( Lebeck 2014 ). It may be a drug target for anti-type 2 diabetes ( Méndez-Giménez et al. 2018…
1.A.8.9.6.name: Glycerol/water/urea/arsenic trioxide-transporting channel protein, aqaporin 7 or Aqp7, but water is a poor substrate.

1.A.8.9.7.description: Glycerol facilitator, Yf1054c (70.5 kDa protein) ( Oliveira et al ., 2003 )
1.A.8.9.7.name: Glycerol facilitator, Yf1054c (70.5 kDa protein)

1.A.8.9.9.description: Aquaporin/glycerol facilitator of 294 aas and 6 TMSs. May play a role in freeze tolerance ( Hirota et al. 2015 ).
1.A.8.9.9.name: Aquaporin/glycerol facilitator of 294 aas and 6 TMSs.

1.A.87.1.1.description: Plant Ca 2+ channel protein, Mid1 complementary activity 1, MCA1 ( Iida et al. 2013 ). MCA1 and MCA2 each forms a homotetramer and exhibit Ca 2+ -permeable mechanosensitive channel activity. Both are single-pass type I transmembrane proteins with their N-termini located extracellularly and their C-termini located intracellularly. An EF hand-like motif, coiled-coil motif, and Plac8 motif may all…
1.A.87.1.1.name: Plant Ca 2+ channel protein, Mid1 complementary activity 1, MCA1.

1.A.87.1.2.description: Plant Ca 2+ channel protein, Mid1 complementary activity 2, MCA2 ( Iida et al. 2013 ). Catalyzes mechanical stress-induced Ca 2+ influx. It is tetrameric with a small transmembrane domain and a large cytoplasmic domain ( Shigematsu et al. 2014 ). MCA1 and MCA2 both have their N-termini located extracellularly and their C-termini located intracellularly. An EF hand-like motif, coiled-coil motif…
1.A.87.1.2.name: Plant Ca 2+ channel protein, Mid1 complementary activity 2, MCA2.

1.A.87.1.3.description: MCA1 isoform X2 of 377 aas with one N-terminal TMS and possibly 3 or 4 C-terminal TMSs.
1.A.87.1.3.name: MCA1 isoform X2 of 377 aas with one N-terminal TMS and possibly 3 or 4 C-terminal TMSs.

1.A.87.2.1.description: Receptor protein kinase of 567 aas. The first 140 aas are homologous to the N-terminal domains of MCA1 and 2; residues 240 - 430 are homologous to ser/thr protein kinases of 9.A.15.1.1, 9.B.45.1.3 and 9.B.106.3.1.
1.A.87.2.1.name: Receptor protein kinase of 567 aas.

2.A.1.1.147.name: MFS glucose transporter, Mfs1, of 550 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.148.description: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1, of 500 aas and 12 TMSs. EgGLUT1 Is crucial for the viability of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto metacestode and may be a new therapeutic target ( Amahong et al. 2021 ).
2.A.1.1.148.name: Glucose transporter 1, GLUT1, of 500 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.149.description: High affinity hexose transporter, HxtA of 531 aas and 12 TMSs. HxtA is induced in vegetative hyphae upon starvation and in ascogenous hyphae during cleistothecium formation ( Wei et al. 2004 ).
2.A.1.1.149.name: High affinity hexose transporter, HxtA of 531 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.150.description: Hexose transporter-like protein, GCR1, of 541 aas and 12 TMSs. Substrates include glucose, mannose and fructose. It functions in catabolite repression (as does Snf3p in S. cerevisiae (TC# 2.A.1.1.18)) of peroxisome biogenesis and of peroxisomal enzymes ( Stasyk et al. 2004 ).
2.A.1.1.150.name: Hexose transporter-like protein, GCR1, of 541 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.151.description: Facilitated trehalose transporter, Tret1-like, of 485 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Trehalose is the main blood sugar in insects and plays an important role in energy metabolism and stress resistance. Plutella xylostella (L.) is an agricultural pest worldwide. Tret1-like was cloned, knoched out and studied ( Zhou et al. 2022 ). It was found that expression of the gene encoding…
2.A.1.1.151.name: Facilitated trehalose transporter, Tret1-like, of 485 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.1.1.152.description: INT7 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern. There are nine INT homologues in Populus trichocarpa, all presumed to transport inositor, and they are involved in stress responses ( Zhang et al. 2023 ).
2.A.1.1.152.name: INT7 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern.

2.A.1.1.154.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs. Symbiotic cnidarians such as corals and anemones form highly productive and biodiverse coral reef ecosystems in nutrient-poor ocean environments, a phenomenon known as Darwin's paradox ( Cui et al. 2023 ). Using the sea anemone Aiptasia , we show that during symbiosis, the increased availability of glucose…
2.A.1.1.154.name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 8 of 509 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.155.description: Sugar transporter ERD6-like 4 of 496 aas and 12 TMSs. Vacuolar sugar transporter EARLY RESPONSE TO DEHYDRATION 6-LIKE4 affects fructose signaling and plant growth ( Khan et al. 2023 ).
2.A.1.1.155.name: Sugar transporter ERD6-like 4 of 496 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.158.description: Plastid glucose transporter 2, pGlcT2, of 493 aas and 12 TMSs. pGlcT2-GFP localized to the chloroplast envelope and is mainly produced in seedlings and in the rosette centers of mature Arabidopsis plants. Therefore, pGlcT2 acts as a glucose importer that can limit cytosolic glucose availability in developing pGlcT2-overexpressing seedlings ( Valifard et al. 2023 ). Possibly pGlcT2 contributes to…
2.A.1.1.158.name: Plastid glucose transporter 2, pGlcT2, of 493 aas and 12 TMSs. pGlcT2-GFP localized to the chloroplast envelope and is mainly produced in seedlings…

2.A.1.1.159.description: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1a, Glut1 of 488 aas and 12 TMSs. Bisphenol S inhibits Glucose Transporter 1, leading to ATP excitotoxicity in the Zebrafish brain ( Wang et al. 2024 ).
2.A.1.1.159.name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1a, Glut1 of 488 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.16.description: Low-affinity hexose (glucose, fructose, mannose, 2-deoxyglucose) uniporter. The evolution of hexose transporters in kinetoplastid protozoans has been studied ( Pereira and Silber 2012 ).
2.A.1.1.16.name: Low-affinity hexose (glucose, fructose, mannose, 2-deoxyglucose) uniporter.

2.A.1.1.160.description: L-Arabinose high specificity and affinity uptake transporter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. The system has low affinity for D-xylose and almost no affinity for D-glucose. It has use for bioengineering purposes ( Havukainen et al. 2021 ). Due to its high affinity for L-arabinose and low inhibition by D-glucose or D-xylose, Trire2_104072 (AraE) could serve as a good candidate…
2.A.1.1.160.name: L-Arabinose high specificity and affinity uptake transporter of 514 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.1.1.161.description: MstH of 540 aas and 12 TMSs. It is the major high-affinity glucose transporter with pleiotropic roles in carbon utilization regulation and citric acid production in Aspergillus niger ( Bankaitis et al. 2025 ).
2.A.1.1.161.name: MstH of 540 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.162.description: MFS traqnsporter of 527 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.
2.A.1.1.162.name: MFS traqnsporter of 527 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.17.description: Glucose transporter of 884 aas and 12 TMSs with a 100 aa hydrophilic N-terminus and a 340 aas hydrophilic C-terminus.
2.A.1.1.17.name: Glucose transporter of 884 aas and 12 TMSs with a 100 aa hydrophilic N-terminus and a 340 aas hydrophilic C-terminus.

2.A.1.1.18.description: Glucose/mannose/fructose transporter and high affinity sensor, Snf3p, (regulates glucose transport via other systems). Residues involved in ligand preference are similar to those involved in transport ( Dietvorst et al. 2010 ). Snf3p in Candida glabrata is essential for growth in low glucose media but not high glucose media, and plays a role in the induction of severall hexose transporters ( Ng…
2.A.1.1.18.name: Glucose/mannose/fructose transporter and high affinity sensor, Snf3p, (regulates glucose transport via other systems).

2.A.1.1.19.description: Glucose transporter and low affinity sensor, Rgt2p (regulates glucose transport in conjunction with Snf3p). Rgt2 generates an intracellular signal in response to glucose that leads to inhibition of the Rgt1 transcriptional repressor and consequently to derepression of HXT genes encoding glucose transporters. They have unusually long C-terminal tails that bind to Mth1 and Std1, paralogous proteins…
2.A.1.1.19.name: Glucose transporter and low affinity sensor, Rgt2p (regulates glucose transport in conjunction with Snf3p).

2.A.1.1.2.description: Arabinose (xylose; galactose):H + symporter, AraE (low affinity high capacity) ( Khlebnikov et al. 2001 ).
2.A.1.1.2.name: Arabinose (xylose; galactose):H + symporter, AraE (low affinity high capacity).

2.A.1.1.24.description: Hexose (Glucose and Fructose) transporter, PfHT1 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs. This is the only hexose transporter, and it is found in the plasma membrane. It is an antimalarial drug target ( Meier et al. 2018 ; Wunderlich 2022 ).
2.A.1.1.24.name: Hexose (Glucose and Fructose) transporter, PfHT1 of 504 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.25.description: Myoinositol:H + symporter, HMIT (also transport other inositols including scyllo-, muco- and chiro-, but not allo-inositol) ( Aouameur et al ., 2007 ). Expressed in the Golgi of the hippocampus and cortex. May also transport inositoltriphosphate ( Di Daniel et al. , 2009 ). Interacts directly with γ-secretase (9.B.47.1.1) to regulate its activity and the production of Abeta production, important…
2.A.1.1.25.name: Myoinositol:H + symporter, HMIT (also transport other inositols including scyllo-, muco- and chiro-, but not allo-inositol).

2.A.1.1.26.description: Major myoinositol:H + symporter, IolT, of 473 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern ( Yoshida et al. 2002 ).
2.A.1.1.26.name: Major myoinositol:H + symporter, IolT, of 473 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS pattern.

2.A.1.1.27.description: Minor, low affinity myoinositol:H + symporter, IolF, of 438 aas and 12 TMSs ( Yoshida et al. 2002 ).
2.A.1.1.27.name: Minor, low affinity myoinositol:H + symporter, IolF, of 438 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.28.description: The erythrocyte/brain hexose facilitator, glucose transporter-1, Gtr1. SLC2a1 or Glut1. Transports D-glucose, dehydroascorbate, arsenite and the flavonone, quercetin, via one pathway and water via a distinct channel. Sugar transport has been suggested to function via a sliding mechanism involving several sugar binding sites ( Cunningham et al ., 2006 ). Glut1 is the receptor for human T-cell…
2.A.1.1.28.name: The erythrocyte/brain hexose facilitator, glucose transporter-1, Gtr1.

2.A.1.1.29.description: Glucosamine/glucose/fructose uniporter, Glut-2, Glut2 or ATG9A; it may also transport dehydroascorbate ( Mardones et al. , 2011 ; Maulén et al. , 2003 ), and cotransports water against an osmotic gradient ( Naftalin, 2008 ). Mutations may give rise to the rare autosomal recessive Fanconi-Bickel syndrome ( Batool et al. 2019 ). It mediates intestinal transport of quercetrin ( Li et al. 2020 ) and…
2.A.1.1.29.name: Glucosamine/glucose/fructose uniporter, Glut-2, Glut2 or ATG9A; it may also transport dehydroascorbate, and cotransports water against an osmotic…

2.A.1.1.3.description: Xylose (xylopyranose):H + symporter of 491 aas and 12 TMSs ( Wambo et al. 2017 ). Also transports and binds D-glucose and 6-bromo-6-deoxy-D-glucose. The 3-d structure is known in three conformers, outward occluded, inward occluded and inward open ( Sun et al. 2012: Quistgaard et al. 2013 ). Most of the sugar-binding residues are conserved with the human Glut-1, 2, 3 and 4 homologues. The…
2.A.1.1.3.name: Xylose (xylopyranose):H + symporter of 491 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.30.description: Low affinity, constitutive, glucose (hexose; xylose) uniporter, Hxt4 (LGT1; Rag1) (also transports arsenic trioxide [As(OH) 3 ] as do Hxtl, 3, 5, 7 and 9) ( Liu et al ., 2004 ). The Kluyveromyces lactis ortholog is 73% identical and is similarly regulated ( Rolland et al. 2006 ). Key residues for efficient glucose transport by the hexose transporter CgHxt4 in the high sugar fermentation yeast…
2.A.1.1.30.name: Low affinity, constitutive, glucose (hexose; xylose) uniporter, Hxt4 (LGT1; Rag1)

2.A.1.1.31.description: High affinity, glucose-repressible, glucose (hexose) uniporter (Hxt6/Hxt7). Asn331 and hydrophobic residue side chains in TMS5 determine substrate affinity ( Kasahara et al. , 2011; Kasahara and Kasahara 2010 ). Also transports xylose ( Wang et al. 2013 ). The F79S mutation in the hexose transporter HXT7 enhances xylose uptake, and five key aromatic hub residues (81W, 122F, 153Y, 208Y, and 492F)…
2.A.1.1.31.name: High affinity, glucose-repressible, glucose (hexose) uniporter (Hxt6/Hxt7).

2.A.1.1.32.description: Glucose/fructose:H + symporter, GlcP ( Zhang et al ., 1989 )
2.A.1.1.32.name: Glucose/fructose:H + symporter, GlcP

2.A.1.1.33.description: Fructose:H + symporter, Frt1 ( Diezemann and Boles, 2003 )
2.A.1.1.33.name: Fructose:H + symporter, Frt1

2.A.1.1.34.description: The broad specificity sugar/sugar alcohol (myo-inositol, glycerol, ribose, sorbitol, mannitol, xylitol, erythritol, etc) H + symporter, AtPLT5 (transports a wide range of hexoses, pentoses, tetroses, sugar alcohols and a sugar acid, but not disaccharides) ( Reinders et al ., 2005 ) (expressed in roots, leaves and floral organs) ( Klepek et al ., 2004 )
2.A.1.1.34.name: The broad specificity sugar/sugar alcohol (myo-inositol, glycerol, ribose, sorbitol, mannitol, xylitol, erythritol, etc) H + symporter, AtPLT5…

2.A.1.1.35.description: The major glucose (or 2-deoxyglucose) uptake transporter, GlcP (van Wezel et al ., 2005 )
2.A.1.1.35.name: The major glucose (or 2-deoxyglucose) uptake transporter, GlcP

2.A.1.1.36.description: The low affinity, glucose-inducible glucose transporter, MstE ( Forment et al. , 2006 )
2.A.1.1.36.name: The low affinity, glucose-inducible glucose transporter, MstE

2.A.1.1.38.description: The glycerol:H + symporter, Stl1p ( Ferreira et al ., 2005 )
2.A.1.1.38.name: The glycerol:H + symporter, Stl1p

2.A.1.1.39.description: The high affinity glucose transporter, Hgt1 ( Baruffini et al ., 2006 )
2.A.1.1.39.name: The high affinity glucose transporter, Hgt1

2.A.1.1.4.description: Glucose uniporter of 473 aas and 12 TMSs. Several GLUT isoforms, especially GLUT1 and GLUT3 in humans, are overexpressed in many tumors, and inhibitors have been identified ( Kawatani and Osada 2025 ).
2.A.1.1.4.name: Glucose uniporter of 473 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.1.40.description: The xylose facilitator, Xylhp ( Nobre et al ., 1999 )
2.A.1.1.40.name: The xylose facilitator, Xylhp

2.A.1.1.41.description: The D-xylose:H + symporter, XylT (K m =220 μM; inhibited competitively by 6-deoxyglucose (K i =220 μM), but not by other sugars tested) ( Chaillou et al ., 1998 )
2.A.1.1.41.name: The D-xylose:H + symporter, XylT (K m =220 μM; inhibited competitively by 6-deoxyglucose (K i =220 μM), but not by other sugars tested)

2.A.1.1.42.description: The D-glucose:H + symporter, GlcP (glucose uptake is inhibited by 2-deoxyglucose, mannose and galactose) ( Parche et al ., 2006 )
2.A.1.1.42.name: The D-glucose:H + symporter, GlcP (glucose uptake is inhibited by 2-deoxyglucose, mannose and galactose)

2.A.1.1.43.description: The monosaccharide (MST) (glucose > mannose > galactose > fructose):H + symporter, MST1 ( Schussler et al. , 2006 ).
2.A.1.1.43.name: The monosaccharide (MST) (glucose > mannose > galactose > fructose):H + symporter, MST1.

2.A.1.1.44.description: The hexose (glucose and fructose but not galactose) transporter (Glut11; SLC2A11) ( Scheepers et al ., 2005 )
2.A.1.1.44.name: The hexose (glucose and fructose but not galactose) transporter (Glut11; SLC2A11)

2.A.1.1.45.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glucose transporter1, Vgt1 (important for seed germination and flowering) ( Aluri and Büttner, 2007 )
2.A.1.1.45.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glucose transporter1, Vgt1 (important for seed germination and flowering)

2.A.1.1.46.description: The blastocyst/testis glucose transporter, Glut8 ( Doege et al ., 2000 ) (insulin stimulated in blastocysts) ( Carayannopoulos et al. , 2000 ).
2.A.1.1.46.name: The blastocyst/testis glucose transporter, Glut8 (insulin stimulated in blastocysts).

2.A.1.1.47.description: The embryonic liver, kidney, and other tissue uric acid (urate) transporter, Glut9 (SLC2A9) ( Wright et al. 2010 ). Mutations in this transporter cause severe renal hyperuricemia. It transports hexoses as well as urate, the latter by an electrogenic uniport mechanism. It's transcription is regulated by a hepatocyte nuclear factor, HNF4α ( Prestin et al. 2014 ).
2.A.1.1.47.name: The embryonic liver, kidney, and other tissue uric acid (urate) transporter, Glut9 (SLC2A9).

2.A.1.1.48.description: The pentose/hexose transporter (sugar transport protein 2), STP2. (Expressed during pollen maturation and early stages of gametophyte development) ( Truernit et al ., 1999 )
2.A.1.1.48.name: The pentose/hexose transporter (sugar transport protein 2), STP2. (Expressed during pollen maturation and early stages of gametophyte development)

2.A.1.1.49.description: The sink-specific, stress-regulated monosaccharide uptake porter, STP4. (Induced upon wounding or infection with bacteria or fungi; expressed in roots and flowers) ( Truernit et al ., 1996 )
2.A.1.1.49.name: The sink-specific, stress-regulated monosaccharide uptake porter, STP4.

2.A.1.1.50.description: The glucose/fructose:H + symporter, STP13 (sugar transport protein 13). Expressed in vascular tissues and induced during programmed cell death ( Norholm et al ., 2006 ). Used to combat bacterial infection by competing with them for sugars by phosphorylation of STP13 by the BAK1 receptor kinase ( Yamada et al. 2016 ).
2.A.1.1.50.name: The glucose/fructose:H + symporter, STP13 (sugar transport protein 13).

2.A.1.1.51.description: Glucose/xylose: H + symporter, Gsx1 ( Leandro et al ., 2006 )
2.A.1.1.51.name: Glucose/xylose: H + symporter, Gsx1

2.A.1.1.52.description: The glucose transport protein, GTP1 ( Skelly et al ., 1994 )
2.A.1.1.52.name: The glucose transport protein, GTP1

2.A.1.1.53.description: Myo -Inositol uptake porter, IolT1 (Km=0.2mM) ( Krings et al ., 2006 ). Can also transport D-glucose ( Ikeda et al. 2011 ).
2.A.1.1.53.name: Myo -Inositol uptake porter, IolT1 (Km=0.2mM).

2.A.1.1.54.description: Myo -Inositol (Km=0.45mM) uptake porter, IolT2 ( Krings et al ., 2006 ). Can not transport D-glucose ( Ikeda et al. 2011 ).
2.A.1.1.54.name: Myo -Inositol (Km=0.45mM) uptake porter, IolT2.

2.A.1.1.55.description: L-arabinose:proton symporter, AraE ( Sa-Nogueira and Ramos, 1997 ). Also transports xylose, galactose and α-1,5 arabinobiose ( Ferreira and Sá-Nogueira, 2010 ).
2.A.1.1.55.name: L-arabinose:proton symporter, AraE.

2.A.1.1.56.description: High affinity monosaccharide (K M ≈ 20 µM):H + symporter, Stp6 (takes up glucose, 3-O-methylglucose, mannose, fructose, galactose and to a lesser extent, xylose and ribulose. ( Scholz-Starke et al ., 2003 )
2.A.1.1.56.name: High affinity monosaccharide (K M ≈ 20 µM):H + symporter, Stp6

2.A.1.1.57.description: High affinity (15 μM) glucose (monosaccharides including xylose):H + symporter, MstA ( Jørgensen et al. , 2007 ).
2.A.1.1.57.name: High affinity (15 μM) glucose (monosaccharides including xylose):H + symporter, MstA.

2.A.1.1.58.description: Low affinity glucose:H + symporter, MstC ( Jørgensen et al. , 2007 ).
2.A.1.1.58.name: Low affinity glucose:H + symporter, MstC.

2.A.1.1.59.description: The glucose transporter, GLUT10, was originally believed to be responsible for Type 2 diabetes. It is now believed to be responsible for arterial tortuosity, a rare autosomal recessive connective tissue disease (Callewaert et al., 2007). GLUT10 transports glucose and 2-deoxy glucose (K m =0.3 mM), and is inhibited by galactose and phloretin ( Coucke et al ., 2006 ).
2.A.1.1.59.name: The glucose transporter, GLUT10, was originally believed to be responsible for Type 2 diabetes.

2.A.1.1.6.description: Galactose, glucose uniporter, Gal2. Also transports xylose ( Wang et al. 2013 ). This transporter has been engineered by mutation (N376F) to transport xylose without being inhibited by glucose or transporting other hexoses ( Farwick et al. 2014 ). The 3-d structure is known ( Wang et al. 2015 ).
2.A.1.1.6.name: Galactose, glucose uniporter, Gal2.

2.A.1.1.60.description: The major hexose transporter, Htr1 (mediates the active uptake of hexoses by sugar:H + symport. Can transport glucose, 3-O-methylglucose, fructose, xylose, mannose, galactose, fucose, 2-deoxyglucose and arabinose. Confers sensitivity to galactose in seedlings. K m =20 uM for glucose) ( Stadler et al ., 2003 ; Boorer et al ., 1994 )
2.A.1.1.60.name: The major hexose transporter, Htr1

2.A.1.1.61.description: High affinity monosaccharide (K m = 25 µM) transporter (takes up glucose, galactose, mannose, xylose and 3-O-methylglucose, but not fructose and ribose), STP11 (expressed in pollen tubes) ( Schneidereit et al ., 2005 ). This protein is also called Sugar Transport Protein (STP). Expression profiles of homologues in cabbage have been studied ( Zhang et al. 2019 ).
2.A.1.1.61.name: High affinity monosaccharide (K m = 25 µM) transporter

2.A.1.1.62.description: High affinity (0.24mM) plasma membrane myoinositol-specific H + symporter, INT4 ( Schneider et al ., 2006 )
2.A.1.1.62.name: High affinity (0.24mM) plasma membrane myoinositol-specific H + symporter, INT4

2.A.1.1.63.description: Low affinity inositol (myoinsoitol (Km = 1 mM), scylloinositol, d-chiroinositol and mucoinositol):H + symporter (expressed in the anther tapetum, the vasculature, and the leaf mesophyll ( Schneider et al ., 2007 )
2.A.1.1.63.name: Low affinity inositol (myoinsoitol (Km = 1 mM), scylloinositol, d-chiroinositol and mucoinositol):H + symporter

2.A.1.1.64.description: The hexose sensor, Hxs1 (believed to be non-transporting) ( Stasyk et al ., 2008 )
2.A.1.1.64.name: The hexose sensor, Hxs1 (believed to be non-transporting)

2.A.1.1.65.description: Glucose permease GlcP ( Pimentel-Schmitt et al ., 2008 ) (most similar to 2.A.1.1.32)
2.A.1.1.65.name: Glucose permease GlcP (most similar to 2.A.1.1.32)

2.A.1.1.66.description: The tonoplast H + :Inositol symporter 1, Int1 (mediates efflux from the tonoplast to the cytoplasm ( Schneider et al ., 2008 ) (most similar to 2.A.1.1.63 and 2.A.1.1.62).
2.A.1.1.66.name: The tonoplast H + :Inositol symporter 1, Int1

2.A.1.1.67.description: Glucose/xylose facilitator-1, GXF1 (functions by sugar uniport; low affinity ( Leandro et al ., 2008 )
2.A.1.1.67.name: Glucose/xylose facilitator-1, GXF1

2.A.1.1.69.description: Sugar & polyol transporter 1 (SPT1): broad specificity; takes up glucose ( Schilling and Oesterhelt, 2007 ). Loss of the first 3 TMSs of the 12 TMSs does not prevent sugar uptake or sugar recognition but lowers substrate affinity & transport rate, and abolished H + symport ( Schilling and Oesterhelt, 2007 ).
2.A.1.1.69.name: Sugar & polyol transporter 1 (SPT1): broad specificity; takes up glucose.

2.A.1.1.71.description: Hexose (glucose) transporter, GT4 (D2) (almost identical to 2.A.1.1.16). The L. infantum ortholog (A4I8N6) is 95% identical to this protein and is the dominant protein in the plasma membrane of this organims ( Oliveira et al. 2020 ).
2.A.1.1.71.name: Hexose (glucose) transporter, GT4 (D2) (almost identical to 2.A.1.1.16).

2.A.1.1.72.description: The kidney basolateral urate efflux transporter (SLC2A9, URATv1 or GLUT9) (orthologue of 2.A.1.1.47) ( Anzai et al. , 2008 ). Human SLC2A9a and SLC2A9b isoforms mediate electrogenic transport of urate with different characteristics in the presence of hexoses ( Witkowska et al. , 2012 ). It transports hexoses, glucose and fructose, but not galactose, at a rate 50-fold slower than urate the latter…
2.A.1.1.72.name: The kidney basolateral urate efflux transporter (SLC2A9, URATv1 or GLUT9) (orthologue of 2.A.1.1.47).

2.A.1.1.73.description: Glycerol uptake permease (Glycerol:H + symporter) Stl1. (Involved in salt stress relief) ( Kayingo et al. 2009 ) (similar to Stl1 of S. cerevisiae (2.A.1.1.38))
2.A.1.1.73.name: Glycerol uptake permease (Glycerol:H + symporter) Stl1. (Involved in salt stress relief) (similar to Stl1 of S. cerevisiae (2.A.1.1.38))

2.A.1.1.75.description: The fructose/xylose:H + symporter, PMT1 (polyol monosaccharide transporter-1). Also transports other substrates at lower rates. PMT2 is largely of the same sequence and function. Both are present in pollen and young xylem cells ( Klepek et al. , 2005 ). A similar ortholog has been identifed in pollen grains of Petunia hybrida ( Garrido et al. 2006 ).
2.A.1.1.75.name: The fructose/xylose:H + symporter, PMT1 (polyol monosaccharide transporter-1).

2.A.1.1.76.description: Glucose transporter, GT1. GT1, 2, and 3 are homologues. GT2 and GT3 transport ribose as well as glucose at different rates. GT3 transports ribose with 6-fold lower efficiency due to two threonines in GT3 that are alanines in GT2. They are in two loops between TMSs 3, 4, and 7, 8 ( Naula et al. , 2010 ). GT1 is expressed in the flagellar membrane and may be both a glucose transporter and sensor…
2.A.1.1.76.name: Glucose transporter, GT1.

2.A.1.1.77.description: The D-glucose/D-ribose transporter, LmGT2 (Most similar to 1.A.1.1.18) ( Naula et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.1.1.77.name: The D-glucose/D-ribose transporter, LmGT2 (Most similar to 1.A.1.1.18).

2.A.1.1.78.description: The glucose transporter, LmGT3 (homologous to LmGT2 (1.A.1.1.75)). Two threonine residues located in the hydrophilic loops connecting TMSs 3 & 4 and 7 & 8 of GT3 prevent transport of D-ribose. Changing these two residues to alanine (as in GT2) allows transport of ribose. Thus, loops 3-4 and 7-8 partially determine substrate specificity ( Naula et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.1.1.78.name: The glucose transporter, LmGT3 (homologous to LmGT2 (1.A.1.1.75)).

2.A.1.1.79.description: Polyol (xylitol):H + symporter, PLT4 ( Kalliampakou et al. , 2011 )
2.A.1.1.79.name: Polyol (xylitol):H + symporter, PLT4

Loss in mice produces circadian-dependent hyperdopaminergia and amiliorates motor disfunction and dopa-mediated dyskinesias in a model of Parkinson's Disease ( Divito et al. 2015 ). 2.A.1.14.6.name: Na:P i symporter, NPT1 or SLC17A1.

It may be involved in the export of griseoluteic acid, an intermediate in the biosynthesis of the broad-spectrum…

Ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin are substrates, to which M. tuberculosis strains have become resistant. The expulsion of the…

2.A.1.3.61.description: MDR efflux pump, MdeA. Exports quaternary ammonium compounds and antibiotics ( Huang et al. 2004 ). Also exports hoechst 33342, doxorubicin, daunorubicin, tetraphenyl phosphonium, ethidium bromide and rhodamine 6G ( Yamada et al. 2006 ). 2.A.1.3.64.description: Uptake permease for cholate (steroid) metabolites, CamM of 513 aas and 14 TMSs. Uptake of 3,7(R),12(S)-trihydroxy-9-oxo-9,10-seco-23,24-bisnorchola-1,3,5(10)-trien-22-oate was observed ( Swain et al. 2012 ).
2.A.1.3.64.name: Uptake permease for cholate (steroid) metabolites, CamM of 513 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.1.3.65.description: ThMFS1 of 563 aas and 14 TMSs. Catalyzes export of fungicides causing tolerance. It exports trichodermin, but it is not the only exporter of this secondary metabolite ( Liu et al. 2012 ). 2.A.1.3.68.description: The PfMFS transporter (551 aas; 14 putative TMSs) is involved in the acid resistance and intracellular pH homeostasis of Penicillium funiculosum ( Xu et al. 2014 ). This protein (AIJ02309) was not in UniProt when enterred into TCDB, and its closest orthologue, PmMFS of Penicillium marneffei, is therefore presented here. These two proteins are 82% identical.
2.A.1.3.68.name: The PfMFS transporter (551 aas; 14 putative TMSs) is involved in the acid resistance and intracellular pH homeostasis of Penicillium funiculosum.

2.A.1.3.71.description: Putative multidrug-resistance exporter of 553 aas and 14 putative TMSs, KNQ1. A zebrafish (Danio rerio; ZF) model has been used to explore the…

It may function as a phospholipid flippase, and five flippases (FgDnfA, B, C1, C2 and D have been identified ( Yun et al. 2020 ). 2.A.1.3.85.description: Acinetobacter baumannii ATCC17978 MDR pump (A1S_0188) of the DHA2 family in the MFS ( Hassan et al. 2011 ). It is of 463 aas with 14 TMSs. There are 6 DHA2 members in A. baumannii . One of these, called AadT, exports a variety of drugs ( Naidu et al. 2023 ).
