This protein (GB# OUT43428) is encoded by a gene that is one gene down from two genes encoding proteins of the MFP family (8.A.1, OUT43436 and OUT43425), clearlly indicating that this system is a solute efflux system, possibly of the ABC superfamily.
2.A.135.1.3.name: Uncharacterized protein of 570 aas and 14 TMSs in a 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 TMS arrangement (GB# OUT43428).

2.A.135.1.5.description: DUF1538 domain protein of 255 aas and 7 TMSs. This protein brings up 2.A.63.1.3 (residues 10 - 251 (TMSs 1 - 7) aligning with residues 157 - 391 aas (TMSs 4 - 9) in 2.A.63.1.3 which has 14 TMSs. It is possible that these two families are part of a superfamily, but this possibility has not yet been tested rigorously. However, if homologous, this suggests that there was a rearrangement between the…
2.A.135.1.5.name: DUF1538 domain protein of 255 aas and 7 TMSs.

2.A.14.1.1.description: Lactate permease, LctP or LidP (substrates: L-lactate, D-lactate and glycolate) ( Núñez et al. 2002 ).
2.A.14.1.1.name: Lactate permease, LctP or LidP (substrates: L-lactate, D-lactate and glycolate).

2.A.14.1.2.description: Glycolate permease, GlcA or YghK (substrates: L-lactate, D-lactate and glycolate). Encoded in an operon with malate synthase and glycolate oxidase ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).
2.A.14.1.2.name: Glycolate permease, GlcA or YghK (substrates: L-lactate, D-lactate and glycolate).

2.A.14.2.2.description: Lactate porter, LldP, of 569 aas and 15 or 16 TMSs in a 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 or 4 TMS arrangement ( Dörries et al. 2016 ).
2.A.14.2.2.name: Lactate porter, LldP, of 569 aas and 15 or 16 TMSs in a 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 or 4 TMS arrangement.

2.A.15.1.1.description: Glycine betaine:Na + symporter (also transports dimethylsulfonioacetate and dimethylsulfoniopropionate)
2.A.15.1.1.name: Glycine betaine:Na + symporter (also transports dimethylsulfonioacetate and dimethylsulfoniopropionate)

2.A.15.1.10.description: Glycine betaine transporter, BetP. BetP is a transporter with three different functions: betaine transport, osmosensing, and osmoregulation ( Krämer and Morbach 2004 ). The x-ray structure is known (3PO3; 2WIT; Ressl et al. , 2009 ). Regulatory crosstalk in the trimeric BetP has been reported ( Gärtner et al. , 2011 ). An extracellular K + -dependent interaction site modulates betaine-binding (…
2.A.15.1.10.name: Glycine betaine transporter, BetP.

2.A.15.1.11.description: Glycine betaine transporter BetL (Glycine betaine-Na(+) symporter)
2.A.15.1.11.name: Glycine betaine transporter BetL (Glycine betaine-Na(+) symporter)

2.A.15.1.12.description: The glycine betaine transporter, BetH, of 505 aas and 12 TMSs ( Lu et al. 2005 ).
2.A.15.1.12.name: The glycine betaine transporter, BetH, of 505 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.15.1.13.description: Glycine betaine transporter, OpuD, of 520 aas and 12 TMSs. It may also transport proline, but with low affinity ( Wetzel et al. 2011 ). It is a dominant proline uptake porter, the other being ProT ( Lehman et al. 2023 ).
2.A.15.1.13.name: Glycine betaine transporter, OpuD, of 520 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.15.1.14.description: Trimethylamine uptake transporter of 529 aas and 12 TMSs. Many microbes can utilize TMA as a carbon, nitrogen, and energy source ( Gao et al. 2025 ). TmaT is an Na + /TMA symporter, which possessed high specificity and binding affinity toward TMA. Furthermore, the structures of TmaT and two TmaT-TMA complexes were solved by cryo-EM. TmaT forms a homotrimer structure in solution. Each TmaT monomer…
2.A.15.1.14.name: Trimethylamine uptake transporter of 529 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.15.1.3.description: Low affinity (0.9 mM), high efficiency, choline/glycine betaine:H + symporter, BetT (Chen and Beattie, 2007). The choline-glycine betaine pathway plays an important role in bacterial survival in hyperosmotic environments. Osmotic activation of BetT promotes the uptake of external choline for synthesizing the osmoprotective glycine betaine. The cryo-EM structures of Pseudomonas syringae BetT in…
2.A.15.1.3.name: Low affinity (0.9 mM), high efficiency, choline/glycine betaine:H + symporter, BetT.

2.A.15.1.4.description: The high-affinity, proton- or sodium-driven, secondary symporter, BetT. The cytoplasmic C-terminal domain of plays a role in the regulation of BetT activity; C-terminal truncations cause BetT to be permanently locked in a low-transport-activity mode. ( Tøndervik and Strøm 2007 ).
2.A.15.1.4.name: The high-affinity, proton- or sodium-driven, secondary symporter, BetT.

2.A.15.1.5.description: Glycine-betaine/proline-betaine:Na + symporter, BetS; BetT, OpuD ( Kappes et al. 1996 ; Boscari et al. 2002 ; Ziegler et al. 2010 ).
2.A.15.1.5.name: Glycine-betaine/proline-betaine:Na + symporter, BetS; BetT, OpuD.

2.A.15.1.6.description: The glycine betaine, dimethylsulfoniopropionate:Na + symporter ( Ziegler et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.15.1.6.name: The glycine betaine, dimethylsulfoniopropionate:Na + symporter.

2.A.15.1.7.description: The ectoine/glycine:Na + symporter, LcoP ( Ziegler et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.15.1.7.name: The ectoine/glycine:Na + symporter, LcoP.

2.A.15.1.8.description: The ectoine/hydroxyectoine:Na + symporter, EctT ( Ziegler et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.15.1.8.name: The ectoine/hydroxyectoine:Na + symporter, EctT.

2.A.15.1.9.description: High affinity glycine betaine uptake system
2.A.15.1.9.name: High affinity glycine betaine uptake system

2.A.15.2.1.description: Carnitine:γ-butyrobetaine antiporter. The x-ray structure is known at 3.5 Å resolution ( Schulze et al. , 2010 ). The structure reveals a homotrimer where each protomer has 12 TMSs with 4 L-carnitine molecules outlining the pathway. There is a central binding site and another in the intracellular vestibule ( Tang et al. 2010 ).
2.A.15.2.1.name: Carnitine:γ-butyrobetaine antiporter.

2.A.15.2.2.description: The L-carnitine:γ-butyrobetaine antiporter, CaiT. The x-ray structure is known at 2.3 Å resolution ( Schulze et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.15.2.2.name: The L-carnitine:γ-butyrobetaine antiporter, CaiT.

2.A.16.1.1.description: Tellurite resistance protein, TehA. Encoded in an operon with the gene for a tellurite S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methyl transferase. Together they confer tellurite resistance ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ). High level cell-free expression and specific labeling of TehA from E. coli has been achieved ( Klammt et al. 2004 ).
2.A.16.1.1.name: Tellurite resistance protein, TehA.

2.A.16.1.2.description: Tellurite resistance protein TehA homologue of 328 aas and 10 TMSs. An anion channel involved in tellurite resistance. A quasi-symmetrical homotrimer in which each subunit has 10 TMSs and forms a channel. The crystal structure is known at 1.2 A resolution ( Chen et al. 2010 ). The helices are arranged from helical hairpin pairs to form a central 5-helix transmembrane pore that is gated by a…
2.A.16.1.2.name: Tellurite resistance protein TehA homologue of 328 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.16.2.1.description: Mae1 malate:proton symport protein. May also transport other dicarboxylates such as oxaloacetate, malonate, succinate and fumarate ( Camarasa et al. 2001 ). May also transport thio-malate ( Osawa and Matsumoto 2006 ).
2.A.16.2.1.name: Mae1 malate:proton symport protein.

2.A.16.2.2.description: The ATP-dependent subtelomeric helicase, RecQ (2100 aas with a 5 TMS N-terminal domain (residues 43-210). 94% identical to 2.A.16.2.1 (malate transporter) of the same species.
2.A.16.2.2.name: The ATP-dependent subtelomeric helicase, RecQ

2.A.16.2.3.description: C4-dicarboxylate transporter/malic acid transport protein, Mae1 of 395 aas and 10 TMSs. It has been overexpressed for the production of L-malate ( Liu et al. 2017 ).
2.A.16.2.3.name: C4-dicarboxylate transporter/malic acid transport protein, Mae1 of 395 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.16.3.1.description: The sulfite efflux (sulfite sensitivity) protein, SSU1. Expression is controlled by the FZF1-4 transcriptional activator; only free sulfite (not complexed sulfite) is exported ( Park and Bakalinsky, 2000 ). Can also export nitrite and nitrate ( Cabrera et al. 2014 ). SSU1 has a putative 10 TMS topology in a (S-L) 5 arrangement where S= a small putative TMS and L= a large TMS.
2.A.16.3.1.name: The sulfite efflux (sulfite sensitivity) protein, SSU1.

2.A.16.3.2.description: Sulfite, nitrate exporter of 384 aas, Ssu1 ( Cabrera et al. 2014 ).
2.A.16.3.2.name: Sulfite, nitrate exporter of 384 aas, Ssu1.

2.A.16.3.3.description: Sulfite/nitrate exporter of 392 aas, Ssu2 ( Cabrera et al. 2014 ).
2.A.16.3.3.name: Sulfite/nitrate exporter of 392 aas, Ssu2.

2.A.16.4.2.description: Sulfite efflux pump, Ssul (Sulfite sensitivity protein) ( Lechenne et al ., 2007 ).
2.A.16.4.2.name: Sulfite efflux pump, Ssul (Sulfite sensitivity protein).

2.A.16.4.3.description: Sulfite efflux pump, Ssul ( Lechenne et al ., 2007 ).
2.A.16.4.3.name: Sulfite efflux pump, Ssul.

2.A.16.5.1.description: The plant guard cell S (Slow)-type anion channel, SLAC1 (based on activation kinetics of anion channel currents in response to voltage changes); functions in stomatal signalling, controls turgor pressure, and regulates the exchange of water and CO 2 ( Chen et al. 2010 ). Also called carbon dioxide insensitive (CDI3) and ozone sensitive (OZS1) ( Kollist et al. , 2011 ). Heterotrimeric G proteins…
2.A.16.5.1.name: The plant guard cell S (Slow)-type anion channel, SLAC1 (based on activation kinetics of anion channel currents in response to voltage changes)…

2.A.16.5.2.description: Slow anion channel homologue-3, SLAH3; nitrate is both a substrate and a gate opener ( Geiger et al. 2011 ). Slow, weak voltage-dependent S-type anion efflux channel involved in maintenance of anion homeostasis ( Negi et al. 2008 ). Binds to the highly selective inward-rectifying potassium channel KAT1 and inhibits its activity. Functions as an essential negative regulator of inward potassium…
2.A.16.5.2.name: Slow anion channel homologue-3, SLAH3; nitrate is both a substrate and a gate opener.

2.A.16.6.1.description: TDT homologue, TehA of 302aas and 10 TMSs
2.A.16.6.1.name: TDT homologue, TehA of 302aas and 10 TMSs

2.A.16.6.3.description: Uncharacterized protein of 332 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.16.6.3.name: Uncharacterized protein of 332 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.17.1.1.description: Di- or tripeptide:H + symporter of 497 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs. DtpT is specific for di- and tripeptides, with the highest affinities for peptides with at least one hydrophobic residue. The effect of the hydrophobicity, size, or charge of the amino acid was different for the amino- and carboxyl-terminal positions of dipeptides. Free amino acids, omega-amino fatty acidss, and peptides with more than…
2.A.17.1.1.name: Di- or tripeptide:H + symporter of 497 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs.

2.A.17.1.2.description: The di/tripeptide:H + symport permease, TppB (DtpA or YdgR) (transports di and tripeptides and peptidomimetics such as aminocephalosporins ( Weitz et al ., 2007 ). The transporter has two alternate conformations, one of which is promoted by inhbitor binding ( Bippes et al. 2013 ). Five major conformational states of DtpA are adopted during the transport cycle. These include key metastable states…
2.A.17.1.2.name: The di/tripeptide:H + symport permease, TppB (DtpA or YdgR)

2.A.17.1.3.description: The dipeptide/tripeptide:H + symport permease, DtpB (YhiP) (transports glycyl-sarcosine (Gly-Sar) with low affinity (6mM) and the toxic dipeptide, alafosfalin ( Harder et al ., 2008 )
2.A.17.1.3.name: The dipeptide/tripeptide:H + symport permease, DtpB (YhiP)

2.A.17.1.4.description: DtpD (YbgH) peptide transporter. A projection structure at 19 Å resolution and a high resolution x-ray structure are available; Casagrande et al. , 2009 ; Zhao et al. 2014 ). Glu21 is the only conserved proton-titratable amino acyl residue (among POTs) that is located in the central cavity, and it is critical for in vivo transport ( Zhao et al. 2014 ).
2.A.17.1.4.name: DtpD (YbgH) peptide transporter.

2.A.17.1.5.description: Peptide transporter, YjdL (preference for di-peptides) ( Ernst et al. , 2009 ; Gabrielsen et al. , 2011 ; Jensen et al. , 2011 ). The motif, ExxERFxxYY has been shown to be involved in proton translocation, and the nearby K 117 may play a dual role in protonation and substrate binding ( Jensen et al. 2014 ).
2.A.17.1.5.name: Peptide transporter, YjdL (preference for di-peptides).

2.A.17.1.6.description: POT famiy di- and tri-peptide porter, DtpT. 3-d structures (PDB:24APS; 5MMT: 5D58' 5D59) are available for an inward open conformation. A hinge-like movement in the C-terminal half facilitates opening of an intracellular gate controlling access to a central peptide binding site. Salt bridges may orchestrate alternating access ( Solcan et al. , 2012 ; Quistgaard et al. 2017 ).
2.A.17.1.6.name: POT famiy di- and tri-peptide porter, DtpT.

2.A.17.1.7.description: Peptide uptake transporter of 496 aas, POT. The 3-d structure has been determined to 1.9Å resolution leading to a proposed mechanism ( Doki et al. 2013 ). Glu310 first may bind the carboxyl group of the peptide substrate. Then deprotonation of Glu310 in the inward open state triggers the release of the bound peptide toward the intracellular space, and salt bridge formation between Glu310 and…
2.A.17.1.7.name: Peptide uptake transporter of 496 aas, POT.

2.A.17.1.8.description: Proton-coupled oligopeptide uptake transporter of 485 aas and 14 TMSs, DtpT or Pot. Expression of the encoded gene is upregulated upon infection. Transports di- and tripeptides but can not accumulate peptides with a positively charged residue in the C-terminal position. An aromatic residue patch in the active site of the transporter may be responsible for it's unusual specificity ( Sharma et al…
2.A.17.1.8.name: Proton-coupled oligopeptide uptake transporter of 485 aas and 14 TMSs, DtpT or Pot.

2.A.17.1.9.description: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs. DtpT plays an important role in biofilm formation and stress resistance in foodborne Staphylococcus aureus RMSA49 ( Wu et al. 2025 ).
2.A.17.1.9.name: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs.

2.A.17.2.2.description: Peptide:H + symporter (dipeptides and tripeptides preferred ( Cai et al ., 2007 ). Substrate preference is altered by mutations in the fifth TMS of Ptr2p ( Hauser et al. 2013 ).
2.A.17.2.2.name: Peptide:H + symporter

2.A.17.2.3.description: Dipeptide uptake porter, Ptr2. Transports dipeptides such as Ala-Leu, Ala-Tyr and Tyr-Ala ( Belmondo et al. 2014 ).
2.A.17.2.3.name: Dipeptide uptake porter, Ptr2.

2.A.17.2.4.description: Di- and tripeptide uptake transporter, Ptr2 of 577 aas and 12 TMSs. The ptr2 gene showed increased expression upon interaction with the plant-pathogenic fungus Botrytis cinerea , suggesting that it is involved in the mycoparasitic process. Its expression was triggered by nitrogen starvation ( Vizcaíno et al. 2006 ).
2.A.17.2.4.name: Di- and tripeptide uptake transporter, Ptr2 of 577 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.2.5.description: Oligopeptide transporter of 576 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR22. Transports a variety of peptides as well as derivatives of antifungal agents, such as chlorotetaine and lysyl-cholortetaine ( Liu et al. 2018 ).
2.A.17.2.5.name: Oligopeptide transporter of 576 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR22.

2.A.17.3.1.description: Dual affinity Nitrate/Chlorate symporter, Nrt1.1; CHL1 of 590 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement ( Martin et al ., 2008 ). The low affinity form is a homo-dimer and has Thr101 in the non-phosphorylated form; the high affinty form (0.1 micromolar K m ) is a monomer and has Thr101 phosphorylated ( Sun and Zheng 2015 ). Rehmannia glutinosa (Chinese foxglove) has 18 ntr1 genes encoding…
2.A.17.3.1.name: Dual affinity Nitrate/Chlorate symporter, Nrt1.1; CHL1 of 590 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.17.3.10.description: solute carrier family 15, member 5. Function unknown as of 1/17, but probably a di- and tri-peptide uptake porter ( Verri et al. 2016 ). The tissue expression profile has been reported ( Sreedharan et al. 2011 ). SLC15A5 and RERG are linked with fat yield in cow's milk ( Silva et al. 2026 ).
2.A.17.3.10.name: solute carrier family 15, member 5.

2.A.17.3.11.description: Solute carrier family 15 member 4 (Peptide transporter 4) (Peptide/histidine transporter 1) (hPHT1; SLC15A4; ) is present in immune cells ( Verri et al. 2016 ). It is a proton-coupled amino-acid transporter that mediates the transmembrane transport of L-histidine and some di- and tripeptides from inside the lysosome to the cytosol, and plays a key role in innate immune responses ( Bhardwaj et al…
2.A.17.3.11.name: Solute carrier family 15 member 4 (Peptide transporter 4) (Peptide/histidine transporter 1) (hPHT1; SLC15A4; ) is present in immune cells.

2.A.17.3.16.description: Nitrate transporter 1.2 (Nitrate transporter NTL1; NRT1:2; PRT family protein 4.6; NPF4.6; AIT1). Low-affinity proton-dependent nitrate transporter involved in constitutive nitrate uptake but not histidine or dipeptides transport. Involved in (+)-abscisic acid (ABA) transport, but not in gibberellin, indole-3-acetic acid or jasmonic acid import; ABA and nitrate do not compete for substrate uptake…
2.A.17.3.16.name: Nitrate transporter 1.2 (Nitrate transporter NTL1; NRT1:2; PRT family protein 4.6; NPF4.6; AIT1).

2.A.17.3.17.description: Transporter for glucosinolates (GLS), GTR1, ( aliphatic but not indole glucosinolates such as 4-methylthiobutyl glucosinolate , major defence compounds, translocated to seeds on maturation) as well as gibberellic acid and jasmonoyl-L-isoleucine, GTR1 or NPF2.10, of 636 aas and 12 TMSs ( Nour-Eldin et al. 2012 ; Ishimaru et al. 2017 ). Regulated at the transcriptional level, but also…
2.A.17.3.17.name: Transporter for glucosinolates (GLS), GTR1

2.A.17.3.2.description: Histidine or peptide:H + symporter of 585 aas and 12 TMSs. It mediates the transport of di- and tripeptides with high affinity, low capacity ( Rentsch et al. 1995 ).
2.A.17.3.2.name: Histidine or peptide:H + symporter of 585 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.3.20.description: High-affinity, proton-dependent glucosinolate-specific transporter-2, GTP2 or NPF2.11. Involved in apoplasmic phloem-loading of glucosinolates and in bidirectional long-distance transport of aliphatic but not indole glucosinolates. May be involved in removal of glucosinolates from the xylem in roots ( Nour-Eldin et al. 2012 ; Andersen et al. 2013 ).
2.A.17.3.20.name: High-affinity, proton-dependent glucosinolate-specific transporter-2, GTP2 or NPF2.11.

2.A.17.3.21.description: Low affinity nitrate transporter, Nrt1, of 584 aas and 13 putative TMSs. Two splice variants, Ntr1.1a and Ntr1.1b, have been identified. Under low nitrogen condition, Nrt1.1b accumulates more nitrogen in plants and improves rice growth, but Ntr1.1a had no such effect ( Fan et al. 2015 ). The absorption and long-distance distribution/transport of nitrate is mediated by NRT1.1B in tabacco ( Wu et…
2.A.17.3.21.name: Low affinity nitrate transporter, Nrt1, of 584 aas and 13 putative TMSs.

2.A.17.3.22.description: Uncharacterized peptide transport protein of 609 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR3-A.
2.A.17.3.22.name: Uncharacterized peptide transport protein of 609 aas and 12 TMSs, PTR3-A.

2.A.17.3.23.description: Protein NRT1, PTR FAMILY 5.1, NPF5.1 of 583 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Mutants defective in NPF5.1 had a higher leaf surface temperature compared to the wild type and, NPF5.1 mediated cellular abscisic acid (ABA) uptake when expressed in a heterologous yeast system ( Shimizu et al. 2021 ). An NRT protein (NPF) from wheat ( Triticum aestivum ) has been identified and partiallly…
2.A.17.3.23.name: Protein NRT1, PTR FAMILY 5.1, NPF5.1 of 583 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.17.3.24.description: NRT1.13; NPF4.4; PTR family 4.4 of 601 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs in a 6 or 7 + 6 TMS arrangement. In contrast to most NRT1 transporters, NRT1.13 does not have the conserved proline residue between TMSs 10 and 11, an essential residue for nitrate transport activity in CHL1/NRT1.1/NPF6.3 ( TC# 2.A.17.3.1). NRT1.13 showed no nitrate transport activity, but when Ser487 at the corresponding position was…
2.A.17.3.24.name: NRT1.13; NPF4.4; PTR family 4.4 of 601 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs in a 6 or 7 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.17.3.25.description: Protein NRT1/ PTR FAMILY 5.8, NPF5.8 or NAEZT1, of 552 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. NAET1 and NAET2, function as nicotianamide (nicotinamide NA) transporters required for translocation of both iron and copper to seeds. Chao et al. 2021 showed that NAET1 and NAET2 are predominantly expressed in the shoot and root vascular tissues and mediate secretion of NA out of the cells, resembling the release of…
2.A.17.3.25.name: Protein NRT1/ PTR FAMILY 5.8, NPF5.8 or NAEZT1, of 552 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.3.26.description: Nicotinamine efflux porter of 563 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. NAET1 and NAET2 function as a nicotianamide (nicotinamide NA) transporters required for translocation of both iron and copper to seeds. Chao et al. 2021 showed that NAET1 and NAET2 are predominantly expressed in the shoot and root vascular tissues and mediate secretion of NA out of cells, resembling the release of neurotransmitters from…
2.A.17.3.26.name: Nicotinamine efflux porter of 563 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.3.27.description: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glycerate transporter AtNPF8.4 or Npf8.4, of 545 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. It facilitates shuttling of glycerate between peroxysomes and chloroplasts ( Lin and Tsay 2023 ). It is a tonoplast glycerate uptake system that plays a role of photorespiration in C/N balance ( Lin and Tsay 2023 ).
2.A.17.3.27.name: Vacuolar (tonoplast) glycerate transporter AtNPF8.4 or Npf8.4, of 545 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.3.3.description: Nitrate (chlorate) or histidine:H + symporter of 589 aas and 12 TMSs, Ntr1. Its structural gene is specifically expressed in the floral nectaries of Brassica species ( Song et al. 2000 ).
2.A.17.3.3.name: Nitrate (chlorate) or histidine:H + symporter of 589 aas and 12 TMSs, Ntr1.

2.A.17.3.30.description: Brassica rapa selenium (selenicate) transporter NPF2.20 (BrNPF2.20) accounts for Se-enrichment in Chinese cabbage ( Hu et al. 2024 ). Note: The UniProt acc # used is for this protein is for a different Brassica species, but the amino acid sequences of these two orthologs are identical.
2.A.17.3.30.name: Brassica rapa selenium (selenicate) transporter NPF2.20 (BrNPF2.20) accounts for Se-enrichment in Chinese cabbage.

2.A.17.3.31.description: NPF transporter of 597 aas and 12 TMSs. It is involved in the uptake of 10-deacetylbaccatin III and facilitates the biosynthesis of taxane compounds ( Kusano et al. 2025 ).
2.A.17.3.31.name: NPF transporter of 597 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.17.3.4.description: Peptide transporter, PTR3-A (induced by histidine, leucine and phenylalanine in cotyledons and lower leaves; involved in stress tolerance in seeds during germination and in defense against virulent bacterial pathogens) ( Karim et al ., 2007 ; Karim et al ., 2005 )
2.A.17.3.4.name: Peptide transporter, PTR3-A

2.A.17.3.5.description: The nitrate excretion transporter1, NaxT1, og 558 aas and 13 TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement (in the plasma membranes of plant cells).
2.A.17.3.5.name: The nitrate excretion transporter1, NaxT1, og 558 aas and 13 TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement (in the plasma membranes of plant cells).

2.A.17.3.6.description: Chloroplast nitrite uptake system, Nitr1-L ( Sugiura et al ., 2007 )
2.A.17.3.6.name: Chloroplast nitrite uptake system, Nitr1-L

2.A.17.3.7.description: The root dipeptide/tripeptide transporter, PTRI ( Komarova et al., 2008 ). Transport is electrogenic and dependent on protons. Leak currents are inhibited by Phe-Ala when this peptide binds at the active site with high affinity ( Hammes et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.17.3.7.name: The root dipeptide/tripeptide transporter, PTRI.

2.A.17.3.8.description: The germinating pollen dipeptide/tripeptide transporter, PTR5 ( Komarova et al. , 2008 ). Transport is electrogenic and dependent on protons. Leak currents are inhibited by Phe-Ala when this peptide binds at the active site with high affinity ( Hammes et al. , 2010 ).
2.A.17.3.8.name: The germinating pollen dipeptide/tripeptide transporter, PTR5.

2.A.3.1.19.name: Transporter of lysine, histidine and arginine, HisP or LysQ, of 477 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.2.description: Lysine:H + symporter. Forms a stable complex with CadC to allow lysine-dependent adaptation to acidic stress ( Rauschmeier et al. 2013 ). The Salmonella orthologue is 95% identical to the E. coli protein and is highly specific for Lysine. Residues involved in lysine binding have been identified ( Kaur et al. 2014 ).
2.A.3.1.2.name: Lysine:H + symporter.

2.A.3.1.20.description: Serine transporter, SerP2 or YdgB, of 459 aas and 12 TMSs ( Trip et al. 2013 ). Transports L-alanine (K m = 20 μM), D-alanine (K m = 38 μM), L-serine, D-serine (K m = 356 μM) and glycine ( Noens and Lolkema 2015 ). The encoding gene is adjacent to the one encoding SerP1 (TC# 2.A.3.1.21).
2.A.3.1.20.name: Serine transporter, SerP2 or YdgB, of 459 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.21.description: Serine uptake transporter, SerP1, of 259 aas and 12 TMSs ( Trip et al. 2013 ). L-serine is the highest affinity substrate (K m = 18 μM), but SerP1 also transports L-threonine and L-cysteine (K m values = 20 - 40 μM). Does not transport D-serine ( Noens and Lolkema 2015 ). The encoding gene is adjacent to a paralogue ( serP2 ) with broad specificity for D- and L-small semipolar amino acids and…
2.A.3.1.21.name: Serine uptake transporter, SerP1, of 259 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.22.description: Transporter for phenylalainine, tyrosine and tryptophan of 449 aas and 12 TMSs, FywP or YsjA ( Trip et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.1.22.name: Transporter for phenylalainine, tyrosine and tryptophan of 449 aas and 12 TMSs, FywP or YsjA.

2.A.3.1.23.description: ProY of 457 aas and 12 TMSs. 96% identical to ProY of Salmonella enterica , a cryptic proline transporter in this organism ( Liao et al. 1997 ).
2.A.3.1.23.name: ProY of 457 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.24.description: Asparagine transporter of 499 aas and 12 TMSs, 91% identical to the orthologue in Salmonella enterica (2.A.3.1.8) ( Jennings et al. 1995 ).
2.A.3.1.24.name: Asparagine transporter of 499 aas and 12 TMSs, 91% identical to the orthologue in Salmonella enterica (2.A.3.1.8).

2.A.3.1.25.description: D-serine/D-alanine/glycine transporter, LysP or AnsP, of 453 aas and 11 TMSs ( Xiao et al. 2020 ).
2.A.3.1.25.name: D-serine/D-alanine/glycine transporter, LysP or AnsP, of 453 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.3.description: Aromatic amino acid:H + symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs ( Cosgriff and Pittard 1997 ). Transports phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan ( Honoré and Cole 1990 ).
2.A.3.1.3.name: Aromatic amino acid:H + symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.1.4.description: γ-aminobutyrate:H + symporter, GabP. It also transports a variety of pyridine carboxylates. Phosphatidylethanolamine is required for its proper topological organization( Zhang et al. 2005 ). GabP in citrus may also play a role in GABA uptake ( Nehela and Killiny 2025 ).
2.A.3.1.4.name: γ-aminobutyrate:H + symporter, GabP.

2.A.3.1.5.description: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H + symporter, GabP ( Ferson et al. 1996 ; Zaprasis et al. 2014 ). Also transports 3-aminobutyrate, 3-aminopropanoate, cis-4-aminobutenoate ( Brechtel and King 1998 ).
2.A.3.1.5.name: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H + symporter, GabP.

2.A.3.1.7.description: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H + symporter (regulated by the small RNA, GcvB; Pulvermacher et al. , 2009 ). The system is active after growth in minimal medium but not after growth in complex medium ( Baisa et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.1.7.name: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H + symporter.

2.A.3.1.8.description: Asparagine permease (AnsP) of 497 aas and 12 TMSs ( Jennings et al. 1995 ).
2.A.3.1.8.name: Asparagine permease (AnsP) of 497 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.10.name: The Yeast Amino Acid Transporter (YAT) Family

2.A.3.10.1.description: High affinity histidine permease (also implicated in Mn 2+ efflux; Co 2+ , Ni 2+ , Zn 2+ and Cu 2+ uptake)
2.A.3.10.1.name: High affinity histidine permease (also implicated in Mn 2+ efflux; Co 2+ , Ni 2+ , Zn 2+ and Cu 2+ uptake)

2.A.3.10.10.description: Lysine permease of 611 aas and 13 putative TMSs, Lyp1. Extracellular loops affect either the localization or activity of Lyp1. Half of the mutants are located in the extension of extracellular loop 3 or in a predicted alpha-helix in extracellular loop 4 ( Van't Klooster et al. 2020 ). Phosphatidylserine and ergosterol are essential for Lyp1 function, and the transport activity displays a…
2.A.3.10.10.name: Lysine permease of 611 aas and 13 putative TMSs, Lyp1.

2.A.3.10.12.description: Leucine sensor/transcription factor. Mutants hyper- and hyposensitive to inducer ( Poulsen et al ., 2008 ) suggest a sensor mechanism involving outward and inward facing conformations.
2.A.3.10.12.name: Leucine sensor/transcription factor.

2.A.3.10.14.description: General amino acid permease with broad specificity, Agp3
2.A.3.10.14.name: General amino acid permease with broad specificity, Agp3

2.A.3.10.15.description: S-adenosylmethionine uptake permease, SAM3 (also takes up polyamines, glutamate, lysine and the toxic S-adenosylmethionine analogue sinefungin) ( Uemura et al ., 2007 ; Zheng et al ., 2007; Kashiwagi and Igarashi 2011 ).
2.A.3.10.15.name: S-adenosylmethionine uptake permease, SAM3 (also takes up polyamines, glutamate, lysine and the toxic S-adenosylmethionine analogue sinefungin).

2.A.3.10.17.description: General amino acid uptake permease, GAP1
2.A.3.10.17.name: General amino acid uptake permease, GAP1

2.A.3.10.18.description: The aromatic amino acid and leucine permease, ArlP (may be a general amino acid permease for neutral and basic [but not acidic] amino acids)
2.A.3.10.18.name: The aromatic amino acid and leucine permease, ArlP (may be a general amino acid permease for neutral and basic [but not acidic] amino acids)

2.A.3.10.19.description: The high affinity carnitine/polyamine (spermidine > putrescine)/carnitine), low affinity amino acid transporter, AGP2, of 596 aas and 12 TMSs ( Aouida et al ., 2005 ; Uemura et al ., 2007 ). Loss of the yeast transporter Agp2 upregulates the pleiotropic drug-resistant pump Pdr5 (TC# 3.A.1.205.1) and confers resistance to the protein synthesis inhibitor, cycloheximide ( Manzoor et al. 2024 ).
2.A.3.10.19.name: The high affinity carnitine/polyamine (spermidine > putrescine)/carnitine), low affinity amino acid transporter, AGP2, of 596 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.10.2.description: General amino acid permease (all L-amino acids and some D-amino acids as well as β-alanine, polyamines and GABA). Systematic mutational analysis of the intracellular regions of yeast Gap1 permease revealed multiple intracellular regions involved in its secretion, transport activity, and down-regulation ( Igarashi and Kashiwagi 2010; Merhi et al. , 2011 ). GAP1 is a "transceptor", fuctioning in…
2.A.3.10.2.name: General amino acid permease (all L-amino acids and some D-amino acids as well as β-alanine, polyamines and GABA).

2.A.3.10.20.description: The high affinity basic amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Can1 ( Matijekova and Sychrova, 1997 )
2.A.3.10.20.name: The high affinity basic amino acid (Arg, Lys, His) transporter, Can1

2.A.3.10.21.description: The basic amino acid (canavanine sensitivity) transporter, Cat1 ( Aspuria and Tamanoi, 2008 ).
2.A.3.10.21.name: The basic amino acid (canavanine sensitivity) transporter, Cat1.

2.A.3.10.22.description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal proline:H + symporter, AAP1 (binds and probably transports nonpolar, hydrophobic amino acids) ( Cappellazzo et al ., 2008 ).
2.A.3.10.22.name: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal proline:H + symporter, AAP1 (binds and probably transports nonpolar, hydrophobic amino acids).

2.A.3.10.23.description: Amino acid permease, GAP1. Transports Arg, Met, Leu and Phe ( Kraidlova et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.3.10.23.name: Amino acid permease, GAP1.

2.A.3.10.24.description: General amino and permease and transceptor, GAP2. Transports all amino acids including citruline and eight tested toxic amino acid derivatives ( Kraidlova et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.3.10.24.name: General amino and permease and transceptor, GAP2.

2.A.3.10.25.description: Arginine transporter, GAP4 ( Kraidlova et al. , 2011 )
2.A.3.10.25.name: Arginine transporter, GAP4

2.A.3.10.26.description: General amino acid porter, GAP6. Transports almost all amino acids tested except arginine and citruline ( Kraidlova et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.3.10.26.name: General amino acid porter, GAP6.

2.A.3.10.28.description: Probable amino-acid permease Meu22 (Meiotic expression up-regulated protein 22)
2.A.3.10.28.name: Probable amino-acid permease Meu22 (Meiotic expression up-regulated protein 22)

2.A.3.10.8.description: Tryptophan permease, Tat2. Regulated via endocytosis by ATP-binding Cassette Transporters, Pdr5 (3.A.1.205.1) and Yor1 (3.A.208.3) as well as a seven-transmembrane protein, RSB1 (9.A.27.1.2) ( Johnson et al. , 2010 ). Residues involved in binding and catalysis have been identified ( Kanda and Abe 2013 ). residues and regions important for proper folding and ER retention have been identified (…
2.A.3.10.8.name: Tryptophan permease, Tat2.

2.A.3.11.1.description: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA (also transports L-aspartate hydroxamate and glutamate, and possibly asparagine and glutamine; Lorca et al ., 2003 )
2.A.3.11.1.name: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA

2.A.3.12.1.description: The plasma membrane polyamine (putrescine, spermidine):H + uptake symporter, LmPOT1 (inhibited by pentamidine and protonophores) ( Hasne and Ullmann, 2005 ; Zhang et al. 2022 ).
2.A.3.12.1.name: The plasma membrane polyamine (putrescine, spermidine):H + uptake symporter, LmPOT1 (inhibited by pentamidine and protonophores).

2.A.3.12.3.description: Plasma membrane polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 490 aas, RMV1. Also called PUT3 and LAT1. Mutations give rise to partial paraquot (a toxic common herbicide that generates superoxide and reactive oxygen species (ROS)) ( Fujita and Shinozaki 2014 ).
2.A.3.12.3.name: Plasma membrane polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 490 aas, RMV1.

2.A.3.12.4.description: Golgi polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 478 aas, LAT4. Also called PUT2 and PAR1. Mutations give rise to paraquot resistance (Par1) both in A. thaliana and in rice. Probably present in the chloroplast membrane ( Fujita and Shinozaki 2014 ).
2.A.3.12.4.name: Golgi polyamine/paraquot uptake transporter of 478 aas, LAT4.

2.A.3.12.5.description: Spermidine-preferring polyamine transporter, PUT1 of 531 aas. Also transports paraquot ( Fujita and Shinozaki 2014 ).
2.A.3.12.5.name: Spermidine-preferring polyamine transporter, PUT1 of 531 aas.

2.A.3.13.1.description: The hydrophobic amino acid efflux transporter, YjeH (exports L-methionine and other neutral, hydrophobic amino acids such as Leu, Ile and Val; R. Figge, personal communication; Liu et al. 2015 ).
2.A.3.13.1.name: The hydrophobic amino acid efflux transporter, YjeH.

2.A.3.13.2.description: The Ceftriaxone resistance porter, YjeH ( Hu et al. 2007 ).
2.A.3.13.2.name: The Ceftriaxone resistance porter, YjeH.

2.A.3.13.3.description: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).
2.A.3.13.3.name: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.14.1.description: APC family member; Ala/Val/Leu-rich protein encoded within an operon that also encodes a 23S rRNA methyl transferase, RumA. Two half sized TrkA proteins are encoded within an operon that is divergently transcribed. Possibly, they regulate transport.
2.A.3.14.1.name: APC family member; Ala/Val/Leu-rich protein encoded within an operon that also encodes a 23S rRNA methyl transferase, RumA.

2.A.3.14.3.description: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs. 77% identical to an orthologue in Weissella viridescens that serves as a receptor or uptake transporter for the two peptide bacteriocin, plantaricin JK (1.C.30.1.1) ( Oppegård et al. 2016 ; Ekblad et al. 2017) .
2.A.3.14.3.name: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.15.2.description: Cationic amino acid transporter, CAAT (462 aas; 12 TMSs)
2.A.3.15.2.name: Cationic amino acid transporter, CAAT (462 aas; 12 TMSs)

2.A.3.2.name: The Basic Amino Acid/Polyamine Antiporter (APA) Family

2.A.3.2.1.description: Putrescine:ornithine antiporter for putrescine export; putrescine:H + symporter for uptake ( Igarashi and Kashiwagi 1996 ). Modeling tools have been used to gain information about the structures and functions of CadB and PotE in E. coli ( Tomitori et al. , 2012 ).
2.A.3.2.1.name: Putrescine:ornithine antiporter for putrescine export; putrescine:H + symporter for uptake.

2.A.3.2.10.description: Arginine/Ornithine antiporter of 497 aas and 13 TMSs, ArcD2 ( Trip et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.2.10.name: Arginine/Ornithine antiporter of 497 aas and 13 TMSs, ArcD2.

2.A.3.2.11.description: Arginine/Ornithine antiporter of 526 aas and 14 TMSs ( Trip et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.2.11.name: Arginine/Ornithine antiporter of 526 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.3.2.2.description: Cadaverine:lysine antiporter [Catalyzes cadaverine uptake via H + symport (Km=21μM) and cadaverine export (Km=300 μM) via cadaverine:lysine antiport.] ( Soksawatmaekhin et al ., 2004 ). Modeling tools have been used to gain information about the structures and functions of CadB and PotE in E. coli ( Tomitori et al. , 2012 ).
2.A.3.2.2.name: Cadaverine:lysine antiporter [Catalyzes cadaverine uptake via H + symport (Km=21μM) and cadaverine export (Km=300 μM) via cadaverine:lysine…

2.A.3.2.5.description: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance ( Fang et al ., 2007 ; Gong et al ., 2003 ; Iyer et al ., 2003 ). A projection structure at 6.5 Å resolution has been published ( Casagrande et al. , 2008 ), and the 3.2 Å resolution X-ray structure was determined by Fang et al. , 2009 and Gao et al. , 2009 . Protonation of glutamate 208…
2.A.3.2.5.name: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance.

2.A.3.2.6.description: Putative lysine uptake permease, YvsH ( Rodionov et al ., 2003 )
2.A.3.2.6.name: Putative lysine uptake permease, YvsH

2.A.3.3.name: The Cationic Amino Acid Transporter (CAT) Family

2.A.3.3.1.description: System Y+ high affinity basic amino acid transporter (CAT1) (ecotropic retrovival leukemia virus receptor (ERR)) (transports arginine, lysine and ornithine; Na + -independent)
2.A.3.3.1.name: System Y+ high affinity basic amino acid transporter (CAT1) (ecotropic retrovival leukemia virus receptor (ERR))

2.A.3.3.10.description: Cationic amino acid transporter 3 (CAT-3) (CAT3) (Cationic amino acid transporter y+) (Solute carrier family 7 member 3). Mutations in CAT3 are potential causes of childhood epilepsy ( Sourbron et al. 2021 ).
2.A.3.3.10.name: Cationic amino acid transporter 3 (CAT-3) (CAT3) (Cationic amino acid transporter y+) (Solute carrier family 7 member 3).

2.A.3.3.19.description: Histamine uptake transporter; involved in the utilization of histamine as a nitrogen source. In an operon with two histamine catabilic enzymes, and all are induced by hsitamine ( Johnson et al. 2008 ).
2.A.3.3.19.name: Histamine uptake transporter; involved in the utilization of histamine as a nitrogen source.

2.A.3.3.2.description: Low affinity basic amino acid transporter (CAT2) (T-cell early activation protein (TEA)) (transports arginine, lysine and ornithine; Na + -independent) ( Habermeier et al ., 2003 )
2.A.3.3.2.name: Low affinity basic amino acid transporter (CAT2) (T-cell early activation protein (TEA))

2.A.3.3.22.description: Amino acid transporter, PotE, of 475 aas.
2.A.3.3.22.name: Amino acid transporter, PotE, of 475 aas.

2.A.3.3.23.description: Branched chain amino acid (Leucine/isoleucine/valine) uptake transporter of 469 aas and 12 TMSs, BcaP or CitA ( den Hengst et al. 2006 ).
2.A.3.3.23.name: Branched chain amino acid (Leucine/isoleucine/valine) uptake transporter of 469 aas and 12 TMSs, BcaP or CitA.

2.A.3.3.24.description: Plastidic cationic amino acid transporter, CAT, of 582 aas and 14 TMSs. Exports phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan our of chloroplasts into the cytoplasm ( Widhalm et al. 2015 ).
2.A.3.3.24.name: Plastidic cationic amino acid transporter, CAT, of 582 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.3.3.3.description: Amino acid transporter, AAT1 or CAT1, of 594 aas and 14 TMSs. It is a high-affinity permease involved in the transport of the cationic amino acids (e.g., arginine, lysine, histidine, citrulline, valine, and glutamate). It transports mostly basic amino acids, and, to a lesser extent, neutral and acidic amino acids. It probably functions as a proton symporter. It transports histidine with a Km of…
2.A.3.3.3.name: Amino acid transporter, AAT1 or CAT1, of 594 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.3.3.4.description: The amino acid transporter, CAT6. Mediates electrogenic transport of large neutral and cationic amino acids in preference to other amino acids. Present in lateral root primordia, flowers and seeds ( Hammes et al ., 2006 )
2.A.3.3.4.name: The amino acid transporter, CAT6.

2.A.3.3.5.description: The brain L-cationic (Arg, Lys, Orn, 2,4-diamino- n -butyrate) transporter, CAT3 (capacity of trans-stimulation by internal Arg) ( Ito and Groudine, 1997 )
2.A.3.3.5.name: The brain L-cationic (Arg, Lys, Orn, 2,4-diamino- n -butyrate) transporter, CAT3 (capacity of trans-stimulation by internal Arg)

2.A.3.3.8.description: Low affinity cationic amino acid transporter 2 (CAT-2) (CAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 2) ( Closs 1996 ). Elevated SLC7A2 expression is associated with an abnormal neuroinflammatory response and nitrosative stress in Huntington's disease ( Gaudet et al. 2024 ).
2.A.3.3.8.name: Low affinity cationic amino acid transporter 2 (CAT-2) (CAT2) (Solute carrier family 7 member 2).

2.A.3.3.9.description: High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1 (CAT-1) (CAT1, CTR1) (Ecotropic retroviral leukemia receptor homologue) (ERR), (SLC7a1) (System Y+ basic amino acid transporter) ( Closs 1996 ). It takes up Arginine, Lysine and Ornithine. Its gene shows increased expression in various cancers such as colorectal cancer (CRC) ( Okita et al. 2020 ). Treatment of a blood-brain barrier (BBB) mimetic…
2.A.3.3.9.name: High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1 (CAT-1) (CAT1, CTR1) (Ecotropic retroviral leukemia receptor homologue) (ERR), (SLC7a1)

2.A.3.4.1.description: The single high affinity plasma membrane choline transporter of 563 aas and 12 TMSs. Expression of the CTR/ HNM1 gene in wild-type cells is regulated by phospholipid precursors, inositol and choline, but no such effect is seen in cells bearing mutations in the phospholipid regulatory genes INO2, INO4 and OPI1. There is no regulation by INO2 and OPI1 in the absence of a conserved decamer motif…
2.A.3.4.1.name: The single high affinity plasma membrane choline transporter of 563 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.3.4.3.description: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) permease, Uga4 (also transports the polyamine, putrescine) ( Uemura et al ., 2007 ; Kashiwagi and Igarashi 2011 ).
2.A.3.4.3.name: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) permease, Uga4 (also transports the polyamine, putrescine).

2.A.3.4.6.description: The thiamine (vitamin B 1 ) transporter, Thi9 (SPAC9.10). Uptake is inhibited by pyrithiamine, oxythiamine, amprolium, and the thiazole part of thiamine indicating that these compounds are substrates of Thi9 ( Vogl et al ., 2008 ).
2.A.3.4.6.name: The thiamine (vitamin B 1 ) transporter, Thi9 (SPAC9.10).

2.A.3.4.8.description: SwnT of 501 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. Slafractonia leguminicola infects red clover and other legumes, causing black patch disease. This fungus produces two mycotoxins, slaframine and swainsonine, that are toxic to livestock grazing on clover hay or pasture infested with S. leguminicola . Swainsonine toxicosis causes locoism, while slaframine causes slobbers syndrome. SwnT may…
2.A.3.4.8.name: SwnT of 501 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.3.6.1.description: Putative cationic amino acid permease of 736 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.
2.A.3.6.1.name: Putative cationic amino acid permease of 736 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.3.6.2.description: The putative permease, MtbP (MA2426) (possibly a methyl amine uptake porter; D.J. Ferguson, personal communication) (12 putative TMSs)
2.A.3.6.2.name: The putative permease, MtbP (MA2426) (possibly a methyl amine uptake porter; D.J. Ferguson, personal communication) (12 putative TMSs)

2.A.3.6.3.description: ApcT, a proton coupled broad specificity amino acid transporter. 3-d structure available at 2.3Å resolution (3GIA_A; Shaffer et al. , 2009 ).
2.A.3.6.3.name: ApcT, a proton coupled broad specificity amino acid transporter.

2.A.3.7.1.description: Glutamate:γ-aminobutyrate antiporter of 477 aas and 12 TMSs, GadC. Expression of gadCB in L. lactis in the presence of chloride is increased when the culture pH decreases to low levels, while glutamate stimulated gadCB expression ( Sanders et al. 1998 ). These genes encode a glutamate-dependent acid resistance mechanism that is optimally active when needed for acid neutralization.
2.A.3.7.1.name: Glutamate:γ-aminobutyrate antiporter of 477 aas and 12 TMSs, GadC.

2.A.3.7.3.description: Glutamate:GABA antiporter, GadC (YcaM). GadC, transports GABA/Glu only under acidic conditions, with no detectable activity at pH values higher than 6.5 ( Ma et al. , 2012 ). Ma et al. ( 2012 ) determined the crystal structure of GadC at 3.1 Å resolution under basic conditions. GadC, comprising 12 TMSs, exists in a closed state, with its carboxy-terminal domain serving as a plug to block an…
2.A.3.7.3.name: Glutamate:GABA antiporter, GadC (YcaM).

2.A.3.7.6.description: Aspartate/Glutamate transporter of 488 aas and 12 TMSs, AcaP ( Trip et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.7.6.name: Aspartate/Glutamate transporter of 488 aas and 12 TMSs, AcaP.

2.A.3.7.7.description: Putriscine/agmatine transporter of 466 aas and 12 TMSs, AguD or YrfD ( Trip et al. 2013 ).
2.A.3.7.7.name: Putriscine/agmatine transporter of 466 aas and 12 TMSs, AguD or YrfD.

2.A.3.8.name: The L-type Amino Acid Transporter (LAT) Family (Many LAT family members function as heterooligomers with rBAT and/or 4F2hc (TC #8.A.9))

2.A.3.8.1.description: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, LAT1 (Na + -independent) (prefers amino acids with branched or aromatic side chains: Phe, Ile, Leu, Val, Trp, His; catalyzes obligatory exchange with μM affinities on the outside and mM affinities on the inside [1000x difference]). Both LAT1 and LAT2 (2.A.3.8.6) catalyze uptake of S -nitroso-L-cysteine. These and other LAT family members are specifically…
2.A.3.8.1.name: L-type neutral amino acid transporter, LAT1 (Na + -independent)

2.A.3.8.10.description: Aromatic amino acid exchanger, AAT-9 ( Veljkovic et al. , 2004b )
2.A.3.8.10.name: Aromatic amino acid exchanger, AAT-9

2.A.3.8.11.description: The aromatic-preferring amino acid transporter (ArpAT or Slc7a15 ). Functions with rBAT or 4F2hc (8.A.9) and transports preferentially tyr and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA), but also ala, glu, ser, cys and arg by a Na + -independent mechanism (present in mouse, rat, dog and chicken, but silenced in humans and chimps)( Fernández et al. , 2005 ; Sato et al ., 2005 ). It is expressed in the…
2.A.3.8.11.name: The aromatic-preferring amino acid transporter (ArpAT or Slc7a15 ).

2.A.3.8.12.description: The Ser/Thr exchange transporter (SteT) (also transports aromatic amino acids with lower efficiency) ( Reig et al ., 2007 ). The substrate-bound state of SteT shows increased conformational flexibility and kinetic stability, enabling transport of substrate across the cell membrane ( Bippes et al. 2009 ). 2.A.31.3.1.name: Boron efflux transporter for xylem loading.

2.A.31.3.2.description: Boron efflux transporter, Ynl275w ( Jennings et al ., 2007 )
2.A.31.3.2.name: Boron efflux transporter, Ynl275w

2.A.31.3.4.description: Borate/boric acid (boron) efflux transporter, Bor1. Involved in boron deficiency tolerance ( Cañon et al. 2013 ).
2.A.31.3.4.name: Borate/boric acid (boron) efflux transporter, Bor1.

2.A.31.3.5.description: Borate exporter of 666 aas and 13 TMSs with 5 cytooplasmic α-helices, Bot1. Also known as the barley root anion-permeable transporter. Confers tolerance to boron. It is believed to be trimeric. Transport is dependent on Na + ( Nagarajan et al. 2016 ).
2.A.31.3.5.name: Borate exporter of 666 aas and 13 TMSs with 5 cytooplasmic α-helices, Bot1.

2.A.31.3.6.description: Inorganic anion transporter and exchanger, BOR1, of 701 aas and 11 TMSs. It transports borate and other anions ( Diehn et al. 2019 ).
2.A.31.3.6.name: Inorganic anion transporter and exchanger, BOR1, of 701 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.31.3.7.description: Sodium bicarbonate transporter family protein of 568 aas and ~13 TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement with two halves of similar sequence.
2.A.31.3.7.name: Sodium bicarbonate transporter family protein of 568 aas and ~13 TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement with two halves of similar sequence.

2.A.33.1.1.description: NhaA Na + :2H + antiporter (structure determined and mechanism proposed ( Williams, 2000 ; Hunte et al ., 2005 ; Olkhova et al ., 2006 ; Screpanti et al ., 2006 ; Arkin et al ., 2007 )). The K300R mutant is also electrogenic ( Călinescu et al. 2017 ). TMS II lines the cation passage, and Asp65 is critical for pH activation of the antiporter ( Herz et al. , 2010 ). NhaA is subject to pH-activation…
2.A.33.1.1.name: NhaA Na + :2H + antiporter (structure determined and mechanism proposed).

2.A.33.1.2.description: NhaA Na + ,K + :H + antiporter ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 )
2.A.33.1.2.name: NhaA Na + ,K + :H + antiporter

2.A.33.1.7.description: Na + or Ca 2+ /H + antiporter, NhaA of 492 aas and 12 TMSs, active at alkaline pH. Confers tolerance to high NaCl concentrations. Has a Km Na + of 0.2 - 1 mM, and a Km Ca 2+ of 0.1 - 0.3 mM ( Dawut et al. 2018 ).
2.A.33.1.7.name: Na + or Ca 2+ /H + antiporter, NhaA of 492 aas and 12 TMSs, active at alkaline pH.

2.A.34.1.1.description: NhaB Na + :H + antiporter of 513 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. NhaB is physiologically important when the level of NhaA activity is growth limiting, when nhaA is not sufficiently induced, and/or when NhaA is not activated ( Pinner et al. 1993 ). The stoichiometry of NhaB is 3H + /2Na + , different from that of NhaA ( Pinner et al. 1994 ). It is required for intracellular pH regulation under alkaline…
2.A.34.1.1.name: NhaB Na + :H + antiporter of 513 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.

2.A.34.1.2.description: NhaB Na + ,K + :H + antiporter ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 )
2.A.34.1.2.name: NhaB Na + ,K + :H + antiporter

2.A.34.1.3.description: Na + /H + antiporter that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons, NhaB of 500 aas. Can also extrude lithium in exchange for protons. Km values for Li + and Na + of 2.0 mM and 1.3 mM, respectively. The antiport activity was inhibited by amiloride with a Ki value of 0.04 mM ( Kuroda et al. 2004 ).
2.A.34.1.3.name: Na + /H + antiporter that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons, NhaB of 500 aas.

2.A.35.1.2.description: Malate + H + : lactate + Na + antiporter, MleN or YqkI of 468 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement ( Wei et al. 2000 ).
2.A.35.1.2.name: Malate + H + : lactate + Na + antiporter, MleN or YqkI of 468 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.35.1.3.description: The putative tyrosine permease, TyrT, of 472 aas and 12 TMSs. Also called NhaC2 ( Panina et al. , 2003 ; Rodionov et al. 2004).
2.A.35.1.3.name: The putative tyrosine permease, TyrT, of 472 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.35.1.4.description: The arginine/ornithine antiporter ArcD ( Wimmer et al. 2008 )
2.A.35.1.4.name: The arginine/ornithine antiporter ArcD

2.A.35.1.5.description: The putative methionine porter, MetT. Regulated by S-adenosylmethionine-dependent repressor MetJ ( Rodionov et al. 2011 ).
2.A.35.1.5.name: The putative methionine porter, MetT.

2.A.35.1.6.description: YheL; TyrT, putative tyrosine uptake cation symporter; NhaC, putative Na + /H + antiporter (Sodium/hydrogen antiporter) ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ).
2.A.35.1.6.name: YheL; TyrT, putative tyrosine uptake cation symporter; NhaC, putative Na + /H + antiporter (Sodium/hydrogen antiporter).

2.A.35.1.8.description: Predicted methionine uptaie cation symporter, MetT, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ).
2.A.35.1.8.name: Predicted methionine uptaie cation symporter, MetT, of 433 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.35.1.9.description: Predicted methioine:cation symporter of 459 aas and 12 TMSs, MetT ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ). Also called NhaC.
2.A.35.1.9.name: Predicted methioine:cation symporter of 459 aas and 12 TMSs, MetT.

2.A.35.2.1.description: Na + /H + antiporter of the NhaC family
2.A.35.2.1.name: Na + /H + antiporter of the NhaC family

2.A.35.2.2.description: Putative lysine transporter, LysW. Regulated by Lysine riboswitch ( Rodionov et al. 2003 )
2.A.35.2.2.name: Putative lysine transporter, LysW.

2.A.35.2.3.description: The NhaC Na + :H + antiporter, G1-NhaC (functions in Na + extrusion at lower pH values and in pH homeostasis at pH 10 under Na + -limiting conditions) ( Liew et al ., 2007 ).
2.A.35.2.3.name: The NhaC Na + :H + antiporter, G1-NhaC

2.A.36.1.1.description: Na + :H + antiporter 1 (Nhe-1) (Regulated by Daxx (O35613)). An integral membrane protein that regulates intracellular pH and has a large N-terminal membrane domain of 12 transmembrane segments and an intracellular C-terminal regulatory domain ( Reddy et al ., 2008 ). The dimer catalyzes antiport with 2Na + /2H + stoichiometry ( Fuster et al. , 2008 ). Nedd4-1 and β-arrestin-1 are key regulators…
2.A.36.1.1.name: Na + :H + antiporter 1 (Nhe-1) (Regulated by Daxx (O35613)).

2.A.36.1.11.description: The Na + :H + Exchanger, NHE1, is developmentally regulated and necessary for cell polarity ( Patel and Barber, 2005 ).
2.A.36.1.11.name: The Na + :H + Exchanger, NHE1, is developmentally regulated and necessary for cell polarity.

2.A.36.1.12.description: Na + :H + antiporter, NHX1; (vacuolar/endosomal Na + tolerance protein). Plays roles in ion homeostasis and vesicle trafficing ( Mukherjee et al. 2006 ). The structures and functions of these NHX homologues have been reviewed ( Dutta and Fliegel 2018 ). K + influx/efflux regulates mitochondrial energetics while maintaining mitochondrial ionic balance and volume homeostasis ( Malas et al. 2022 ).
2.A.36.1.12.name: Na + :H + antiporter, NHX1; (vacuolar/endosomal Na + tolerance protein).

2.A.36.1.13.description: Na + /H + exchanger-1 (NHE1). Stoichiometry = 1:1. TMS VI of NHE1 is a discontinuous pore-lining helix with residues Asn(227), Ile(233), and Leu(243) lining the translocation pore ( Tzeng et al. , 2010 ). (orthologous to NHE1 of rat, TC# 2.A.36.1.1). Both Pro167 and Pro168 in TMS IV are required for normal NHE activity ( Slepkov et al. 2004 ). NHE1 regulates internal pH in human monocytes and is…
2.A.36.1.13.name: Na + /H + exchanger-1 (NHE1).

2.A.36.1.14.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 6 (Na + /H + exchanger 6) (NHE-6) (Solute carrier family 9 member 6; SLC9A6). This Na + /H + exchanger is encoded by an X-linked gene that is widely expressed and especially abundant in brain, heart and skeletal muscle where it is implicated in endosomal pH homeostasis and trafficking as well as maintenance of cell polarity. Several mutations in the coding region of NHE6…
2.A.36.1.14.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 6 (Na + /H + exchanger 6) (NHE-6) (Solute carrier family 9 member 6; SLC9A6).

2.A.36.1.15.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (Na + /H + exchanger 3) (NHE-3) of 834 aas and 12 TMSs (Solute carrier family 9 member 3) ( Dominguez Rieg et al. 2016 ). A missense mutation in SLC26A3 is associated with human male subfertility and impaired activation of CFTR ( Wedenoja et al. 2017 ). SLC9A3 affects vas deferens development ( Wu et al. 2019 ). SLC9A3 deficiency-mediated micturition dysfunction is…
2.A.36.1.15.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (Na + /H + exchanger 3) (NHE-3) of 834 aas and 12 TMSs (Solute carrier family 9 member 3).

2.A.36.1.16.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 5 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 5) (NHE-5) (Solute carrier family 9 member 5)
2.A.36.1.16.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 5 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 5) (NHE-5) (Solute carrier family 9 member 5)

2.A.36.1.17.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2 (Na + /H + exchanger 2) (NHE-2 or NHE2) (Solute carrier family 9 member 2). Mediates butyrate-dependent Na + absorption ( Rajendran et al. 2015 ).
2.A.36.1.17.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2 (Na + /H + exchanger 2) (NHE-2 or NHE2) (Solute carrier family 9 member 2).

2.A.36.1.18.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 4) (NHE-4) (Solute carrier family 9 member 4). NHE4 had previously been suggested to play a critical role in renal ammonia metabolism through its role in thick ascending limb (TAL) ammonia transport. Lee et al. 2025 showed that its deletion does not alter renal ammonia handling and that neither the mouse nor human kidney expresses NHE4 in the TAL.
2.A.36.1.18.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4 (Na(+)/H(+) exchanger 4) (NHE-4) (Solute carrier family 9 member 4).

2.A.36.1.19.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 9 (Na + /H + exchanger 9) (NHE-9; NHE9) (Solute carrier family 9 member 9, SLC9A9) of 645 aas and 12 TMSs. It may act in electroneutral exchange of protons for Na + across membranes and is involved in the effusion of Golgi luminal H + in exchange for cytosolic cations. It is also involved in organellar ion homeostasis by contributing to the maintenance of the unique…
2.A.36.1.19.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 9 (Na + /H + exchanger 9) (NHE-9; NHE9) (Solute carrier family 9 member 9, SLC9A9) of 645 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.36.1.2.description: N + :H + antiporter 3 (NHE-3 or NHE3). Regulated by Na + /H + exchange regulatory cofactors (NHERF; O14745; TC #8.A.24.1.1) ( Seidler et al. , 2009 ). Cyclic AMP-mediated endocytosis of intestinal epithelial NHE3 requires binding to synaptotagmin 1 ( Musch et al. , 2010 ). Decreased activity is responsible for congenital Na + diarrhea in the human brush boarder ( Janecke et al. 2015 ). Reduced…
2.A.36.1.2.name: N + :H + antiporter 3 (NHE-3 or NHE3).

2.A.36.1.20.description: Endomembrane (Golgi) K + , Na + /H + exchanger 5, NHX5, of 521 aas and 11 TMSs. Three acidic residues are critical for transport activity as well as seedling growth, regulation of protein transport into vesicles and ionic homeostasis ( Qiu 2016 ). NHX6 is 80% identical to NHX5 (535 aas and 11 TMSs) and serves the same function. They are all located in Golgi, trans-Golgi network (TGN), endoplasmic…
2.A.36.1.20.name: Endomembrane (Golgi) K + , Na + /H + exchanger 5, NHX5, of 521 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.36.1.22.description: Na + /H + exchanger, beta-like, NHE, of 917 aas and 11 putative TMSs. Involved in pH homeostasis ( Li et al. 2019 ).
2.A.36.1.22.name: Na + /H + exchanger, beta-like, NHE, of 917 aas and 11 putative TMSs.

2.A.36.1.23.description: Sodium/proton exchanger of 529 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs. The six NHXs in grape have been bioinformatically characterized ( Ayadi et al. 2019 ). This protein is 81% identical to the exchanger with TC# 2.A.36.1.5.
2.A.36.1.23.name: Sodium/proton exchanger of 529 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.1.24.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2a NHE2a, of 818 aas and 13 TMSs. Expression of several NHE genes were regulated bylow, isotonic or high salinity treatments, indicating an involvements in salinity and osmotic regulation in teleosts ( Liu et al. 2019 ).
2.A.36.1.24.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2a NHE2a, of 818 aas and 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.1.3.description: Na + /K + :H + antiporter, Nhe-7, present in the Golgi apparatus and endosomes. There are four isoforms, NHE6-9. They regulate the luminal pH as well as intracellular trafficking, and function in cell polarity development ( Ohgaki et al. , 2011 ). Nhe-6 (Nhe6) is associated with X-linked intellectural disability and autism when processing and trafficking is impaired ( Ilie et al. 2013 ).
2.A.36.1.3.name: Na + /K + :H + antiporter, Nhe-7, present in the Golgi apparatus and endosomes.

2.A.36.1.4.description: Cl - -dependent Na + :H + antiporter (Nhe) (residues 1-375 are identical to Nhe-1 [TC #2.A.36.1.1]).
2.A.36.1.4.name: Cl - -dependent Na + :H + antiporter (Nhe) (residues 1-375 are identical to Nhe-1 [TC #2.A.36.1.1]).

2.A.36.1.5.description: Na + /K + :H + antiporter, NHX2, of531 aas and 12 TMSs. It is involved in salt tolerance.
2.A.36.1.5.name: Na + /K + :H + antiporter, NHX2, of531 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.36.1.6.description: Zebrafish Na + :H + antiporter NheC ( Yan et al ., 2007 ) (most similar to TC# 2.A.36.1.2, 48% identical)
2.A.36.1.6.name: Zebrafish Na + :H + antiporter NheC (most similar to TC# 2.A.36.1.2, 48% identical)

2.A.36.1.7.description: The basolateral intestinal Na + /H + antiporter PBO-4 ( Beg et al ., 2008 )
2.A.36.1.7.name: The basolateral intestinal Na + /H + antiporter PBO-4

2.A.36.1.8.description: Na + /H + exchanger, Nhx-2 ( Pfeiffer et al ., 2008 )
2.A.36.1.8.name: Na + /H + exchanger, Nhx-2

2.A.36.1.9.description: Human Na + /H + Exchanger, NHE-8 or SLC9A8. Functions in intracellular pH homeostasis, cell volume regulation, and electroneutral NaCl absorption in epithelia. It attenuates Ca 2+ influx in the proximal tubular epithelium ( Wiebe et al. 2019 ).
2.A.36.1.9.name: Human Na + /H + Exchanger, NHE-8 or SLC9A8.

2.A.36.2.2.description: The electroneutral Na + /Li + :H + antiporter, Nha2. Catalyzes Na + :Li + antiport; contributes to salt homeostasis. It correlates with heritable hypertension ( Xiang et al ., 2007 ) and is critical for insulin secretion ( Deisl et al. 2013 ). Like electrogenic Na + /H + exchangers, it has two conserved aspartyl residues in the Na + binding site but seems to be electroneutral ( Uzdavinys et al…
2.A.36.2.2.name: The electroneutral Na + /Li + :H + antiporter, Nha2.

2.A.36.2.3.description: solute carrier family 9, subfamily B, SLC9B. (NHA1, cation proton antiporter 1). The SLC9 gene family encodes Na + /H + exchangers (NHEs), a group of membrane transport proteins critically involved in the regulation of cytoplasmic and organellar pH, cell volume, as well as systemic acid-base and volume homeostasis ( Anderegg et al. 2022 ). NHEs of the SLC9A subfamily (NHE 1-9) are well-known for…
2.A.36.2.3.name: solute carrier family 9, subfamily B, SLC9B. (NHA1, cation proton antiporter 1).

2.A.36.3.1.description: Putative antiporter of 549 aas (function unknown) ( Verkhovskaya et al. 2001 ).
2.A.36.3.1.name: Putative antiporter of 549 aas (function unknown).

2.A.36.3.2.description: Na + , K + , Li + , Rb + :H + antiporter, YvgP
2.A.36.3.2.name: Na + , K + , Li + , Rb + :H + antiporter, YvgP

2.A.36.4.1.description: [Na + or K + ]:H + antiporter Nha1 of 985 aas and 13 or 14 predicted TMSs, all at the N-terminus of the protein in a possible 6 +1 + 6 TMS arrangement. The ceontral TMS is much lower in hydrophobicity than the other TMSs. All TMSs are in residues 1 - 430 while the rest of the protein is strongly hydrophilic.
2.A.36.4.1.name: [Na + or K + ]:H + antiporter Nha1 of 985 aas and 13 or 14 predicted TMSs, all at the N-terminus of the protein in a possible 6 +1 + 6 TMS…

2.A.36.4.2.description: Na + :H + antiporter, Nha2 or Sod2-22. Exports Na+ and Li+ but not K+. Three residues, T141 in TMS 4, A179 in TMS 5 and V375 in TMS 11, determine the cation selectivity ( Kinclova-Zimmermannova et al. 2015 ).
2.A.36.4.2.name: Na + :H + antiporter, Nha2 or Sod2-22.

2.A.36.4.3.description: Na + :H + antiporter, Nha1 or Sod2 of 468 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs. It provides salt tolerance by removing sodium and lithium ions in exchange for protons, and TMS 4 plays an important role ( Ullah et al. 2013 ). The Asp266/Asp267 pair are critical for Sod2 function ( Fliegel 2005 ). Residues within TMS 11 also play important roles in transport, suggesting that this TMS forms part of the ion…
2.A.36.4.3.name: Na + :H + antiporter, Nha1 or Sod2 of 468 aas and 12 or 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.4.4.description: The K + , Rb + and other alkali metal cation efflux porter, Cnh1 ( Kinclova-Zimmermannova and Sychrova, 2007 ). Transports Na + , K + , Li + and Rb + in several Candida species. Confers tolerance to high salt concentrations ( Krauke and Sychrova 2008 ).
2.A.36.4.4.name: The K + , Rb + and other alkali metal cation efflux porter, Cnh1.

2.A.36.5.1.description: Low-affinity Na + (K + , Li + or Cs + ):H + antiporter, Nhx1. It is up-regluated in response to high salt stress conditions ( Yang et al. 2018 ). It has the same general architecture as CHX17 of A. thaliana (TC# 2.A.37.4.2) ( Sze and Chanroj 2018 ). Four NHX proteins (1-4) have been identified in Argania spinosa L ( Karim et al. 2020 ). Structural features of Grapevine NHX antiporters have been…
2.A.36.5.1.name: Low-affinity Na + (K + , Li + or Cs + ):H + antiporter, Nhx1.

2.A.36.5.2.description: Vacuolar Na + /H + antiporter, NHX1. A class-I type NHX. Confers NaCl tolerance and therefore pumps Na + from the cytosol to the vacuole ( Jha et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.36.5.2.name: Vacuolar Na + /H + antiporter, NHX1.

2.A.36.5.3.description: Vacuolar Na + /H + exchanger, DgNHX1 or NHX1, of 510 aas and 13 putative (but possibly 9 actual) TMSs. Involved in adaptation to salt stress conditions and expressed under these same conditions ( Liu et al. 2013 ).
2.A.36.5.3.name: Vacuolar Na + /H + exchanger, DgNHX1 or NHX1, of 510 aas and 13 putative (but possibly 9 actual) TMSs.

2.A.36.5.4.description: Vacuorlar Na + /H + exchanger, Nhx1 of 542 aas and 13 TMSs. Involved in salt tolerance ( Mishra et al. 2014 ).
2.A.36.5.4.name: Vacuorlar Na + /H + exchanger, Nhx1 of 542 aas and 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.5.5.description: Na + :H + antiporter, Nhx1 of 470 aas and 9 TMSs. NHX1 can confer a high level of salinity tolerance when overexpressed in Brassica juncea . Verma et al. 2007 reported its functional characterization. Overexpression conferred a high level of salinity tolerance in rice. Transgenic rice plants overexpressing PgNHX1 developed more extensive root systems and completed their life cycle by setting…
2.A.36.5.5.name: Na + :H + antiporter, Nhx1 of 470 aas and 9 TMSs.

2.A.36.5.6.description: Na + /Li + /H + exchanger of 545 aas and 12 TMSs, NHX3. It is localized to the tonoplast membrane where it increases salt tolerance and reduces Li + toxicity. TMS 11 is important in Li + and Na + transport ( Pan et al. 2017 ).
2.A.36.5.6.name: Na + /Li + /H + exchanger of 545 aas and 12 TMSs, NHX3.

2.A.36.5.8.description: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4, NHX4, of 529 aas and 8 TMSs. This endosomal protein is critical for salt tolerance in cotton ( Ma et al. 2020 ). It probably acts as a low affinity electroneutral exchanger of protons for cations such as Na + or K + across membranes, but may also exchange Li + and Cs + with lower affinities.
2.A.36.5.8.name: Sodium/hydrogen exchanger 4, NHX4, of 529 aas and 8 TMSs.

2.A.36.5.9.description: The sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2, NHX2, of 546 aas and 13 TMSs. It catalyzes the low affinity electroneutral exchange of protons for cations such as Na + or K + across membranes, and may also exchange Li + and Cs + with a lower affinity. It is involved in vacuolar ion compartmentalization necessary for cell volume regulation and cytoplasmic Na + detoxification ( Yokoi et al. 2002 ). Its ortholog…
2.A.36.5.9.name: The sodium/hydrogen exchanger 2, NHX2, of 546 aas and 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.6.10.description: Na + /H + antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH. Exchanges Na + or Li + but not K + for H + ( Zou et al. 2008 ). Confers Na + and Li + tolerance.
2.A.36.6.10.name: Na + /H + antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH.

2.A.36.6.11.description: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs. Involved in growth at low osmolarity, intracellular K + maintenance, and volume regulation ( Verkhovskaya et al. 2001 ). Hyposaline xonsiriona induces oxidative stress and disrupts gut microbiome stability in C. notata , thereby triggering complex physiological and molecular responses ( Kim et al. 2025 ).
2.A.36.6.11.name: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs.

2.A.36.6.2.description: Na + (Li + ):H + antiporter NhaG ( Gouda et al. 2001 ). Several very similar antiporters have been isolated from uncultured bacteria from a lake in China ( Wang et al. 2013 ).
2.A.36.6.2.name: Na + (Li + ):H + antiporter NhaG.

2.A.36.6.3.description: K + :H + antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2). Participates in volume control under low osmorality conditions ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 ; Resch et al. , 2010 )
2.A.36.6.3.name: K + :H + antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2).

2.A.36.6.4.description: The K + (NH 4 + ):H + antiporter, NhaP (confers alkali resistance for alkaline pH homeostasis) ( Wei et al ., 2007 )
2.A.36.6.4.name: The K + (NH 4 + ):H + antiporter, NhaP (confers alkali resistance for alkaline pH homeostasis)

2.A.36.6.5.description: K + :H + antiporter NhaP2 (catalyzes K + :H + and Na + :H + exchange; Resch et al. , 2010 ). (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3). A cation binding pocket in the middle of the membrane and a pathway leading to it have been identified ( Mourin et al. 2018 ). There are 3 NhaP types in Vibrio cholerae (Vc-NhaP1, 2, and 3). They are critical for maintenance of K + homeostasis in the cytoplasm, and all 3 are…
2.A.36.6.5.name: K + :H + antiporter NhaP2. (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3).

2.A.36.6.6.description: Na + /H + antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1). NhaP1 is a dimer with 13 TMSs per monomer as revealed by electron crystalography of 2-d crystals ( Goswami et al. 2011 ). This structure is contrasted with that of the distantly related bacterial NhaA; these two structures are quite different in detail, but similar within the 6 TMS repeat unit. Asp234/235 of helix VIII are involved in ligand-binding, and helix X…
2.A.36.6.6.name: Na + /H + antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1).

2.A.36.6.7.description: NhaH Na + /Li + /H + antiporter ( Yang et al. 2006 ).
2.A.36.6.7.name: NhaH Na + /Li + /H + antiporter.

2.A.36.6.8.description: Na + /H + antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons. Has weak (if any) Li + /H + antiport activity ( Kuroda et al. 2004 ).
2.A.36.6.8.name: Na + /H + antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons.

2.A.36.6.9.description: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP, of 443 aas. Several 3-d structures are known ( Wöhlert et al. 2014 ). The ion is coordinated by three acidic side chains, a water molecule, a serine and a main-chain carbonyl in an unwound stretch of TMS 5 at the deepest point of a negatively charged cytoplasmic funnel.
