2.A.4.1.7.name: Dimeric Zn 2+ efflux carrier of 299 aas and 5 TMSs, CzcD.

2.A.4.2.1.description: Mitochondrial Co 2+ /Zn 2+ uptake (into mitochondria) permease. A single mutation (N45I) increases the specificity for Fe 2+ and decreases it for Co 2+ ( Lin et al. , 2008 ).
2.A.4.2.1.name: Mitochondrial Co 2+ /Zn 2+ uptake (into mitochondria) permease.

2.A.4.2.2.description: Vacuolar Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ uptake (into vacuoles) permease (Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ :H + antiporter). A single mutation (N44I) changes the specificity from Zn 2+ to Fe 2+ ( Lin et al. , 2008 ). Lin et al. (2009) have identified transmembrane residues that determine metal specificity.
2.A.4.2.2.name: Vacuolar Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ uptake (into vacuoles) permease (Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ :H + antiporter).

2.A.4.2.3.description: Plasma membrane Zn 2+ efflux permease. Substituing H43 with N (asn) changed the specificity from Zn 2+ to Mn 2+ , and this difference was found in the Mn 2+ -specific metal ion exporter, ZnT10 (TC# 2.A.4.2.5) ( Nishito et al. 2016 ). Expression on the cell surface is controlled by cellular zinc levels ( Nishito and Kambe 2019 ).
2.A.4.2.3.name: Plasma membrane Zn 2+ efflux permease.

2.A.4.2.5.description: Solute carrier family 30, member 10, ZnT10. Manganese efflux transporteer of 485 aas and 6 TMSs in a 4 + 2 TMS arrangement with two long hydrophilic regions between residues 135 and 240, and residues 300 and 485 ( Nishito et al. 2016 ). Homozygous mutations lead to the development of familial manganese Mn 2+ -induced parkinsonism; it is a cell surface-localized Mn 2+ efflux transporter, and…
2.A.4.2.5.name: Solute carrier family 30, member 10, ZnT10.

2.A.4.2.6.description: Zinc transporter 1 (ZnT-1 or ZnT1) (Solute carrier family 30 member 1). The loss of the sialic acid transporter SLC35A1/CST (TC# 2.A.7.12.11) and the zinc transporter, ZnT1, affected cell survival upon infection with cytolytic vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). Both of these transporters seem to play a role in the apoptotic response induced by VSV ( Moskovskich et al. 2019 ). ZnT1 functions by Zn…
2.A.4.2.6.name: Zinc transporter 1 (ZnT-1 or ZnT1) (Solute carrier family 30 member 1).

2.A.4.2.7.description: ZnT63C Zinc exporter, ZnT1, of 545 aas and 5 putative TMSs ( Lye et al. 2013 ; Dechen et al. 2015 ).
2.A.4.2.7.name: ZnT63C Zinc exporter, ZnT1, of 545 aas and 5 putative TMSs.

2.A.4.2.8.description: Vacuolar CDF1 transporter. Transports Zn 2+ , Co 2+ and Cd 2+ but not Mn 2+ , of 487 aas and 6 TMSs ( Sácký et al. 2016 ).
2.A.4.2.8.name: Vacuolar CDF1 transporter.

2.A.4.2.9.description: The plasma membrane zinc efflux system, ZnT-1, of 485 aas and 6 predicted TMSs with a large histidine-rich intracellular loop between TMSs 4 and 5 and intracellular C- and N-termini ( Balesaria and Hogstrand 2006 ).
2.A.4.2.9.name: The plasma membrane zinc efflux system, ZnT-1, of 485 aas and 6 predicted TMSs with a large histidine-rich intracellular loop between TMSs 4 and 5…

2.A.4.3.1.description: Vesicular Zn 2+ uptake (into endosomal/lysosomal vesicles) permease, ZnT2. There are two isoforms due to alternative splicing, 35 kDa (plasma membrane localized) and 42 kDa (endosome/secretory compartment localized) ( Lopez and Kelleher, 2009 ).
2.A.4.3.1.name: Vesicular Zn 2+ uptake (into endosomal/lysosomal vesicles) permease, ZnT2.

2.A.4.3.10.description: CDF transporter, MTP1 of 640 aas and 6 TMSs. It transports zinc (Zn 2+ ) and cobalt (Co 2+ ) ( Ibuot et al. 2020 ).
2.A.4.3.10.name: CDF transporter, MTP1 of 640 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.3.12.description: Zinc transporter, Ttm-1, of 410 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. It promotes excretion of zinc from intestinal cells into the intestinal lumen in response to increased dietary zinc ( Roh et al. 2013 ). It is also involved in cadmium resistance, possibly by promoting its transport from cells ( Huffman et al. 2004 ). It is also involved in resistance to B. thuringiensis pore-forming…
2.A.4.3.12.name: Zinc transporter, Ttm-1, of 410 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.4.3.13.description: Zn 2+ , Fe 2+ and Co 2+ exporter, AitP, of 321 aas and 6 TMSs. The N 2 -fixing bacteria, Sinorhizobium meliloti , is a suitable model to determine the roles of Co 2+ -transporting Co-eCDF in Fe 2+ homeostasis because it has a putative member of this subfamily, AitP, and two specific Fe 2+ -export systems. An insertional mutant of AitP showed Co 2+ sensitivity and accumulation, Fe accumulation and…
2.A.4.3.13.name: Zn 2+ , Fe 2+ and Co 2+ exporter, AitP, of 321 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.3.2.description: Vesicular Zn 2+ uptake (into synaptic vesicles) permease, ZnT3 (SLC30A subfamily). ZnT-3 regulates presynaptic Erk1/2 signaling and hippocampus-dependent memory ( Sindreu et al. , 2011 ). Cryo-EM structures of the zinc transporters ZnT3 and ZnT4 provide insights into their transport mechanisms ( Ishida et al. 2024 ). SLC30A3 is a zinc transporter-related biomarker and a potential therapeutic…
2.A.4.3.2.name: Vesicular Zn 2+ uptake (into synaptic vesicles) permease, ZnT3 (SLC30A subfamily).

2.A.4.3.3.description: Mammary epithelia/brain Zn 2+ transporter ZnT4 (the cause of inherited zinc deficiency in the lethal milk (lm) syndrome of mice, due to a nonsense mutation at codon 297 (arg) in the ZnT4 gene) ( Huang and Gitschier, 1997 ). (see TC# 2.A.4.3.2 for more details revealed by cryoEM analyses) ( Ishida et al. 2024 ).
2.A.4.3.3.name: Mammary epithelia/brain Zn 2+ transporter ZnT4

2.A.4.3.4.description: Plant root and leaf vacuolar Zn 2+ transporter, ZAT-1 or MTP1 (metal tolerance protein 1) ( Desbrosses-Fonrouge et al ., 2005 ). Loss of the cytoplasmic histidine-rich loop, where 4 Zn 2+ (or Ni 2+ or Co 2+ ) bind, stimulates transport activity ( Kawachi et al ., 2008 ), presumably providing a feedback sensor of cytoplasmic Zn 2+ ( Tanaka et al. 2013 ). The barley orthologue has broader metal…
2.A.4.3.4.name: Plant root and leaf vacuolar Zn 2+ transporter, ZAT-1 or MTP1 (metal tolerance protein 1).

2.A.4.3.5.description: Homodimeric solute carrier family 30 (zinc transporter), member 8, ZnT8 or ZnT-8. An inherited R325W mutant gives aberant zinc transport in pancreatic beta cells ( Weijers 2010 ). It is chiefly expressed in pancreatic islet cells, where it mediates zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake into secretory granules. It plays a role in glucose tolerance ( Mitchell et al. 2016 ). ZnT8 is one of four human vesicular zinc…
2.A.4.3.5.name: Homodimeric solute carrier family 30 (zinc transporter), member 8, ZnT8 or ZnT-8.

2.A.4.3.8.description: Metal tolerance protein 4, MTP4, of 386 aas. Exports Zn 2+ and Cd 2+ ( Migocka et al. 2015 ). MTP1 transports the same two ions but is less restrictive with respect to the tissues in which the protein is synthesized.
2.A.4.3.8.name: Metal tolerance protein 4, MTP4, of 386 aas.

2.A.4.3.9.description: Co 2+ resistance protein, DmeF, of 382 aas and 6 TMSs. Co 2+ export appears to be its dominant physiological function, but it may also export other heavy metal ions such as Zn 2+ and Cd 2+ ( Munkelt et al. 2004 ).
2.A.4.3.9.name: Co 2+ resistance protein, DmeF, of 382 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.4.1.description: Heteromeric nuclear/ER Zn 2+ uptake permease, Msc2/Zrg17 ( Ellis et al ., 2005 ). Zrg17 is also called Meiotic sister-chromatid recombination-related protein or metal cation transporter Msc2p of 724 aas and 15 TMSs in a 7 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement. Only the last 6 TMSs are homologous to CDF transporters.
2.A.4.4.1.name: Heteromeric nuclear/ER Zn 2+ uptake permease, Msc2/Zrg17.

2.A.4.4.3.description: Golgi/secretory granule Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT5 or ZTL1 (ZnT5 forms heterooligomers with ZnT6) ( Ellis et al ., 2005 ; Ishihara et al ., 2006; Fukunaka et al. 2009 ) (Variant B catalyzes bidirectional transport ( Valentine et al ., 2007 ) )
2.A.4.4.3.name: Golgi/secretory granule Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT5 or ZTL1 (ZnT5 forms heterooligomers with ZnT6)

2.A.4.4.4.description: Golgi/secretory granule/endoplasmic reticulum Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi, the ER, or granules) permease, ZnT6. ZnT6 forms heterooligomers with ZnT5 ( Ellis et al ., 2005 ; Ishihara et al ., 2006 ; Fukunaka et al. 2009 ). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) primarily originates from the exocrine cells of the pancreas. SLC transporters, [more than 450 proteins divided into 65 families] are…
2.A.4.4.4.name: Golgi/secretory granule/endoplasmic reticulum Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi, the ER, or granules) permease, ZnT6.

2.A.4.4.5.description: Golgi/secretory granule Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT7 ( Ishihara et al ., 2006 ). Bui et al. 2023 presented the 2.2-3.1 Å-resolution cryo-EM structures of the human Zn 2+ /H + antiporter ZnT7 in Zn 2+ -bound and unbound forms. Cryo-EM analyses show that hZnT7 exists as a dimer via tight interactions in both the cytosolic and transmembrane (TM) domains of two protomers, each…
2.A.4.4.5.name: Golgi/secretory granule Zn 2+ uptake (into Golgi or granules) permease, ZnT7.

2.A.4.4.6.description: Metal tolerance protein C2 (AtMTPc2) (AtMTP5). Forms a large, active, heteromeric complex with MTP12 in the golgi and pumps Zn 2+ into this organelle ( Fujiwara et al. 2015 ). MTP12 has 798 aas and 14 TMSs. Its UniProt acc # is A0A0A8IL98. In Citrus sinensis , expression is induced by Zn 2+ in roots ( Fu et al. 2017 ).
2.A.4.4.6.name: Metal tolerance protein C2 (AtMTPc2) (AtMTP5).

2.A.4.4.7.description: Lead (Pb 2+ ) efflux transporter of 211 aas, PbtF ( Hložková et al. 2013 ).
2.A.4.4.7.name: Lead (Pb 2+ ) efflux transporter of 211 aas, PbtF.

2.A.4.5.1.description: Golgi/endomembrane Mn 2+ -specific CDF transporter (394 aas) ( Peiter et al ., 2007 ). A rice homologue, MTP8.1, has been characterized ( Chen et al. 2016 ).
2.A.4.5.1.name: Golgi/endomembrane Mn 2+ -specific CDF transporter (394 aas).

2.A.4.5.2.description: CDF2 transporter for Zn 2+ and Co 2+ but not Cd 2+ or Mn 2+ of 417 aas and 5 TMSs ( Sácký et al. 2016 ).
2.A.4.5.2.name: CDF2 transporter for Zn 2+ and Co 2+ but not Cd 2+ or Mn 2+ of 417 aas and 5 TMSs.

2.A.4.5.4.description: Metal tolerance protein 8, MTP8, of 411 aas and 6 TMSs. In Citrus sinensis , expression is induced by Mn 2+ in roots ( Fu et al. 2017 ). In A. thaliana , MPT8 determines the localization of manganese and iron in seeds ( Chu et al. 2017 ). The endodermal vacuole is the iron and manganese storage compartment in the A. thaliana embryo ( Roschzttardtz et al. 2009 ).
2.A.4.5.4.name: Metal tolerance protein 8, MTP8, of 411 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.5.6.description: CDF transporter, MTP3, of 458 aas and 7 TMSs. It transports Mn 2+ , Zn 2+ and Co 2+ ( Ibuot et al. 2020 ).
2.A.4.5.6.name: CDF transporter, MTP3, of 458 aas and 7 TMSs.

2.A.4.5.7.description: Mn 2+ transporting CDF porter, MTP4, of 538 aas and 6 TMSs.
2.A.4.5.7.name: Mn 2+ transporting CDF porter, MTP4, of 538 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.5.8.description: Metal tolerance protein 4 (MTP4) of 412 aas and 6 central TMSs It has dual functions in maintaining zinc homeostasis in tea plants ( Li et al. 2024 ).
2.A.4.5.8.name: Metal tolerance protein 4 (MTP4) of 412 aas and 6 central TMSs It has dual functions in maintaining zinc homeostasis in tea plants.

2.A.4.6.1.description: CDF transporter, ZnT9 (568 aas) ( Montanini et al ., 2007 ). Mutations cause autosomal recessive cerebro-renal syndrome and affect intracellular Zinc homeostasis ( Perez et al. 2017 ). 2.A.4.6.1.name: CDF transporter, ZnT9 (568 aas).

2.A.4.6.2.description: Metal tolerance protein C4, MTPC4 of 457 aas and 6 TMSs. It is involved in sequestration of excess metal ions, including Zn 2+ in the cytoplasm into vacuoles to maintain metal homeostasis.
2.A.4.6.2.name: Metal tolerance protein C4, MTPC4 of 457 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.7.1.description: Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ /Hg 2+ /Fe 2+ :H + antiporter, YiiP or FieF ( Chao and Fu, 2004b ; Grass et al ., 2005 ; Wei et al ., 2004 ; Wei and Fu, 2006 ). The structure (3.8 Å resolution) reveals a homodimer interconnected at the cytoplasmic domain through four Zn 2+ ions. A 6 TMS bundle features of a tetrahedral Zn 2+ binding site ( Lu and Fu, 2007 ). The gated water access to the transport site enables a…
2.A.4.7.1.name: Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ /Hg 2+ /Fe 2+ :H + antiporter, YiiP or FieF.

2.A.4.7.10.description: Cobalt/zinc resistance protein B, CzrB, of 291 aas and 6 TMSs. It has a cytosolic extramembranal C-terminus. This 92-residue fragment may function independently of the full-length integral membrane protein. X-ray analyses of this fragment to 2.2 A resolution with and 1.7 A without zinc ions have been solved. The former has at least two zinc ions bound per monomer ( Höfer et al. 2007 )…
2.A.4.7.10.name: Cobalt/zinc resistance protein B, CzrB, of 291 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.7.12.description: Mn 2+ uptake and efflux system of the rice node ( Li et al. 2026 ).
2.A.4.7.12.name: Mn 2+ uptake and efflux system of the rice node.

2.A.4.7.3.description: Magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamB. Forms a heterodimeric stable complex with MamM which stabilizes MamB. MamB also interacts with other proteins including the PDZ1 domain of MamE (Q6NE61). Both MamB and MamM are essential for magnetite biomineralization and are involved in several steps in magnetosome formation. MamM was used to probe the role of the hydrophilic C-terminal domain (CTD)…
2.A.4.7.3.name: Magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamB.

2.A.4.7.4.description: Putative magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamM. Forms a heterodimeric stable complex with MamB which it stabilizes. MamB (see TC# 2.A.4.7.3) also interacts with other proteins including the PDZ1 domain of MamE (Q6NE61). Both MamB and MamM are essential for magnetite biomineralization and are involved in several steps in magnetosome formation, but only MamB is essential for formation of…
2.A.4.7.4.name: Putative magnetosome membrane iron transporter, MamM.

2.A.4.7.5.description: Cd 2+ /Zn 2+ efflux pump, YiiP or FieF. A low resolution structure in the open configuration has been determined by cryoelectron microscopy ( Coudray et al. 2013 ).
2.A.4.7.5.name: Cd 2+ /Zn 2+ efflux pump, YiiP or FieF.

2.A.4.7.6.description: Dimeric Mn 2+ efflux transporter, MntE of 394 aas ( Rosch et al. 2009; Lisher et al. 2013 ; Jakubovics and Valentine 2009 ; Martin and Giedroc 2016).
2.A.4.7.6.name: Dimeric Mn 2+ efflux transporter, MntE of 394 aas.

2.A.4.7.7.description: Mn 2+ efflux pump, YiiP, probably a Mn 2+ :H + antiporter. Necessary for efficient nodulation of alfalfa plants ( Raimunda and Elso-Berberián 2014 )
2.A.4.7.7.name: Mn 2+ efflux pump, YiiP, probably a Mn 2+ :H + antiporter.

2.A.4.7.8.description: CDF protein, exporting Zn 2+ and Cd 2+ (323 aas). It lacks the C-terminal hydrophilic domain (CTD) common to many CDF homologues ( Kolaj-Robin et al. 2015 ).
2.A.4.7.8.name: CDF protein, exporting Zn 2+ and Cd 2+ (323 aas).

2.A.4.7.9.description: Ferrous iron detoxifying protein, FieF, of 337 aas and 6 TMSs. Also probably exports Zn 2+ , Co 2+ , Cd 2+ and Ni 2+ ( Munkelt et al. 2004 ).
2.A.4.7.9.name: Ferrous iron detoxifying protein, FieF, of 337 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.4.8.1.name: CDF Family homologue with MMT1 domain

2.A.4.8.3.description: Zn 2+ transporter, TMEM163 or Znt11, of 289 aas and 6 TMSs. It interacts with TrpML1 (TC# 1.A.5.3.1), but by itself, it can pump out Zn 2+ ( Sanchez et al. 2019 ). It may be involved in the human lipid storage disorder, mucolipidosis type IV (MLIV), caused by Zn 2+ overload ( Cuajungco et al. 2014 ). TMEM163 is found in synaptic vesicles where it is called SV31 ( Burré et al. 2007 ). It plays a…
2.A.4.8.3.name: Zn 2+ transporter, TMEM163 or Znt11, of 289 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.40.1.1.description: Uracil permease, UraA. The crystal structure of UraA with bound uracil at 2.8 Å resolution is available (PDB: 3QE7) ( Lu et al. , 2011 ). UraA has a novel structural fold, with 14 TMSs divided into two inverted repeats. A pair of antiparallel β-strands is located between TMS3 and TMS10 and has an important role in structural organization and substrate recognition. The structure is spatially…
2.A.40.1.1.name: Uracil permease, UraA.

2.A.40.1.2.description: High affinity uracil permease ( Martinussen et al. 2001 ).
2.A.40.1.2.name: High affinity uracil permease.

2.A.40.1.3.description: P yrimidine transporter of broad specificity , RutG of 442 aas and 14 TMSs; transports both uracil and thymine with high affinity as well as, xanthine with low efficiency ( Loh et al. , 2006 ; Kim et al. 2010 ; Botou et al. 2018 ).
2.A.40.1.3.name: P yrimidine transporter of broad specificity , RutG of 442 aas and 14 TMSs; transports both uracil and thymine with high affinity as well as…

2.A.40.3.2.description: Uric acid permease of 449 aas and 13 TMSs, PucJ. May function together with PucK (TC# 2.A.40.3.4) ( Schultz et al. 2001 ).
2.A.40.3.2.name: Uric acid permease of 449 aas and 13 TMSs, PucJ.

2.A.40.3.3.description: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU. YgfU exhibits low affinity (0.5 mM) but high capacity for urate and very poor activity for xanthine. Essential residues were identified. Coversion of Thr-100 to ala resulted in efficient xanthine transport ( Papakostas and Frillingos 2012 ).
2.A.40.3.3.name: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU.

2.A.40.3.4.description: Uric acid uptake porter of 430 aas and 13 TMSs, PucK. May function together with PucJ (TC# 2.A.40.3.2) ( Schultz et al. 2001 ).
2.A.40.3.4.name: Uric acid uptake porter of 430 aas and 13 TMSs, PucK.

2.A.40.4.1.description: High affinity uric acid-xanthine permease, UapA. Functionaly critical residues in transmembrane segments 1 and 3 have been identified ( Amillis et al. , 2011 ). The substrate recognition and transport pathway have been proposed ( Kosti et al. , 2012; Kosti et al. 2010 ). UapA oligomerization is essential for membrane trafficking and turnover and is a common theme in fungi and mammalian cells (…
2.A.40.4.1.name: High affinity uric acid-xanthine permease, UapA.

2.A.40.4.2.description: The putative xanthine permease, YicE ( Karatza and Frillingos, 2005 )
2.A.40.4.2.name: The putative xanthine permease, YicE

2.A.40.4.3.description: The YgfO (XanQ) purine (xanthine) transporter. Residues involved in substrate binding have been identified ( Georgopoulou et al. , 2010 ). TMS3 functions in substrate recognition ( Karena and Frillingos, 2011 ). Many more essential residues have more recently been identified ( Karena et al. 2015 ). An "ancestral" homolog (AncXanQ) has been constructed and proved to have broader specificity…
2.A.40.4.3.name: The YgfO (XanQ) purine (xanthine) transporter.

2.A.40.4.4.description: Purine (uric acid and xanthine) permease, UapC. Present in many Ascomycetes ( Krypotou and Diallinas 2014 ). Drought is an important abiotic stress that constrains the quality and quantity of tea plants. The green leaf volatiles, Z-3-hexenyl acetate (Z-3-HAC), play an essential role in stress responses ( Wang et al. 2023 ).
2.A.40.4.4.name: Purine (uric acid and xanthine) permease, UapC.

2.A.40.4.6.description: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine. It is of 463 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs in a 5 + 3 or 4 +1 + 4 TMS arrangement ( Tatsaki et al. 2021 ).
2.A.40.4.6.name: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine.

2.A.40.5.1.description: Putative purine permease, YbbY. The ybbY gene is in an operon involved with allantoin metabolism, and is flanked by allB , encoding allantoinase, and the glxK gene, encoding glycerate kinase II. Downstream of glxK is YlbA, encoding S-uridoglycine aminohydrolase, the second enzyme involved in allantoin degradation ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).
2.A.40.5.1.name: Putative purine permease, YbbY.

2.A.40.6.1.name: L -ascorbate:Na + symporter, SVCT1..

2.A.40.6.2.name: Ca 2+ /Mg 2+ -dependent L -ascorbate:Na + symporter, SVCT2; Na + :ascorbate = 2:1; binding order: Na + , ascorbate, Na +

2.A.40.6.4.description: solute carrier family 23 (nucleobase transporters), member 3, SVCT3 or SLC23A3. Function not certain as of 1/2013 ( Bürzle et al. 2013 ).
2.A.40.6.4.name: solute carrier family 23 (nucleobase transporters), member 3, SVCT3 or SLC23A3.

2.A.40.6.5.description: Solute carrier family 23 member 1 (Na + /L-ascorbic acid transporter 1; Sodium-dependent vitamin C transporter 1) (hSVCT1; Yolk sac permease-like molecule 3) ( Bürzle et al. 2013 ). Members of the SLC23 family have the UraA fold ( Ferrada and Superti-Furga 2022 ). Gut microbiota remodeling mediates the therapeutic effects of a plant-based medicine on DSS-induced ulcerative colitis in mice via the…
2.A.40.6.5.name: Solute carrier family 23 member 1 (Na + /L-ascorbic acid transporter 1; Sodium-dependent vitamin C transporter 1)

2.A.40.6.7.description: Solute carrier family 23 member 2-like protein (SLC23.A.4) of 614 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs, SNBT1. 2.A.47.1.3.description: The brush boarder intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na -dependent, low affinity (0.1-4.0mM), dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate, malate, α-ketoglutarate, oxaloacetate, L- and D-glutamate, and citrate):H cotransporter, NaDC-1 or SDCT1. Functions in acid regulation. An acidic pH stimullates citrate uptake; acid stimulation is mediated by endothelin-1 (ET-1) and its receptor ( Liu et al. 2010 ).
2.A.47.1.3.name: The brush boarder intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na -dependent, low affinity (0.1-4.0mM), dicarboxylate

2.A.47.1.4.description: The basolateral intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na + -dependent high affinity (2-50µM) dicarboxylate:(Na + ) 3 cotransporter (NaDC-3) (substrate range similar to that of NDC-1 except that tricarboxylates are transported with very low affinity). 2.A.47.1.4.name: The basolateral intestinal and renal electrogenic, Na + -dependent high affinity (2-50µM) dicarboxylate:(Na + ) 3 cotransporter (NaDC-3)

2.A.47.1.6.name: The tonoplast dicarboxylate (malate) transporter, AtDCT.

2.A.47.1.8.name: High affinity dicarboxylate:Na + symporter, NaDC2 (INDY2) (relative affinities: fumarate > malate > α-ketoglutarate > maleate > succinate > lactate)

Na + :citrate = 3-4:1 ( Wada et al ., 2006 ).Targeting longevity gene SLC13A5 provides a novel approach to preventing age-related bone fragility and osteoporosis ( Zahn et al. 2023 ). 2.A.47.1.9.name: Na + -coupled citrate transporter (NaCT) (K m =20 μM) (also may transport dicarboxylates and other tricarboxylates with lower affinity).

2.A.47.2.1.description: Inorganic phosphate transporter, Pho87 of 923 aas and 12 TMSs. Also transports selenite ( Lazard et al., 2010 ).
2.A.47.2.1.name: Inorganic phosphate transporter, Pho87 of 923 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.47.2.2.description: Vacuolar low affinity phosphate transporter, Pho91 ( Estrella et al ., 2008 ) with 12 C-terminal TMSs and an N-terminal 360 hydrophilic region. Also transports selenite ( Lazard et al., 2010 ). Pyrophosphate stimulates the phosphate - sodium symporter of Trypanosoma brucei (TC# 2.A.47.2.4) acidocalcisomes and Saccharomyces cerevisiae vacuoles (this protein) ( Potapenko et al. 2019 ).
2.A.47.2.2.name: Vacuolar low affinity phosphate transporter, Pho91 with 12 C-terminal TMSs and an N-terminal 360 hydrophilic region.

2.A.47.2.3.description: Low affinity phosphate transporters (881aas). Also transports selenite ( Lazard et al., 2010 ).
2.A.47.2.3.name: Low affinity phosphate transporters (881aas).

2.A.47.2.4.description: Contractile vacuole phosphate:Na + symporter of 727 aas and 12 TMSs, Pho91 (Pho90; Pho87). Has an N-terminal SPX domain and a C-terminal anion permease domain. Plays an indirect role in pyrophosphate and oligophosphate synthesis ( Jimenez and Docampo 2015 ). Pyrophosphate stimulates the phosphate - sodium symporter of Trypanosoma brucei acidocalcisomes and Saccharomyces cerevisiae vacuoles (…
2.A.47.2.4.name: Contractile vacuole phosphate:Na + symporter of 727 aas and 12 TMSs, Pho91 (Pho90; Pho87).

2.A.47.3.2.description: Citrate:succinate antiporter ( Pos et al. 1998 ). Binds and presumably regulates the heterodimeric citrate lyase, CitE/CitF which converts citrate to succinate and acetate ( Quentmeier et al. 1987 ). These proteins form a metabolon which together catalyze citrate fermentation under anaerobic conditions.
2.A.47.3.2.name: Citrate:succinate antiporter.

2.A.47.3.3.description: L-tartrate:succinate antiporter, TtdT (YgjE). (also takes up meso and L-tartrate and succinate; does not transport D-tartrate) ( Kim and Unden, 2007 ). It is induced in the presence of L- or meso tartrate under anaerobic conditions in the presence of TtdR ( Kim et al. 2009 ).
2.A.47.3.3.name: L-tartrate:succinate antiporter, TtdT (YgjE). (also takes up meso and L-tartrate and succinate; does not transport D-tartrate).

2.A.47.3.4.description: The pmf-dependent citrate uptake system, Cit1 ( Urbany and Neuhaus, 2008 )
2.A.47.3.4.name: The pmf-dependent citrate uptake system, Cit1

2.A.47.4.2.description: Antimonite resistance protein (inducible by both arsenite and antimonite).

2.A.47.4.6.name: The oxyanion (molybdate, sulfate, tungstate and vanidate) permease PerO.

2.A.47.5.2.name: Dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate, malate) transporter, vcINDY.

2.A.47.5.3.description: The Na + -dependent C4-dicarboxylate (fumarate, succinate) uptake transporter, SdcA of 425 aas and 15 TMSs ( Rhie et al. 2014 ).
2.A.47.5.3.name: The Na + -dependent C4-dicarboxylate (fumarate, succinate) uptake transporter, SdcA of 425 aas and 15 TMSs.

2.A.49.1.10.description: Auxin efflux carrier, PIN1a (REH1) of 595 aas and 10 TMSs, 5 at the N-terminus and 5 at the C-terminus. The LRR receptor-like kinase OsXIAO regulates rice root growth by interacting with the auxin transporter OsPIN1a ( Ding et al. 2026 ).
2.A.49.1.10.name: Auxin efflux carrier, PIN1a (REH1) of 595 aas and 10 TMSs, 5 at the N-terminus and 5 at the C-terminus.

2.A.49.1.2.description: The vascular wilt fungal CLC-type voltage-gated chloride channel, Clc1 (influences disease progression and stress responses) ( Canero and Roncero, 2008 ).
2.A.49.1.2.name: The vascular wilt fungal CLC-type voltage-gated chloride channel, Clc1 (influences disease progression and stress responses).

2.A.49.1.3.name: The voltage-gated chloride channel, CLC-A (required for capsule and laccase expression)

2.A.49.1.4.description: Chloride channel protein of 2075 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.49.1.4.name: Chloride channel protein of 2075 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.49.2.1.description: Voltage and (possibly) ATP-gated Cl - channel, ClC-1 or CLCN1 ( Bennetts et al ., 2005 ; Zifarelli and Pusch, 2008 ). It may also transport other anions such as thiocyanate, perchlorate, bromide, nitrate, chlorate and iodide. When mutant, it causes dominant and recessive myotonia. Myotonia congenita is a genetic disease characterized by impaired muscle relaxation after forceful contraction (…
2.A.49.2.1.name: Voltage and (possibly) ATP-gated Cl - channel, ClC-1 or CLCN1.

2.A.49.2.10.description: Chloride transporter/chloride channel (ClC) family protein of 1604 aas ( Docampo et al. 2013 ).
2.A.49.2.10.name: Chloride transporter/chloride channel (ClC) family protein of 1604 aas.

2.A.49.2.11.description: The voltage-gated torpedo chloride channel, CLC-0, of 810 aas. This channel is thought to ensure the high conductance of the non-innervated membrane of the electrocyte necessary for efficient current generation caused by sodium influx through the acetylcholine receptor at the innervated membrane. ClC-0 is a homodimer with separate pores in each subunit. Each protopore can be opened and closed…
2.A.49.2.11.name: The voltage-gated torpedo chloride channel, CLC-0, of 810 aas.

2.A.49.2.12.description: Chloride (bromide; iodide) channel-2, CLC-2, CLC2, CLCN2; 94% identical to the rat orthologue, 2.A.49.2.6. Hyperpolarization activates CLC-2 mainly by driving intracellular anions into the channel pores. Protonation by extracellular H + plays a minor role in dislodging the glutamate gate ( De Jesús-Pérez et al. 2016 ). The absence of ClC-2 results in less differentiated colonic crypts and…
2.A.49.2.12.name: Chloride (bromide; iodide) channel-2, CLC-2, CLC2, CLCN2; 94% identical to the rat orthologue, 2.A.49.2.6.

2.A.49.2.13.description: Clh-3; Clc-3, Clh3, Clc3 of 1001 aas and 11 TMSs. Isoform a: Voltage-gated chloride channel ( Rutledge et al. 2002 ; Denton et al. 2005 ). Insensitive to depolarizing voltages; requires low voltages for activation; insensitive to chloride levels but has a mild sensitivity to low pH. Channel gating properties are conferred by the cytoplasmic C-terminus ( He et al. 2006 ). Plays a role in egg…
2.A.49.2.13.name: Clh-3; Clc-3, Clh3, Clc3 of 1001 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.49.2.15.description: Chloride channel protein, CLCNKB or ClC-Kb or CLCKB of 687 aas and 10 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. Voltage-gated chloride channel. Chloride channels have several functions including the regulation of cell volume; membrane potential stabilization, signal transduction and transepithelial transport. May be important in urinary concentrating mechanisms ( Estévez et al. 2001 ). CLCNKB…
2.A.49.2.15.name: Chloride channel protein, CLCNKB or ClC-Kb or CLCKB of 687 aas and 10 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.49.2.16.description: H + /Cl - exchange transporter 5, ClC-5 (CLCN5; CLCK2) of 816 aas and 12 TMSs in a 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. It functions as antiport system and exchanges chloride ions against protons ( Neagoe et al. 2010 ). ClC-5 is expressed in the apical membrane of cyst epithelia and is a likely candidate mediating Cl - secretion into the kidney cyst lumen in the tuberous sclerosis complex…
2.A.49.2.16.name: H + /Cl - exchange transporter 5, ClC-5 (CLCN5; CLCK2) of 816 aas and 12 TMSs in a 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.49.2.17.description: ClC-c of 893 aas and 11 TMSs. Drosophila ClC-c is a homolog of human CLC-5 and a new model for Dent Disease type 1 ( Reynolds et al. 2024 ).
2.A.49.2.17.name: ClC-c of 893 aas and 11 TMSs.

2.A.49.2.2.description: Intracellular (endosomal) outward rectifying kidney Cl - :H (2:1) antiporter ClC5; CLC-5; CLCN5 (nitrate > Cl - = Br - > I - > acetate > gluconate) ( Picollo and Pusch, 2005 ; Scheel et al ., 2005 ); responsible for Dent''s disease in humans, an X-linked disorder characterized by low molecular weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, and nephrolithiasis ( Stechman et al ., 2007 ; Zifarelli and Pusch…

2.A.49.2.3.description: The hepatocyte canalicular chloride channel/carrier, CLC-3 or CLCN3 of 818 aas with 11 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 +2 + 2 TMS arrangement (I - > Br - > Cl - ); outward rectifying; inactivated at positive voltages ( Shimada et al ., 2000 ). 2.A.49.2.3.name: The hepatocyte canalicular chloride channel/carrier, CLC-3 or CLCN3 of 818 aas with 11 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 +2 + 2 TMS arrangement

2.A.49.2.4.description: The kidney medulla voltage-gated dimeric chloride channel, ClC-K1 or CLCNKA. Transports Br - , I - and NO 3 - as well as Cl - . Regulated by dehydration; functions in the regulation of cell volume, membrane potential stabilization, signal transduction and transepithelial transport. Possibly required for urinary concentration in the kidney ( Uchida et al ., 1993 ). The human orthologue when…
2.A.49.2.4.name: The kidney medulla voltage-gated dimeric chloride channel, ClC-K1 or CLCNKA.

2.A.49.2.5.description: The kidney thick ascending limb of Henle's loop and collecting duct chloride channel/carrier, ClC-K2 (Br - > I - > Cl - >> cyclamate) ( Adachi et al ., 1994 ). Regulated by the accessory subunit, Barttin ( Wojciechowski et al. 2015 ).
2.A.49.2.5.name: The kidney thick ascending limb of Henle's loop and collecting duct chloride channel/carrier, ClC-K2 (Br - > I - > Cl - >> cyclamate).

2.A.49.2.6.description: The ClC-2 or CLCN2 chloride channel is expressed in many tissues (Cl - ≥ Br - > I - ) ( Thiemann et al ., 1992 ). Regulated in the retina by Cereblon (Q96SW2) ( Hohberger and Enz, 2009 ). A toxin, GaTx2, is a potent and specific inhibitor of ClC-2, binding with a Ki of 20pM ( Thompson et al. , 2009 ). ClC-2 channels constitute part of the background conductance and assist chloride extrusion (…
2.A.49.2.6.name: The ClC-2 or CLCN2 chloride channel is expressed in many tissues (Cl - ≥ Br - > I - ).

2.A.49.2.7.description: The ClC-A of the trophozoite plasma membrane (Cl - >Br - >I - >F - >NO 3 - ). Functions as an ion channel, not a Cl:H + antiporter; regulates cell pH and volume ( Salas-Casas et al ., 2006 )
2.A.49.2.7.name: The ClC-A of the trophozoite plasma membrane (Cl - >Br - >I - >F - >NO 3 - ).

2.A.49.2.8.description: ClC-4 or CLCN4 of760 aas with 11 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. It catalyzes 2 Cl - :H + exchange, but NO 3 - uniport ( Bergsdorf et al. , 2009 ). SCN - uncouples Cl - from H + transport so anions are transported with high unitary transport rates. Voltage then influences transport as is observed for the gating of ion channels ( Orhan et al. , 2011 ). Also transports bromide and…
2.A.49.2.8.name: ClC-4 or CLCN4 of760 aas with 11 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.49.2.9.description: The CIC carrier (stoichiometry H + :Cl - = 2:1). 3D structure known to 3.5 Å resolution (PDB# 3ORG; Feng et al., 2010 ).
2.A.49.2.9.name: The CIC carrier (stoichiometry H + :Cl - = 2:1).

2.A.49.3.1.description: NO 3 - :H + (or less efficiently, Cl - :H + ) antiporter, ClC-A or CLCa ( De Angeli et al. , 2006 ; Bergsdorf et al. , 2009 ). Responsible for nitrate uptake into vacuoles ( Zifarelli and Pusch, 2009b ). It is up-regulated under salt stress conditions ( Yang et al. 2018 ) and may play a role in nitrate and Cd 2+ resistance ( Liao et al. 2019 ). The cryoEM structure has been solved at 2.8 Å…
2.A.49.3.1.name: NO 3 - :H + (or less efficiently, Cl - :H + ) antiporter, ClC-A or CLCa.

2.A.49.3.2.description: Mitochondrial inner membrane anion channel (IMAC). Fatty acids induce chloride permeation in rat liver mitochondria probably by activation of the inner membrane anion channel (IMAC) ( Schönfeld et al. 2004 ).
2.A.49.3.2.name: Mitochondrial inner membrane anion channel (IMAC).

2.A.49.3.3.description: CLC-7, CLC7 or Clcn7 Cl - :H + antiporter; provides the primary Cl - permeation pathway in the lysosome ( Graves et al ., 2008 ). Cl - provides the counter ion for acidification of the lysosomal lumen via the V-type ATPase ( Mindell, 2012 ). It is a slowly voltage-gated 2Cl - /1H + -exchanger and requires Ostm1 for transport activity ( Leisle et al. , 2011 ). Common gating (involving both of the…
2.A.49.3.3.name: CLC-7, CLC7 or Clcn7 Cl - :H + antiporter; provides the primary Cl - permeation pathway in the lysosome.

2.A.49.3.4.description: CLC-6 or CLCN6, Cl - :H + late endosomal/lysosomal antiporter (43% identical to CLC-7) and 99% identical to the human ortholog (P51797). Cl - > I - ; mutating the gating glutamate yielded ohmic anion conductance ( Neagoe et al. , 2010 ). A recurrent gain-of-function mutation in CLCN6, encoding the ClC-6 Cl - /H + -exchanger, causes early-onset neurodegeneration ( Polovitskaya et al. 2020 ). Loss…
2.A.49.3.4.name: CLC-6 or CLCN6, Cl - :H + late endosomal/lysosomal antiporter (43% identical to CLC-7) and 99% identical to the human ortholog (P51797).

2.A.49.3.5.description: Anion transporter with specificity for nitrate (NO 3 - ) and chloride (Cl - ), CLCa1, of 811 aas and probably 12 TMSs in a 4 + 4 + 4 TMS arrangement ( Nedelyaeva et al. 2019 ). It is expressed in the roots, and induced with nitrate depletion.
2.A.49.3.5.name: Anion transporter with specificity for nitrate (NO 3 - ) and chloride (Cl - ), CLCa1, of 811 aas and probably 12 TMSs in a 4 + 4 + 4 TMS arrangement.

2.A.49.5.1.description: Cl - :H + (2:1) antiporter, EriC or ClcA (ClC-ecl) ( Accardi and Miller, 2004 ). The x-ray structure has been determined (PDB 1OTS) Dutzler et al ., 2002 , 2003 ). The exchange mechanism involves a conformational cycle of alternating exposure of Cl - and H + binding sites of both ClC pores to the two sides of the membrane ( Miloshevsky et al. , 2010 ). Specific aspects of these conformational…
2.A.49.5.1.name: Cl - :H + (2:1) antiporter, EriC or ClcA (ClC-ecl).

2.A.49.5.2.description: Slow CLC Cl - :H + antiporter. 3-d structures known at 3.1 Å resolution (3Q17A) (turnover rate: 20/sec; Cl - :H + stoichiometry = 2:1). The turnover rate of the E. coli EriC is ~2000/sec. ( Jayaram et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.49.5.2.name: Slow CLC Cl - :H + antiporter.

2.A.49.5.4.name: Voltage-gated ClC-type Cl - channel, ClcB.

2.A.49.5.5.description: H + /Cl - antiporter, ClcA (stoichiometry 1:2) ( Phillips et al. 2012 ).

2.A.49.6.2.name: Voltage-gated Cl - channel, ClC chloride channel core, CCC

2.A.49.6.3.description: Chloride channel protein CLC-e (AtCLC-e) (CBS domain-containing protein CBSCLC3). Present in the thylacoid membrane of the chloroplast. Initially proposed to function in photosynthesis, and later in nitrate assimilation ( Herdean et al. 2016 ).
2.A.49.6.3.name: Chloride channel protein CLC-e (AtCLC-e) (CBS domain-containing protein CBSCLC3).

2.A.49.6.4.name: Putative chloride:H + antiporte r, voltage gated, of 792 aas and 15 TMSs with an N-terminal 4 TMS domain of unknown function found only in a few…

2.A.49.6.5.description: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 481 aas and 10 - 13 TMSs. This protein was probably incorrectly assigned the function as the membrane constituent of an ABC Zn 2+ uptake transporter ( Mandal et al. 2019 ). However, this is unlikely; it is probably a Cl- transporter in agreement with its assignment to TC family 2.A.49.
2.A.49.6.5.name: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 481 aas and 10 - 13 TMSs.

2.A.49.9.1.name: Fluoride:proton antiporter of 459 aas and 10 TMSs, CLCF, with high selectivity for fluoride over chloride.

2.A.49.9.2.name: Fluoride:proton antiporter, CLCF, of 426 aas and 10 TMSs, with specificity for fluoride over other anions.

2.A.49.9.3.name: Fluoride:proton antiporter of 406 aas and 10 TMSs, CLCF.

2.A.49.9.4.description: Putative fluoride:proton antiporter of 403 aas and 10 TMSs ( Brammer et al. 2014 ).
2.A.49.9.4.name: Putative fluoride:proton antiporter of 403 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.49.9.5.description: Anion transporter, EriC, of 452 aas and 10 TMSs. Transports Cl- and F-, and probably other anions ( Baker et al. 2012 ).
2.A.49.9.5.name: Anion transporter, EriC, of 452 aas and 10 TMSs.

2.A.5.1.1.description: High affinity zinc-regulated zinc uptake transporter, Zrt1 of 376 aas and 8 TMSs. May be a transceptor with both transport and receptor (signal transduction) functions ( Diallinas 2017; Schothorst et al. 2017 ). Activated at the transcriptional level by Yap1 and Ace1 ( Gomes et al. 2005 ). Zrt1 may also transport, or influence the uptake of Cd 2+ ( Gomes et al. 2005 ).
2.A.5.1.1.name: High affinity zinc-regulated zinc uptake transporter, Zrt1 of 376 aas and 8 TMSs.

2.A.5.1.11.description: Ferrous iron (Fe 2+ ) transporting ZIP family member, LIT1, required for intracellular growth and virulence ( Huynh et al. 2006 ). Also transports other metal ions less efficiently. Residues involved in targetting and activity have been identified including His108, 283 and 309 ( Jacques et al. 2010 ).
2.A.5.1.11.name: Ferrous iron (Fe 2+ ) transporting ZIP family member, LIT1, required for intracellular growth and virulence.

2.A.5.1.12.description: Root iron transporter IRT1 of 364 aas and 9 TMSs. Has an uncleaved signal peptide that targets the protein to the endoplasmic reticulum for transport to the plasma membrane ( Zhang et al. 2014 ).
2.A.5.1.12.name: Root iron transporter IRT1 of 364 aas and 9 TMSs.

2.A.5.1.13.description: Ferrous iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake transporter of 347 aas and 9 TMSs. Transports iron and possibly Cd 2+ in this hyperaccumulating plant. Induced by iron deficiency and cadmium excess ( Plaza et al. 2007 ).
2.A.5.1.13.name: Ferrous iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake transporter of 347 aas and 9 TMSs.

2.A.5.1.14.description: Low affinity zinc-regulated zinc uptake transporter, Zrt2 of 422 aas and 7 TMSs. Active in zinc-replete cells and is time-, temperature- and concentration-dependent. It prefers zinc over other metals as its substrate ( Zhao and Eide 1996 ).

Expressed only in the symbiosome membrane of rhizobial nodules; transports sulfate from the plant cell cytoplasm to the intracellular rhizobia, where the nutrient is essential for protein and cofactor synthesis, including nitrogenase biosynthesis ( Krusell et al. 2005 ).
2.A.53.1.12.name: Symbiotic sulfate transporter-1, SST1 of 645 aas.

It is a H + /sulfate cotransporter that may play a role in the regulation of sulfate assimilation. The structure of AtSULTR4;1, in complex with SO 4 2- at an overall resolution of 2.8 Å has been determined ( Wang et al. 2021 ). AtSULTR4;1 forms a homodimer and has a structural fold typical of the SLC26 family…
2.A.53.1.14.name: Sulfate transporter 4:1, chloroplastic, SULTR4;1, MSH12.1, of 685 aas and 13 - 15 TMSs.

2.A.53.1.15.description: Sulfate transporter 3.1 of 658 aas and 14 putative TMSs in a probable 6 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement. 2.A.53.1.15.name: Sulfate transporter 3.1 of 658 aas and 14 putative TMSs in a probable 6 + 2 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.53.1.16.description: Probabe phosphate transporter, SPDT, of 670 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs. The transporter gene (Os06g0143700) product probably transports phosphate, possibly instead of or in addition to sulfate ( Yamaji et al. 2017 ). T he expression of SPDT in the shoot basal region was highly upregulated by phosphate-deficiency, but not by sulfate-deficiency. Fulvic acid increase the expression of several phosphate…
2.A.53.1.16.name: Probabe phosphate transporter, SPDT, of 670 aas and 12 - 16 TMSs.

2.A.53.1.17.description: Rice sulfur/selenium uptake porter, OsSULTR1;1, of 662 aas and 12 probable TMSs. Differential expression of sulfate transporters under selenium supply identifies OsSULTR1;1 as a candidate for nutritional enhancement in super basmati rice ( Aslam et al. 2026 ).
2.A.53.1.17.name: Rice sulfur/selenium uptake porter, OsSULTR1;1, of 662 aas and 12 probable TMSs.

2.A.53.1.3.name: The molybdate (high affinity)/Sulfate (lower affinity) transporter, ShsT1.

2.A.53.1.6.name: The sulfate transporter, Sultr1.2 with C-terminal STAS domain that is required both for activity and biogenesis/stability.

2.A.53.1.7.name: High affinity sulfate transporter, Sultr1.1 regulated differently from Sultr1.2 (2.A.53.1.6)

2.A.53.1.9.name: Slc26a11 Cl - /oxalate or sulfate (but not bicarbonate) exchanger.

It catalyzes electroneutral SO 4 - , OH - and Cl - exchange, regulated by extracellular Cl - ( Ohana et al. , 2011 ). Biji et al. 2022 have expanded the spectrum of SLC26A2-related lethal…
2.A.53.2.1.name: Sulfate/anion transporter (diastrophic dysplasia protein) (SLC26A2).

Differential contributions and interactions of SLC26A9 with CFTR to Cl - conductance in polarized and non-polarized epithelial cells have been demonstrated ( Ousingsawat et al. , 2012 ). Slc26a9 (-/-) mice have reduced gastric acid secretion ( Chen et al. , 2012 ). Polymorphisms in the human orthologue lead to…
2.A.53.2.10.name: The anion exchanger, channel and Na + -transporter, SLC26a9.

2.A.53.2.11.description: Guinea pig Slc26a3 electroneutral Cl - /HCO 3 - exchanger (does not transport oxalate or sulfate). ( Stewart et al. , 2011 ).
2.A.53.2.11.name: Guinea pig Slc26a3 electroneutral Cl - /HCO 3 - exchanger (does not transport oxalate or sulfate)..

2.A.53.2.12.name: Slc26a6 Cl - /oxalate, sulfate or bicarbonate exchanger.

2.A.53.2.14.description: Solute exchange carrier family 26, member 8, SLC26A8 or Testis anion transporter 1 (Tat1), of 970 aas and possibly 17 TMSs in a 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 3 TMS arrangement. It acts as a DIDS-sensitive anion exchanger mediating chloride, sulfate and oxalate transport. May fulfill critical anion exchange functions in male germ line during meiosis and hence may play a role in spermatogenesis. It may be…
2.A.53.2.14.name: Solute exchange carrier family 26, member 8, SLC26A8 or Testis anion transporter 1 (Tat1), of 970 aas and possibly 17 TMSs in a 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 3 TMS…

2.A.53.2.15.description: Solute carrier family 26 member 9 (Anion transporter/exchanger protein 9; AE9). May play a role in chronic inflammatory airway diseases ( Sala-Rabanal et al. 2015 ). The Cl - -transporting proteins CFTR (TC# 3.A.1.202.1), SLC26A9, and anoctamin (ANO1; ANO6) (see TC family 1.A.17) all participate in the pathogenic process and clinical outcomes of airway and renal diseases ( Kunzelmann et al. 2023…
2.A.53.2.15.name: Solute carrier family 26 member 9 (Anion transporter/exchanger protein 9; AE9).

2.A.53.2.16.description: Sulfate anion transporter 1 (SAT-1 or SAT1) (Solute carrier family 26 member 1); anion exchanger. Transports chloride , sulfate, bicarbonate and oxalate ( Regeer et al. 2003; Lee et al. 2003 ). The mouse and rat orthologues have the same specificities and functions. Loss in mice is associated with hyperoxalurea and calcium oxalate kidney stones, and specific mutations when heterozygous in humans…
2.A.53.2.16.name: Sulfate anion transporter 1 (SAT-1 or SAT1) (Solute carrier family 26 member 1); anion exchanger.

2.A.53.2.17.description: Pendrin (Sodium-independent chloride/iodide/bicarbonate transporter) (Solute carrier family 26 member 4, Slc26a4; PDS). Involved in ion homeostasis of the endolymph of the inner ear. Missense mutations cause sensorineuronal hearing loss, but salicylate (aspirin) restored transport function by allowing transport from cytosolic sites to the plasma membrane ( Ishihara et al. 2010 ). May also…
2.A.53.2.17.name: Pendrin (Sodium-independent chloride/iodide/bicarbonate transporter) (Solute carrier family 26 member 4, Slc26a4; PDS).

2.A.53.2.18.description: Chloride anion exchanger (Down-regulated in adenoma) (Protein DRA) (Solute carrier family 26 member 3). The intracellular pH regulates ion exchange ( Hayashi et al. 2009 ). Reduced functional expression of NHE3, and DRA contribute to Cl - and Na + stool loss in microvillus inclusion disease (MVID) diarrhea ( Kravtsov et al. 2016 ). Mutations cause Congenital Chloride Diarrhea (CCD), an autosomal…
2.A.53.2.18.name: Chloride anion exchanger (Down-regulated in adenoma) (Protein DRA) (Solute carrier family 26 member 3).

2.A.53.2.19.description: Prestin (Solute carrier family 26 member 5). The motor protein responsible for the somatic electromotility of cochlear outer hair cells (OHC); essential for normal hearing sensitivity and frequency selectivity in mammals. Prestin transports a wide variety of monovalent and divalent anions. Many SulP transporters have C-terminal hydrophilic STAS domains that are essential for plasma membrane…
2.A.53.2.19.name: Prestin (Solute carrier family 26 member 5).

2.A.53.2.3.description: Intestinal down-regulated in adenoma (DRA) protein; HCO 3 - /Cl - antiporter, SLC26a3 (responsible for congenital chloride-losing diarrhea in humans) ( Schweinfest et al ., 2006 ). DRA has 12 putative TMSs and a C-terminal STAS domain required for function and activation of CFTR by DRA ( Dorwart et al ., 2008 ). Catalyzes 2Cl - /1HCO 3 - antiport, Cl - /OH - exchange and sulfate transport (…
2.A.53.2.3.name: Intestinal down-regulated in adenoma (DRA) protein; HCO 3 - /Cl - antiporter, SLC26a3 (responsible for congenital chloride-losing diarrhea in humans).

2.A.53.2.4.description: Pendrin (Pendred) syndrome (hereditary deafness) anion transporter (Na + -independent). Anions transported: iodide (thyroid gland; apical membrane of follicular epithelium); bicarbonate (kidney; apical membrane of intercalated cells of the cortical collecting duct), chloride, formate, etc. Pendrin probably catalyzes uniport and anion/anion antiport (SLC26A4). It also regulates Na + absorption by…
2.A.53.2.4.name: Pendrin (Pendred) syndrome (hereditary deafness) anion transporter (Na + -independent).

2.A.53.2.5.description: Prestin, the outer hair cell voltage-sensitive motor protein (voltage sensitivity depends on intracellular Cl - and HCO 3 - which may bind to prestin). Prestin transports anions including formate and oxalate; transport and voltage-sensing capabilities are independent functions of the same protein ( Bai et al. , 2009 ). Prestin-mediated electromotility is a dual-step process: transport of anions…
2.A.53.2.5.name: Prestin, the outer hair cell voltage-sensitive motor protein

2.A.53.2.7.description: The human Slc26a6 anion exchanger (transports sulfate, formate, oxalate, chloride and bicarbonate in antiport with any one of these anions) ( Jiang et al ., 2002 ). However, Cl - and HSO 4 - are transported slowly; Cl - /HCO 3 - , Cl - /OH - and Cl - :oxalate exchange reactions are electroneutral ( Chernova et al ., 2005 ). (The oxalate nephrolithiasis gene; Clark et al ., 2008 ). Catalyzes 1Cl -…
2.A.53.2.7.name: The human Slc26a6 anion exchanger (transports sulfate, formate, oxalate, chloride and bicarbonate in antiport with any one of these anions).

2.A.53.2.8.description: The mouse Slc26a6 anion exchanger (same substrate specificity as its human orthologue (2.A.53.2.7)), but Cl - and HSO 4 - are transported rapidly. Moreover, although Cl - /HCO 3 - and Cl - /OH - exchange reactions are electroneutral, Cl - :oxalate exchange is electrogenic ( Chernova et al ., 2005 ). Also catalyzes Cl - :formate exchange ( Knauf et al. , 2001 ).
2.A.53.2.8.name: The mouse Slc26a6 anion exchanger (same substrate specificity as its human orthologue (2.A.53.2.7)), but Cl - and HSO 4 - are transported rapidly.

2.A.53.2.9.name: The electrogenic divalent anion: chloride exchanger (1:1 stoichiometry) (transports sulfate, chloride, and oxalate)

2.A.53.3.10.name: Vacuolar membrane protein, YGR125W, basic amino acid (arginine, etc.) transporter of 1036 aas and 10 - 13 TMSs.

2.A.53.3.11.name: Bicarbonate transporter, DauA (YchM).

2.A.53.3.12.description: A bicarbonate transporter fused to a carbonic anhydrase, Rv3273 ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).
2.A.53.3.12.name: A bicarbonate transporter fused to a carbonic anhydrase, Rv3273.

2.A.53.3.13.description: Fumarate (Na + -independent anion) transporter, SLC26dg of 499 aas and 14 TMSs. It has an N-terminal Sulfate-tra-GLY domain with a glycine motif of unknown function and a C-terminal STAS (sulfate transporter and antisigma factor antagonist) domain. 2.A.53.3.13.name: Fumarate (Na + -independent anion) transporter, SLC26dg of 499 aas and 14 TMSs.

2.A.53.4.2.name: Sulfate transporter, Rv1739c.

A n N-terminal di-leucine motif is critical for correct subcellular localisation of MOT2, and its activity is required for accumulation of molybdate in Arabidopsis seeds. It is involved in inter-organ translocation ( Gasber et al. 2011 ).
2.A.53.5.3.name: Molybdate transporter 2, MOT2, of 464 aas and 10 TMSs.

This system is believed to be required for one-carbon metabolism because serine is converted into glycine and formate in the mitochondrion. SFXN1, an integral inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) protein with an uneven number of transmembrane…
2.A.54.1.1.name: Mitochondrial serine (and possibly cystine and alanine) carrier, Sideroflexin-1 (SFXN1; SLC56A1), of 322 aas and probably 5 TMSs.

2.A.54.1.10.name: Sideroflexin-4 isoform X4 of 327 aas and 7 probable TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

It may form a complex with poly( rC )-binding protein-2, PCBP2 (335 aas and possibly 4 N-terminal TMSs; AAI07689.1) and TOM20 (145 aas and possibly 1 N-terminal TMS; NP_055580.1) ( Mi et al. 2024 ). 2.A.54.1.14.name: Sideroflexin 3 (SFXN3) with 308 aas and 4 putative C-terminal TMSs.

2.A.54.1.3.description: Sideroflexin-4 (Breast cancer resistance marker 1) or SFXN4 (SLC56A4) of 337 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 +2 + 2 TMS arrangement. It has been found mutated in mice with siderocytic anemia ( Zheng et al. 2003 ).
2.A.54.1.3.name: Sideroflexin-4 (Breast cancer resistance marker 1) or SFXN4 (SLC56A4) of 337 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 +2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.54.1.4.description: Probable mitochondrial transport protein FSF1 (Fungal sideroflexin-1)
2.A.54.1.4.name: Probable mitochondrial transport protein FSF1 (Fungal sideroflexin-1)

2.A.54.1.5.description: Sideroflexin-5 (SFXN5; SLC56A5) of 342 aas and 5 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement. The identification and characterization of the human sideroflexin 5 gene, and its high expression in the brain have been reported ( Lockhart et al. 2002 ). It does not appear to be a Parkinson disease protein but may be a citrate transporter. It is 99% identical to the human ortholog.
2.A.54.1.5.name: Sideroflexin-5 (SFXN5; SLC56A5) of 342 aas and 5 TMSs in a 1 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.54.1.6.name: Sideroflexin-3, Sfxn3 or SLC56A3, of 321 aas and 4 TMSs in a 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

2.A.54.1.7.name: Tricarboxylic acid (TCA) transporter of 327 aas and 6 TMSs.

2.A.55.2.12.name: VO 2+ (vanidate) NRAMP uptake system in vacuoles of vanadocytes.

The epiphytic Pseudomonas syringae strain which produces and excretes 3-methyarginine does so to compete with pathogenic strains of P. syringae for which 3-methyarginine is toxic.

The MsmX ATPase can function with other receptor-dependent ABC transporters (TC# 3.A.1.1.2 and 3.A.1.1.34). The crystal structure of MsmX provides a framework to understand the molecular basis of the broader specificity of interaction with the transmembrane subunits of these systems ( Leisico et al. 2020 ).

3.A.1.1.28.name: The raffinose/stachyose transporter, MsmEFGK (MalK (3.A.1.1.27) can probably substitute for MsmK; Webb et al. , 2008 ).

UgpB (the receptor) binds glycerol 3-P with high affinity, but not glycerol 2-P ( Wuttge et al. 2012 ). 3.A.1.1.31.name: The trehalose-recycling ABC transporter, LpqY-SugA-SugB-SugC (essential for virulence).

MsmX is also used by the MdxEFG-MsmX system (3.A.1.1.36) ( Ferreira and Sá-Nogueira, 2010 ). Involved in the uptake of pectin…
3.A.1.1.34.name: The arabinosaccharide transporter AraNPQMsmX.
