3.A.1.1.41.description: Trehalose porter. Also binds sucrose ( Boucher and Noll, 2011 ). Induced by glucose and trehalose. Directly regulated by trehalose-responsive regulator TreR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).
3.A.1.1.41.name: Trehalose porter.

3.A.1.1.42.description: α-glucoside uptake permease, Agl3E/Agl3F/Agl3G. Plays a role in normal morphogenesis and antibiotic production. Strongly induced by trehalose and melibiose, and weakly induced by lactose and glycerol but not glucose ( Hillerich and Westpheling 2006 ).The operon is controlled by a GntR homologue, Agl3R, and downstream of the gntR gene is a gene encoding an extracellular carbohydrase.
3.A.1.1.42.name: α-glucoside uptake permease, Agl3E/Agl3F/Agl3G.

3.A.1.1.43.description: Agl3E, Agl3F and Agl3G ABC porter. Induced by trehalose and melibiose using a GntR-like transcription factor ( Hillerich and Westpheling 2006 ) . The ATPase subunit, Agl3K, may be the MsiK (Sco4240; see 3.A.1.1.33) protein ( Saito et al. 2008 ).
3.A.1.1.43.name: Agl3E, Agl3F and Agl3G ABC porter.

3.A.1.1.44.description: MalEFG (K unknown), involved in maltose and maltodextrin uptake ( van Wezel et al. 1997 ). The MalK protein may be the MsiK (Sco4240; Q9L0Q1; see 3.A.1.1.33) protein.
3.A.1.1.44.name: MalEFG (K unknown), involved in maltose and maltodextrin uptake.

3.A.1.1.45.description: Maltose transporter, MusEFGKI. All five genes have been reported to be essential for uptake activity ( Henrich et al. 2013 ). The MusI gene product is of 215 aas with 5 TMSs and comprises the founding member of a distinct family of poorly characterized protein in TC family 9.B.28.
3.A.1.1.45.name: Maltose transporter, MusEFGKI.

3.A.1.1.46.description: Probable glucoside uptake porter, YcjNOPV. Encoded in an operon or gene cluster with a glucosyl hydrolase and two oxidoreductases ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).
3.A.1.1.46.name: Probable glucoside uptake porter, YcjNOPV.

3.A.1.1.47.description: ABC-type fucose uptake porter FucABCD. The ATPase subunit, FucD, has not been identified (Manzoor I., Shafeeq S., Afzal M. and Kuipers OP, JMMB, in press, 2015).
3.A.1.1.47.name: ABC-type fucose uptake porter FucABCD.

3.A.1.1.48.description: The lacto-N-biose I (LNB; Gal β-1,3-GlcNAc)/galacto-N-biose (GNB; Gal β-1,3-GalNAc) transporter. The solute-binding protein crystallizes only in the presence of LNB or GNB, and it was therefore named GNB/LNB-binding protein (GL-BP) ( Wada et al. 2007; Suzuki et al. 2008; Asakuma et al. 2011 ). Isothermal titration calorimetry measurements revealed that GL-BP specifically binds LNB and GNB with…
3.A.1.1.48.name: The lacto-N-biose I (LNB; Gal β-1,3-GlcNAc)/galacto-N-biose (GNB; Gal β-1,3-GalNAc) transporter.

3.A.1.1.49.description: The polyol (mannitol, glucitol (sorbitol), arabitol (arabinitol; lyxitol)) uptake porter, MtlEFGK ( Brünker et al. 1998 ).
3.A.1.1.49.name: The polyol (mannitol, glucitol (sorbitol), arabitol (arabinitol; lyxitol)) uptake porter, MtlEFGK.

3.A.1.1.50.description: Probable glycerophosphocholine (GPC) uptake porter ( Chandravanshi et al. 2016 ). The system may include a receptor and three membrane proteins (of 378 aas and 6 TMSs, 299 aas and 7 TMSs, and 113 aas and 3 TMSs (?). The ATPase has not been identified.
3.A.1.1.50.name: Probable glycerophosphocholine (GPC) uptake porter.

3.A.1.1.51.description: Maltose - maltoheptaose transporter, MalEFGK. MalEF is a R-M fusion protein with the MalE domain N-terminal and the MalF domain C-terminal. The protein, of 733 aas, has 8 TMSs, one N-terminal to MalE (a signal sequence for export of the MalE domain to the periplasm), an extra TMS at the N-terminus to bring the N-terminus to the periplasmic side of the inner membrane, and then the usual 6 TMSs…
3.A.1.1.51.name: Maltose - maltoheptaose transporter, MalEFGK.

3.A.1.1.52.description: Sugar (sucrose, maltose, glucose, fructose, esculin (coumarin β-glucoside)) uptake system possibly consisting of 5 or 6 proteins (see below) ( Nieves-Morión and Flores 2017 ). These proteins are all implicated in sugar uptake, but they may include components of multiple transporters. The system may also regulate formation of septal nanopores ( Flores et al. 2018 ).
3.A.1.1.52.name: Sugar (sucrose, maltose, glucose, fructose, esculin (coumarin β-glucoside)) uptake system possibly consisting of 5 or 6 proteins (see below).

3.A.1.1.53.description: Oligosaccharide transporter RafEFGK. RafE, the binding protein, has be extensively characterized. It binds α-(1,6)-linked glucosides and galactosides of varying size, linkage, and monosaccharide composition with preference for the trisaccharides raffinose and panose. This preference is reflected in the α-(1,6)-galactoside uptake profile of the bacterium. Structures of RafE (BlG16BP) in complex…
3.A.1.1.53.name: Oligosaccharide transporter RafEFGK.

3.A.1.1.55.description: Four comoponent ABC uptake porter, possibly transporting mannosyl glycerate. The four components of this system and a potential mannosyl glycerate hydrolase are encoded within a single operon.
3.A.1.1.55.name: Four comoponent ABC uptake porter, possibly transporting mannosyl glycerate.

3.A.1.1.56.description: Uptake transport system for L-arabinose and D-xylose, XacGHIJK ( Johnsen et al. 2019 ). The system has a receptor, two 6 TMS membrane proteins and two ATPases. xacGHIJK is upregulated by growth in the presence of either D-xylose or L-arabinose, mediated by the transcriptional regulator, XacR, the general regulator of xac catabolic genes ( Johnsen et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.1.56.name: Uptake transport system for L-arabinose and D-xylose, XacGHIJK.

3.A.1.1.57.description: ABC uptake porter consisting of AbnE (R), AbnF (M) and AbnJ (M). The ATPase (C) has not been identified and does not appear to be encoded within the same gene cluster. This gene cluster also encodes an extracellular arabinanase, an intracellular arabinofuranosidase, and many other enzymes of arabinose/pentose metabolism as well as a sensor kinase/response regulator and another ABC transporter…
3.A.1.1.57.name: ABC uptake porter consisting of AbnE (R), AbnF (M) and AbnJ (M).

3.A.1.1.58.description: Four component putative ABC transporter specific for N-acetylglucosamine.
3.A.1.1.58.name: Four component putative ABC transporter specific for N-acetylglucosamine.

3.A.1.1.59.description: Probable ABC transport system for the uptake of oligosaccharides (including a tetrasaccharide) of glucose, galactose and N-acetylglucosamine. The two membrane proteins are of 320 and 317 aas, both with 6 TMSs, and an extracytoplasmic binding receptor; the ATPase has not been identified.
3.A.1.1.59.name: Probable ABC transport system for the uptake of oligosaccharides (including a tetrasaccharide) of glucose, galactose and N-acetylglucosamine.

3.A.1.1.60.description: UspABC putative sugar uptake transporter, that probably imports peptidoglycan precursors ( Karlikowska et al. 2021 ).
3.A.1.1.60.name: UspABC putative sugar uptake transporter, that probably imports peptidoglycan precursors.

3.A.1.1.61.description: ABC sugar uptake porter with four protein components, 1 C, 2 M, and 1 R. This system has been found only in pathogenic Mycobacterium species ( De la Torre et al. 2021 ).
3.A.1.1.61.name: ABC sugar uptake porter with four protein components, 1 C, 2 M, and 1 R. This system has been found only in pathogenic Mycobacterium species.

3.A.1.1.62.description: MdxEFG/MsmX maltose/cyclodextrin uptake system of the ABC-type. This system transports (takes up) maltose and malto-cyclodextrins. The binding specificity of MdxE and its role in the cyclodextrin import in Thermoanaerobacterales has been determined ( Aranda-Caraballo et al. 2023 ).
3.A.1.1.62.name: MdxEFG/MsmX maltose/cyclodextrin uptake system of the ABC-type.

3.A.1.1.9.description: The oligosaccharide (glucuronate-linked to a xylo-oligosaccharide) ABC uptake porter, GuoEFGK in AguEFGK. GuoE binds with high affinity a four sugar aldotetrouronic acid [2-O-α-(4-O-methyl-α-D-glucuronosyl)-xylotriose] ( Shulami et al. , 1999 ; S.Shulami, personal communication)
3.A.1.1.9.name: The oligosaccharide (glucuronate-linked to a xylo-oligosaccharide) ABC uptake porter, GuoEFGK in AguEFGK.

3.A.1.10.name: The Ferric Iron Uptake Transporter (FeT) Family

3.A.1.10.1.description: Ferric iron (Fe 3+ ) porter, SfuABC ( Angerer et al. 1990 ). These iron uptake systems have been reviewed ( Angerer et al. 1992 ). Delepelaire 2019 reviewed structural and functional aspects of iron ABC transporters with emphasis on their substrate binding proteins.
3.A.1.10.1.name: Ferric iron (Fe 3+ ) porter, SfuABC.

3.A.1.10.3.description: Ferric iron (Fe 3+ ) porter, FbpABC or HitABC (selective for trivalent cations, Fe 3+ , Ga 3+ and Al 3+ ) ( Anderson et al ., 2004 )
3.A.1.10.3.name: Ferric iron (Fe 3+ ) porter, FbpABC or HitABC (selective for trivalent cations, Fe 3+ , Ga 3+ and Al 3+ )

3.A.1.10.4.description: The Fe-hydroxamate-type siderophore uptake porter (transports Fe +3 bound to ferrioxamine, ferrichrome or pyoverdine siderophores) ( Vajrala et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.10.4.name: The Fe-hydroxamate-type siderophore uptake porter (transports Fe +3 bound to ferrioxamine, ferrichrome or pyoverdine siderophores).

3.A.1.10.5.description: Siderophore-independent iron uptake system, AfuABC ( Saken et al. 2000 ).
3.A.1.10.5.name: Siderophore-independent iron uptake system, AfuABC.

3.A.1.10.6.description: Fe 3+ uptake porter consisting of 3 subunits, R, 330 aas, M, 516 aas and 12 TMSs, and C, 350 aas ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.10.6.name: Fe 3+ uptake porter consisting of 3 subunits, R, 330 aas, M, 516 aas and 12 TMSs, and C, 350 aas.

3.A.1.101.2.description: Vi polysaccharide exporter, VexBC ( Hashimoto et al , 1993 ).
3.A.1.101.2.name: Vi polysaccharide exporter, VexBC.

3.A.1.101.3.description: Capsular polysialate exporter, CtrC/D (functions with 1.B.18.2.3 (OMA) and 1.B.4.2.1 (MPA2)) ( Larue et al. , 2011 ).
3.A.1.101.3.name: Capsular polysialate exporter, CtrC/D (functions with 1.B.18.2.3 (OMA) and 1.B.4.2.1 (MPA2)).

3.A.1.103.10.description: Wzm (M; 280 aas; 6 or 7 TMSs in a 2 + 3 + 1 or 2 TMS arrangement)-Wzt (C) ABC lipid-linked galactan precursor exporter. Deletion of the encoding genes results in severe morphological changes and the accumulation of an aberrantly long galactan precursor. A model for coupled synthesis and export of the galactanpolymer precursor in mycobacteria has been proposed ( Savková et al. 2021 ). The two…
3.A.1.103.10.name: Wzm (M; 280 aas; 6 or 7 TMSs in a 2 + 3 + 1 or 2 TMS arrangement)-Wzt (C) ABC lipid-linked galactan precursor exporter.

3.A.1.103.11.description: ABC exporter for lipid-linked O-antigen lipopolysaccharide: Wzm (membane constituent; 261 aas with 5 or 6 TMSs) + Wzt (ATPase constituent; 431 aas with 0 TMSs). This system transports the lipid-linked LPS from the cytoplasm to the periplasm of the bacterial cell ( Kelly et al. 2024 ).
3.A.1.103.11.name: ABC exporter for lipid-linked O-antigen lipopolysaccharide: Wzm (membane constituent; 261 aas with 5 or 6 TMSs) + Wzt

3.A.1.103.2.description: Heteropolysaccharide O-antigen exporter, Wzm/Wzt ( Feng et al ., 2004 ). The C-terminal cytoplasmic domain of Wzt (an IgG-like β-sandwich) determines the specificity of the transporter for either O8 or O9a O-PS ( Cuthbertson et al., 2007 ). The transporter structure reveals a continuous transmembrane channel in a nucleotide-free state ( Caffalette et al. 2019 ). Upon ATP binding, large structural…
3.A.1.103.2.name: Heteropolysaccharide O-antigen exporter, Wzm/Wzt.

3.A.1.103.3.description: ABC transporter required for O-antigen biosynthesis and multicellular development, RfbAB ( Guo et al. 1996 ). Functions with the RfbC glycosyl transferase (TC#4.D.1.3.4).
3.A.1.103.3.name: ABC transporter required for O-antigen biosynthesis and multicellular development, RfbAB.

3.A.1.103.4.description: RfbAB lipopolysaccharide exporter ( Guo et al. 1996 ).
3.A.1.103.4.name: RfbAB lipopolysaccharide exporter.

3.A.1.103.5.description: ABC transporter mediating ethanol tolerance, Slr0977 (M)/Slr0982 (C) ( Zhang et al. 2015 ). Present in a gene cluster with (lipo)polysaccharide biosynthetic enzymes, so could be a cell surface carbohydrate export system.
3.A.1.103.5.name: ABC transporter mediating ethanol tolerance, Slr0977 (M)/Slr0982 (C).

3.A.1.103.6.description: Two component lipopolysaccharide exporter, Wzm/Wzt. Wzm is the membrane component (265 aas with 6 TMSs) which forms a ring-like large ion conductance channel. The ATPase, Wzt, functions both as the energizer and regulator ( Mohammad et al. 2016 ).
3.A.1.103.6.name: Two component lipopolysaccharide exporter, Wzm/Wzt.

3.A.1.103.7.description: ABC-type polysaccharide/polyol phosphate export systems, permease componentof 262 aas and 6 or 7 TM
3.A.1.103.7.name: ABC-type polysaccharide/polyol phosphate export systems, permease componentof 262 aas and 6 or 7 TM

3.A.1.103.9.description: ABC O-antigen lipopolysaccharide/polysaccharide export transporter, Wzm/Wzt of 253 aas and 6 TMSs (Wzm; also called AbcT3) and 396 aas and 0 TMSs (Wzt). The crystal structure is available (PDB 6AN7) ( Bi et al. 2018 ) for the Wzm-Wzt homologue from Aquifex aeolicus in an open conformation. The transporter forms a transmembrane channel that is sufficiently wide to accommodate a linear…
3.A.1.103.9.name: ABC O-antigen lipopolysaccharide/polysaccharide export transporter, Wzm/Wzt of 253 aas and 6 TMSs (Wzm; also called AbcT3) and 396 aas and 0 TMSs…

3.A.1.104.1.description: Teichoic acid exporter, TagGH. It is present in a large complex with the teichoic acid precursor synthetic enzymes ( Formstone et al. 2008 ). The substrate may be the diphospholipid-linked disaccharide portion of the teichoic acid precursor ( Schirner et al. 2011 ). 3-d structural studies have been reported ( Ko et al. 2016 ) showing that TagG and TagH are localized on the cytoplasmic membrane in…
3.A.1.104.1.name: Teichoic acid exporter, TagGH.

3.A.1.104.2.description: The teichoic acid precursor exporter, TarGH. May be specific for the diphospholipid linked disaccharide portion of the teichoic acid precursor ( Schirner et al. 2011 ). TarG is the target of a small antimicrobial inhibitor of S. aureus growth ( Swoboda et al. 2009 ). TarGH is a WTA transporter and has been purified and reconstituted in proteoliposomes ( Matano et al. 2017 ). They showed that a…
3.A.1.104.2.name: The teichoic acid precursor exporter, TarGH.

3.A.1.105.1.description: Daunorubicin, doxorubicin etc. (multidrug resistance) exporter, DrrAB. DrrB binds drugs with variable affinities and contains multiple drug binding sites. The two asymmetric nucleotide binding sites in DrrA have strikingly different binding affinities. Long-range conformational changes occur between DrrA and DrrB. The transduction pathway from the nucleotide-binding DrrA subunit to the substrate…
3.A.1.105.1.name: Daunorubicin, doxorubicin etc. (multidrug resistance) exporter, DrrAB.

3.A.1.105.10.description: AbcG homologue, ABCH1 of 705 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M arrangement. May be involved in steroid or drug efflux ( Popovic et al. 2010 ). Of the vertbrates, it may be restricted to fish.
3.A.1.105.10.name: AbcG homologue, ABCH1 of 705 aas and 6 TMSs in a C-M arrangement.

3.A.1.105.11.description: ABC-2 transporter probably specific for a lantibiotic. The genes for this system are adjacent to an S2P-M50 peptidase (G0Q3D2), probably involved in pro-lantibiotic processing, as well as a lantibiotic biosynthetic enzyme (G0Q3D1) and a lantibiotic dehydratase (G0Q3D0).
3.A.1.105.11.name: ABC-2 transporter probably specific for a lantibiotic.

3.A.1.105.12.description: Three component ABC-2 transporter: (1) the membrane (M) subunit with a C-terminal CBS domain, (2) an ABC ATPase subunit and (3) an M50 peptidase (Zn 2+ -metalopeptidase) of 392 aas and 6TMSs. they may export a bacteriocin, and the protease cleaves off the signal peptide during export. The three encoding genes are in a single gene cluster.
3.A.1.105.12.name: Three component ABC-2 transporter: (1) the membrane (M) subunit with a C-terminal CBS domain, (2) an ABC ATPase subunit and (3) an M50 peptidase

3.A.1.105.14.description: RagAB, involved in both aerial hyphae formation and sporulation ( San Paolo et al. 2006 ).
3.A.1.105.14.name: RagAB, involved in both aerial hyphae formation and sporulation.

3.A.1.105.15.description: Putative drug exporter, YbhFGRS ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).
3.A.1.105.15.name: Putative drug exporter, YbhFGRS.

3.A.1.105.16.description: Putative ABC export system (MDR?), RbbA/YhhJ/YhiI (All three genes are in a single operon; this system may comprise a single ABC exporter with MFP; substrate unknown ( Moussatova et al. 2008 and unpublished observations).
3.A.1.105.16.name: Putative ABC export system (MDR?), RbbA/YhhJ/YhiI

3.A.1.105.17.description: The putative polyketide drug exporter, YadGH. May also transport phospholipids, participating in phospholipid trafficking together with the Mla complex. It interacts with MlaABCDEF (TC# 3.A.1.27.3) to preserve outer membrane asymmetry ( Malinverni and Silhavy 2009 ; Babu et al. 2018 ).
3.A.1.105.17.name: The putative polyketide drug exporter, YadGH.

3.A.1.105.19.description: Poorly characterized ABC exporter involved in bacterial competitiveness and bioflim morphology, YfiLMN ( Stubbendieck and Straight 2017 ).
3.A.1.105.19.name: Poorly characterized ABC exporter involved in bacterial competitiveness and bioflim morphology, YfiLMN.

3.A.1.105.20.description: Putative 5 component ABC exporter with two membrane constituents, two cytoplasmic ATPases, and one membrane fusion protein (truncated at the N-terminus, probably because of an incorrect initiation codon assignment).
3.A.1.105.20.name: Putative 5 component ABC exporter with two membrane constituents, two cytoplasmic ATPases, and one membrane fusion protein

3.A.1.105.21.description: Uncharacterized ABC transporter with two components, a transmembrane protein with 6 TMSs and an ATPase. The substrate in unknown.
3.A.1.105.21.name: Uncharacterized ABC transporter with two components, a transmembrane protein with 6 TMSs and an ATPase.

3.A.1.105.25.description: ATP-binding cassette transporter subfamily Gof 687 aas and 7 TMSs in a 1 + 6 TMS arrangement. 13 ABCG genes were identified in N. lugens, and expression levels of these ABCG transporter genes after treatment with thiamethoxam, abamectin, and cyantraniliprole has been examined. Some increase in amounts while others do not ( Yang et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.105.25.name: ATP-binding cassette transporter subfamily Gof 687 aas and 7 TMSs in a 1 + 6 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.105.28.description: ABC-like transporter with 4 components, two integrals membrane ABC proteins (O26020 and O26021, 376 and 365 aas, respectively) , an MFP protein (OP94851; 329 aas) and a TolC-like protein (O026022; 510 aas). This system appears to play a role in flagellar stability and bacterial motility ( Gibson et al. 2022 ).
3.A.1.105.28.name: ABC-like transporter with 4 components, two integrals membrane ABC proteins (O26020 and O26021, 376 and 365 aas, respectively) , an MFP protein…

3.A.1.105.3.description: The 4A-4E-O-dideacetyl-chromomycin A 3 (biosynthetic precursor of chromomycin) exporter (may also export chromomycin and mithramycin ( Menendez et al ., 2007 ).
3.A.1.105.3.name: The 4A-4E-O-dideacetyl-chromomycin A 3 (biosynthetic precursor of chromomycin) exporter

3.A.1.105.4.description: The pyoluteorin (a chlorinated polyketide) efflux pump, PltHIJKN ( Brodhagen et al. 2005 ; Huang et al. 2006 ).
3.A.1.105.4.name: The pyoluteorin (a chlorinated polyketide) efflux pump, PltHIJKN.

3.A.1.105.5.description: AbcG homologue, Snustorr, sioform A, Snu, of 808 aas and 6 TMSs in a 1 + 5 TMS arrangement at the C-terminal part of the protein. The N-terminal domain is the ATPase domain. The protein therefore has a C-M domain arrangement. Lipids in extracellular matrices (ECM) contribute to barrier function and stability of epithelial tissues such as the pulmonary alveoli and the skin. In insects, skin…
3.A.1.105.5.name: AbcG homologue, Snustorr, sioform A, Snu, of 808 aas and 6 TMSs in a 1 + 5 TMS arrangement at the C-terminal part of the protein.

3.A.1.105.8.description: ABC-2 transporter. The two genes encoding this system are adjacent to one encoding an squalene-hopene cyclase that coverts squalene to hopene. The substrate could therefore be hopene or a hydrocarbon triterpene derivative of it ( Racolta et al. 2012 ).
3.A.1.105.8.name: ABC-2 transporter.

3.A.1.105.9.description: ABC2 membrane proteins (J7ZHK9 and J8A8S6) with ATPase (J8ABC0) transporter
3.A.1.105.9.name: ABC2 membrane proteins (J7ZHK9 and J8A8S6) with ATPase (J8ABC0) transporter

3.A.1.106.1.description: Phospholipid, LPS, lipid A and drug exporter, MsbA, which flips the substrate from the inner leaflet of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer leaflet ( Eckford and Sharom, 2010 ). MsbA also confers drug resistance to azidopine, daunomycin, vinblastine, Hoechst 33342 and ethidium ( Reuter et al ., 2003 ). Four x-ray structures, trapped in different conformations, two with and two without…
3.A.1.106.1.name: Phospholipid, LPS, lipid A and drug exporter, MsbA, which flips the substrate from the inner leaflet of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer leaflet.

3.A.1.106.10.description: Involved in the export of a molecule required for the autochemotactic process. AbcA integrated permease/ATPase (M-C) protein, MXAN_1286 ( Ward et al. 1998 ).
3.A.1.106.10.name: Involved in the export of a molecule required for the autochemotactic process.

3.A.1.106.11.description: HlyA/MsbA family transporter of 595 aas. The gene for this protein is adjacent to and probably in the same operon as that encoding 3.A.1.106.12. They both have 6 TMSs, so they may together comprise a single heterodimeric system.
3.A.1.106.11.name: HlyA/MsbA family transporter of 595 aas.

3.A.1.106.12.description: HlyA/MsbA family transporter of 577 aas. The gene encoding this protein is adjacent to and in the same operon with that encoding 3.A.1.106.11. They both have 6 TMSs, so they may together comprise a single heterodimeric system.
3.A.1.106.12.name: HlyA/MsbA family transporter of 577 aas.

3.A.1.106.13.description: Multidrug resistance-like ABC exporter, MdlAB; exports peptides of 6 - 21 aas ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).
3.A.1.106.13.name: Multidrug resistance-like ABC exporter, MdlAB; exports peptides of 6 - 21 aas.

3.A.1.106.14.description: Lipid A exporter homologue of 593 aas and 6 TMSs (N-terminal with a C-terminal ATPase domain. Essential for acid, salt and thermal tolerance ( Matsuhashi et al. 2015 ).
3.A.1.106.14.name: Lipid A exporter homologue of 593 aas and 6 TMSs

3.A.1.106.15.description: Lipid flippase, PglK or WlaB, of 564 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs with a C-terminal ATPase domain. Mediates the ATP-dependent translocation of an undecaprenylpyrophosphate-linked heptasaccharide intermediate (LLO) across the cell membrane, an essential step during the N-linked protein glycosylation pathway. Transport across the membrane is effected via ATP-driven conformation changes. Most likely…
3.A.1.106.15.name: Lipid flippase, PglK or WlaB, of 564 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs with a C-terminal ATPase domain.

3.A.1.106.18.description: Peptide and multidrug resistance porter of the ABC superfamily, TmrAB. TmrA (Q72J05; 600 aas with 6 N-terminal TMSs) and TmrB (Q72J04; 578 aas with 6 N-terminal TMSs) comprise this heterodimeric transporter, both proteins of the M-C structure. The system has been found to export the dye, hoechst 33342, and to be inhibited by verapamil ( Zutz et al. 2011 ). The subnanometre-resolution structure of…
3.A.1.106.18.name: Peptide and multidrug resistance porter of the ABC superfamily, TmrAB.

3.A.1.106.19.description: ABC exporter. It has been suggested that it might be a glycolate exporter ( Braakman et al. 2017 ). However it's closest hit in TCDB (31% identity in the transmembrane domain) has TC# 3.A.1.106.18, which is probably a peptide/multidrug (and possibly glycolipid) exporter with broad substrate specificity.
3.A.1.106.19.name: ABC exporter.

3.A.1.106.2.description: The homodimeric Sav1866 multidrug exporter (transports doxorubicin, verapamil, ethidium, tetraphenylphosphonium, vinblastine and the fluorescent dye, Hoechst 33342; 3-D structure known at 3 Å resolution; Dawson and Locher, 2006 ; Velamakanni et al. , 2008 ) The empty site opens by rotation of the nucleotide-binding domain whereas the ATP-bound site remains occluded ( Jones and George, 2011 )…
3.A.1.106.2.name: The homodimeric Sav1866 multidrug exporter The empty site opens by rotation of the nucleotide-binding domain whereas the ATP-bound site remains…

3.A.1.106.20.description: MsbA of 582 aas and 6 TMSs in an M-C arrangement. The X-ray structure at 2.8 Å resolution in an inward-facing conformation after cocrystallization with lipid A and using a stabilizing facial amphiphile has been reported ( Padayatti et al. 2019 ). The structure displays a large amplitude opening in the transmembrane portal, which is likely to be required for lipid A to pass from its site of…
3.A.1.106.20.name: MsbA of 582 aas and 6 TMSs in an M-C arrangement.

3.A.1.106.21.description: Quiinol:oxygen oxidoreductzase; thiol reductant ABC exporter subunit CydC, of 583 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement plus a hydrophilic C-terninal half ( Murali et al. 2021 ).
3.A.1.106.21.name: Quiinol:oxygen oxidoreductzase; thiol reductant ABC exporter subunit CydC, of 583 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement plus a…

3.A.1.106.22.description: Heme transporter (previously proposed to be a thiol (cysteine/glutathione) exporter, CydDC; CydC is also called MdrH (periplasmic cysteine is required for cytochrome bd assembly) ( Cruz-Ramos et al ., 2004 ). The purified asymmetric heterodimer exhibits low ATPase activity which is activated by both thiols and heme (e.g., heme b) ( Yamashita et al. 2014 ). Bacterial redox homoeostasis during…
3.A.1.106.22.name: Heme transporter

3.A.1.106.3.description: The dimeric multidrug resistance exporter, ABC1/2 (exports the peptide antimicrobials, nisin and polymyxin; ( Margolles et al ., 2006 ) (both ABC1 and ABC2 also show striking similarity to family 3.A.1.117).
3.A.1.106.3.name: The dimeric multidrug resistance exporter, ABC1/2

3.A.1.106.5.description: The heterodimeric multidrug efflux pump, SmdAB (exports norfloxacin, tetracycline, 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI), and Hoechst 33342) ( Matsuo et al ., 2008 ).
3.A.1.106.5.name: The heterodimeric multidrug efflux pump, SmdAB (exports norfloxacin, tetracycline, 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI), and Hoechst 33342).

3.A.1.106.6.description: Multidrug efflux pump, Rv0194 (exports & causes resistance to ampicillin, streptomycin and chloramphenicol by 32- to 64-fold and to vancomycin and tetracycline by 4- to 8-fold ( Danilchanka et al ., 2008 )).
3.A.1.106.6.name: Multidrug efflux pump, Rv0194

3.A.1.106.7.description: The Salmochelin/Enterobactin secretory exporter, IroC ( Crouch et al ., 2008 ; Müller et al. 2009 ).
3.A.1.106.7.name: The Salmochelin/Enterobactin secretory exporter, IroC.

3.A.1.106.8.description: The heterodimeric BmrC/BmrD (YheHI) MDR transporter. Transports a wide range of structurally unrelated drugs including doxorubicin, mitoxantrone, ethidium, and hoechst 33342 ( Torres et al. , 2009 ). It activates the sensor kinase, KinA, during sporulation initiation ( Fukushima et al. 2006 ). Large scale purification has been achieved ( Galián et al. 2011 ). It has been reconstituted in giant…
3.A.1.106.8.name: The heterodimeric BmrC/BmrD (YheHI) MDR transporter.

3.A.1.106.9.description: SoxR regulon single protein ABC exporter, Sco7008, containing an N-terminal membrane domain and a C-terminal ATPase domain ( Shin et al. 2011 ). SoxR responds to extracellular redox-active compounds. Thus, it is induced in stationary phase during the production of the benzochromanequinone blue-pigmented antibiotic, actinorhodin ( Naseer et al. 2014 ). Possibly an actinorhodin exporter.
3.A.1.106.9.name: SoxR regulon single protein ABC exporter, Sco7008, containing an N-terminal membrane domain and a C-terminal ATPase domain.

3.A.1.107.1.description: Putative heme exporter, CcmABC=CycVWZ (Note: CcmC may function independently of CcmAB) ( Feissner et al ., 2006 ; Christensen et al ., 2007 )
3.A.1.107.1.name: Putative heme exporter, CcmABC=CycVWZ (Note: CcmC may function independently of CcmAB)

3.A.1.107.2.description: The mitochondrial ABC transporter involved in cytochrome c maturation, CcmA/CcmB. (Note: CcmA is nuclearly encoded while CcmB is mitochondrially encoded) ( Rayapuram et al ., 2007 )
3.A.1.107.2.name: The mitochondrial ABC transporter involved in cytochrome c maturation, CcmA/CcmB.

3.A.1.107.3.description: CcmABCD exporter; CcmD (69aas, 1TMS) is required for the release of CcmE (which binds heme in the periplasm) from CcmABC. CcmC (9.B.14.2.3) is required for the transfer of heme to CcmE in the periplasm ( Richard-Fogal et al ., 2008 ) In the presence of heme, CcmC and CcmE form a stable complex ( Richard-Fogal & Kranz, 2010 ) as do CcmE and CcmF ( San Francisco and Kranz 2014 ). The cytochrome c…
3.A.1.107.3.name: CcmABCD exporter; CcmD (69aas, 1TMS) is required for the release of CcmE (which binds heme in the periplasm) from CcmABC.

3.A.1.107.4.description: Cytochrome c maturation system (heme exporter?), CcmA/B
3.A.1.107.4.name: Cytochrome c maturation system (heme exporter?), CcmA/B

3.A.1.107.5.description: CcmB of 353 aas with 9 TMSs. It may act with TC# 9.B.14.1.21, involved in heme insertioin into cytochrome c ( Gupta et al. 2022 ).
3.A.1.107.5.name: CcmB of 353 aas with 9 TMSs.

3.A.1.108.1.description: β-(1,2)-Glucan exporter, NdvA, of 585 aas and 6 TMSs in an N-terminal 2 2 + 2 TMS arrangement followed by a C-terminal ATPase. It mediates the export of the nascent β-D-glucan polymer to the cell surface where it functions in biofilm formation ( Römling and Galperin 2015 ).
3.A.1.108.1.name: β-(1,2)-Glucan exporter, NdvA, of 585 aas and 6 TMSs in an N-terminal 2 2 + 2 TMS arrangement followed by a C-terminal ATPase.

3.A.1.108.2.description: Glucan ABC transporter of 593 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement at the N-terminus followed by the ATPase domain (C-terminus), NdvA. It is involved in beta-(1-->2)glucan export. The transmembrane segments (TMSs) form a pore in the inner membrane and the ATP-binding domain (NBD) is responsible for energy generation.
3.A.1.108.2.name: Glucan ABC transporter of 593 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement at the N-terminus followed by the ATPase domain (C-terminus), NdvA.

3.A.1.109.1.description: α-Hemolysin exporter. HlyB has an (inactive?) N-terminal C39 peptidase-like domain ( Lecher et al. , 2011 ). It is essential for secretion and interacts with the unfolded HlyA, thereby protecting it from cytoplasmic degradation ( Lecher et al. 2012 ). Type 1 secretion systems (T1SSs) extruding protein substrates following synthesis of the entire polypeptide. The E. coli hemolysin A secretion…
3.A.1.109.1.name: α-Hemolysin exporter.

3.A.1.109.2.description: Cyclolysin exporter, CyaB ( Glaser et al ., 1988 ) (Possesses an N-terminal lysosomal sorting signal within the amino-terminal transmembrane domain; Kamakura et al. , 2008 ).
3.A.1.109.2.name: Cyclolysin exporter, CyaB.

3.A.1.109.3.description: LapA adhesin protein exporter, LapB ( Hinsa et al ., 2003 )
3.A.1.109.3.name: LapA adhesin protein exporter, LapB

3.A.1.109.4.description: The biofilm inducible ABC drug (tobramycin, gentamycin, and ciprofloxacin) resistance pump, PA1875-PA1877 ( Zhang and Mah, 2008 ). It is specifically induced and is most active when growing in a biofilm.
3.A.1.109.4.name: The biofilm inducible ABC drug (tobramycin, gentamycin, and ciprofloxacin) resistance pump, PA1875-PA1877.

3.A.1.109.6.description: Probable 2646 aa extracellular adhesin (acc# C6BWI7) ABC exporter of 715 aas. Functions as a type I protein secretion system together with an MFP and an OMF which all are encoded within a single operon together with the adhesin and SiiAB homologues as for TC# 3.A.1.109.5.
3.A.1.109.6.name: Probable 2646 aa extracellular adhesin (acc# C6BWI7) ABC exporter of 715 aas.

3.A.1.109.8.description: Leukotoxin export protein of 707 aas, LtxB (has a fused M-C structure with 6 TMSs) ( Guthmiller et al. 1995 ). Functions with the MFP, LtxD (TC# 8.A.1.3.4) and the TolC-like protein, TdeA (TC# 1.B.17.3.11).
3.A.1.109.8.name: Leukotoxin export protein of 707 aas, LtxB (has a fused M-C structure with 6 TMSs).

3.A.1.11.1.description: Polyamine (putrescine/spermidine) uptake porter. Plays a role in biofilm formation ( Zhang et al. 2013 ). Spermidine-preferring ( Igarashi and Kashiwagi 1996 ).
3.A.1.11.1.name: Polyamine (putrescine/spermidine) uptake porter.

3.A.1.11.10.description: The 3-component polyamine uptake transporter, PotABD. Transports homospermidine and possibly other polyamines. Inactivation of the potADB gene cluster (potADB) disrupted diazotrophic growth, clearly suggesting the importance of polyamine homeostasis in Anabaena. ( Burnat et al. 2018 ).
3.A.1.11.10.name: The 3-component polyamine uptake transporter, PotABD.

3.A.1.11.6.description: The γ-aminobutyrate (GABA) uptake system, GtsABCD ( White et al. , 2009 ).
3.A.1.11.6.name: The γ-aminobutyrate (GABA) uptake system, GtsABCD.

3.A.1.11.7.description: The spermidine/putrescine uptake porter, PotABCD ( Shah et al. 2008; Shah et al. 2006; Ware et al. 2006 Shah et al. 2006; Ware et al. 2006 Ware et al. 2006 ).
3.A.1.11.7.name: The spermidine/putrescine uptake porter, PotABCD.

3.A.1.11.9.description: Putative polyamine (spermidine/putrescine) uptake porter, YdcSTUV ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ). May also be involved in the uptake of double stranded DNA ( Sun 2018 ).
3.A.1.11.9.name: Putative polyamine (spermidine/putrescine) uptake porter, YdcSTUV.

3.A.1.110.10.description: The AlgE-type Mannuronan C-5-Epimerase exporter, EexD (PrtD) ( Gimmestad et al ., 2006 ).
3.A.1.110.10.name: The AlgE-type Mannuronan C-5-Epimerase exporter, EexD (PrtD).

3.A.1.110.11.description: Secretion system for metalloprotease, PrtA, PrtDEF ( Akatsuka et al. 1997 ). (PrtF=1.B.17.1.2)
3.A.1.110.11.name: Secretion system for metalloprotease, PrtA, PrtDEF. (PrtF=1.B.17.1.2)

3.A.1.110.12.description: Thermostable lipase, TliA (Q9ZG91; 476 aas with a C-terminal region that shows similarity to members of the RTX toxin family (1.C.11)) exporter, TliDEF. The wild type transporter has a temperature sensitive defect which can be corrected by a single mutation in TliD ( Eom et al. 2016 ).
3.A.1.110.12.name: Thermostable lipase, TliA (Q9ZG91; 476 aas with a C-terminal region that shows similarity to members of the RTX toxin family (1.C.11)) exporter…

3.A.1.110.13.description: Protein export system, PrtD of 564 aas and 6 TMSs. The 3.15 Å structure has been solved ( Morgan et al. 2017 ). The structure suggests a substrate entry window just above the transporter's nucleotide binding domains. Highly kinked transmembrane helices, which frame a narrow channel, not observed in canonical peptide transporters, are likely involved in substrate translocation. The PrtD structure…
3.A.1.110.13.name: Protein export system, PrtD of 564 aas and 6 TMSs.

3.A.1.110.3.description: The multiple protein exporter, PrsD/PrsE (exports EPS glycanases, PlyA and PlyB, as well as Rhizobium adhering proteins) ( Russo et al ., 2006 ). 12 substrates have been identified; PrsDE provide the major route of protein export in R. leguminosarum ( Krehenbrink and Downie, 2008 ).
3.A.1.110.3.name: The multiple protein exporter, PrsD/PrsE (exports EPS glycanases, PlyA and PlyB, as well as Rhizobium adhering proteins).

3.A.1.110.6.description: Exporter for lipase LipA, protease PrtA and S-layer protein SlaA, LipBCD ( Akatsuka et al. 1997 ). LipABC is also called PrtDEF.
3.A.1.110.6.name: Exporter for lipase LipA, protease PrtA and S-layer protein SlaA, LipBCD.

3.A.1.110.7.description: Exporter for heme-binding protein, HasA and metaloprotease, PrtA. Functions as a complex spanning the two membranes of the cell envelope: HasDEF (HasD = ABC protein; HasE = the MFP; HasF = the OMF (see 2.A.6.2.31 for HasF) ( Akatsuka et al. 1997 ).
3.A.1.110.7.name: Exporter for heme-binding protein, HasA and metaloprotease, PrtA.

3.A.1.110.9.description: Exporter of HasA lipase, and alkaline protease
3.A.1.110.9.name: Exporter of HasA lipase, and alkaline protease

3.A.1.111.1.description: Hemolysin/bacteriocin (cytolysin) exporter with associated proteolytic activity
3.A.1.111.1.name: Hemolysin/bacteriocin (cytolysin) exporter with associated proteolytic activity

3.A.1.111.4.description: Bacteriocin immunity protein, SmbG (198 aas; 6TMSs in a 2+2+2 arrangement. (Exports bacteriocins and causes resistance to antibiotics such as tetracycline, penicillin and triclosan). Upregulated by exposure to antibiotics ( Matsumoto-Nakano and Kuramitsu, 2006 )
3.A.1.111.4.name: Bacteriocin immunity protein, SmbG

3.A.1.111.7.description: Nukacin ISK-1 bacteriocin exporter, NukT of 694 aas and 6 TMSs. The protease domain is N-terminal, the membrane domain is central, and the ATPase domain in C-terminal. NukT and its peptidase-inactive mutant have been expressed, purified, and reconstituted into liposomes for analysis of their peptidase and ATPase activities. The ATPase activity of the NBD (C) region is required for the…
3.A.1.111.7.name: Nukacin ISK-1 bacteriocin exporter, NukT of 694 aas and 6 TMSs.

3.A.1.112.1.description: Competence factor (CSF; a heptadecapeptide) exporter of 717 aas. The transporter is fused to an N-terminal peptidase domain and functions with an MFP accessory protein, ComB (TC# 8.A.1.4.2) ( Ishii et al. 2006 ).
3.A.1.112.1.name: Competence factor (CSF; a heptadecapeptide) exporter of 717 aas.

3.A.1.112.10.description: Bacteriocin exporter of 721 aas and 7 TMSs. Residues 10 - 134: peptidase with N-terminal TMS; residues 167 - 446: TM domain; residues 480 - 715: ATPase.
3.A.1.112.10.name: Bacteriocin exporter of 721 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.A.1.112.11.description: Enterocin CRL35 exporter, MunB, of 674 aas and 6 TMSs in an M-C domain arrangement. The specific receptor for Enterocin CRL35 (MunA; TC# 1.C.24.1.15) acts as a docking molecule, not a structural part of the pore, but the bacteriocin must be anchored to the membrane ( Ríos Colombo et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.112.11.name: Enterocin CRL35 exporter, MunB, of 674 aas and 6 TMSs in an M-C domain arrangement.

3.A.1.112.12.description: Colicin V exporter. The ATPase is a GTPase ( Zhong and Tai 1998 ; ).
3.A.1.112.12.name: Colicin V exporter.

3.A.1.112.13.description: Microcin E492 exporter, MceFGH (MceF has 5 - 7 TMSs and is most likely a CAAX amino terminal protease that might function in the processing of microcin E492; MceG has a short hydrophilic N-terminus, a centra 6 TMS ABC domain, and a C-terminal ABC ATPase domain; MceH has 1 N-terminal TMS) ( Bieler et al ., 2006 ; Lagos et al ., 1999 )
3.A.1.112.13.name: Microcin E492 exporter, MceFGH

3.A.1.112.9.description: ABC bacteriocin exporter with two peptidase domains, Pcat1. 3-D structures are known (4S0F, 6V9Z, 4RY2). The pathway for peptide export consists of an large α-helical barrel for small folded peptides. ATP binding alternates access to the transmembrane pathway and reglates protease activity ( Lin et al. 2015 ). Subunit asymmetry of the M3-M4 loops contribute to optimizing AChR activation through…
3.A.1.112.9.name: ABC bacteriocin exporter with two peptidase domains, Pcat1.

3.A.1.113.3.description: The multidrug/microcin J25 (MccJ25; 21 aa cyclic peptide antibiotic; the precursor peptide is McjA) exporter, YojI ( Delgado et al ., 2005 ). TolC is also required for export; Vincent and Morero, 2009 ). This system exports many phytol derivatives ( Upadhyay et al. 2014 ). Also exports L-cysteine ( Yamada et al. , 2006 ). This is one of two microcin J25 exporters, the other being McjD (TC#…
3.A.1.113.3.name: The multidrug/microcin J25 (MccJ25; 21 aa cyclic peptide antibiotic; the precursor peptide is McjA) exporter, YojI.

3.A.1.114.1.description: Glycolipid exporter (under nitrogen control in heterocysts), DevABC-HgdD ( Moslavac et al ., 2007 ). Heterocyst envelope glycolipids (HGLs) function as an O 2 diffusion barrier, being deposited over the heterocyst outer membrane, surrounded by an outermost heterocyst polysaccharide envelope. DevBCA and TolC form an ATP-driven efflux pump required for the export of HGLs across the Gram-negative…
3.A.1.114.1.name: Glycolipid exporter (under nitrogen control in heterocysts), DevABC-HgdD.

3.A.1.114.2.description: Alr4280, Alr4281 and Alr4282 of (1)) 436 aas (Q8YPB8, 0 TMSs, 40% identical to DevB in TC# 3.A.1.114.1), (2) 395 aas (Q8YPB7, 4 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS arrangement, 52% identical to DevC in TC# 3.A.1.114.1), and (3) 276 aas (Q8YPB6, 1 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS arrangement, 70% identical to DevA in 3.A.1.114.1), respectively ( Shvarev and Maldener 2019 ). The substrate is unknown.
3.A.1.114.2.name: Alr4280, Alr4281 and Alr4282 of (1)) 436 aas (Q8YPB8, 0 TMSs, 40% identical to DevB in TC# 3.A.1.114.1), (2) 395 aas

3.A.1.114.3.description: Putative lipid transporter (based on similarity with TC# 3.A.1.114.1), DevC, of 392 aas and 6 putative TMSs ( Parveen et al. 2026 ).
3.A.1.114.3.name: Putative lipid transporter (based on similarity with TC# 3.A.1.114.1), DevC, of 392 aas and 6 putative TMSs.

3.A.1.115.1.description: Na + efflux pump NatAB. It is induced by ethanol andby protonophores ( Cheng et al. 1997 ). A similar system was found in the alkaliphilic Bacillus firmus OF4 species ( Wei et al. 1999 ). The Bacillus subtilis NatK-NatR two-component system regulates expression of the natAB operon ( Ogura et al. 2007 ).
3.A.1.115.1.name: Na + efflux pump NatAB.

3.A.1.115.2.description: Putative Na extrusion pump, NatAB. NatB has an N-terminal NatB domain (residues 1 - 375) as well as a C-terminal CAAX protease domain (9.B.2; residues 380 - 650).
3.A.1.115.2.name: Putative Na extrusion pump, NatAB.

3.A.1.115.4.description: Probable two component Na + efflux system, NatAB, where NatB is a 228 aa ATPase and NatA is a 416 aa membrane protein with 6 TMSs in a 1 + 5 TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.115.4.name: Probable two component Na + efflux system, NatAB, where NatB is a 228 aa ATPase and NatA is a 416 aa membrane protein with 6 TMSs in a 1 + 5 TMS…

3.A.1.117.1.description: The multidrug exporter, LmrA (can also substitute for MsbA [TC #3.A.1.106.1] to export lipid A; Reuter et al ., 2003 ). Structural models have been presented ( Ecker et al. 2004 ; Federici et al. 2007 ). Hoechst 33342 is a substrate ( van den Berg and van Saparoea et al. 2005 ). Coupled ATPase-adenylate kinase activity in ABC transporters including LmrA has been demonstrated ( Kaur et al. 2016 )…
3.A.1.117.1.name: The multidrug exporter, LmrA.

3.A.1.117.2.description: Hop resistance protein, HorA. Reconstitution in phosphatidyl ethanolamine bilayers resulted in normal activity, but reconstitution in phosphatidyl choline resulted in uncoupling of ATP hydrolysis from transport and a change in the orientations of the TMSs ( Gustot et al. 2010 ).
3.A.1.117.2.name: Hop resistance protein, HorA.

3.A.1.117.3.description: Multidrug resistance homodimeric efflux pump, BmrA (YvcC) of 589 aas ( Dalmas et al. 2005 ). The low resolution cryo-electron microscopy reconstitution suggests large conformational changes occur during it's catalytic cycle ( Fribourg et al. 2014 ). Backbone NMR assignments of the nucleotide binding domain of BmrA in the post-hydrolysis state have been determined ( Pérez Carrillo et al. 2022 )…
3.A.1.117.3.name: Multidrug resistance homodimeric efflux pump, BmrA (YvcC) of 589 aas.

3.A.1.119.3.description: Exochelin exporter, ExiT ( Zhu et al. 1998 ).
3.A.1.119.3.name: Exochelin exporter, ExiT.

3.A.1.119.4.description: Putative coelichelin (hydroxamate siderophore) exporter, Sco0493; the gene is in a gene cluster encoding the recognized coelichelin uptake system (TC# 3.A.1.14.12) as well as coelichelin biosynthetic enzymes ( Barona-Gómez et al. 2006). Sco0493 may function together with Sco0540 which is another putative ABC exporter of similar equence (see TC# 3.A.1.119.5). However, alternatively, these two…
3.A.1.119.4.name: Putative coelichelin (hydroxamate siderophore) exporter, Sco0493; the gene is in a gene cluster encoding the recognized coelichelin uptake system…

3.A.1.119.5.description: Putative coelichelin (hydroxamate siderophore) exporter, Sco0493; the gene is in a gene cluster encoding the recognized coelichelin uptake system (TC# 3.A.1.14.12) as well as coelichelin biosynthetic enzymes ( Barona-Gómez et al. 2006). Sco0493 (see TC# 3.A.1.119.4) may function together with Sco0540, both of which are putative ABC exporters of similar sequence. Alternatively, these two genes may…
3.A.1.119.5.name: Putative coelichelin (hydroxamate siderophore) exporter, Sco0493; the gene is in a gene cluster encoding the recognized coelichelin uptake system…

3.A.1.12.name: The Quaternary Amine Uptake Transporter (QAT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.16 and 3.A.1.17)

3.A.1.12.1.description: Glycine betaine/proline porter, ProU or ProVWX (also transports proline betaine, carnitine, dimethyl proline, homobetaine, γ-butyrobetaine and choline with low affinity). Contributes to the regulation of cell volume is response to osmolarity. A reconsituted system shows osmotic strength-gating ( Gul and Poolman 2012 ).
3.A.1.12.1.name: Glycine betaine/proline porter, ProU or ProVWX

3.A.1.12.10.description: The OpuC transporter selective for glycine betaine > choline, acetylcholine, carnitine and proline betaine (contains tandem cystathionine-β-synthase (CBS) domains in the ABC component of OpuC that are required for osmoregulatory function ( Chen and Beattie, 2007 )).
3.A.1.12.10.name: The OpuC transporter selective for glycine betaine > choline, acetylcholine, carnitine and proline betaine

3.A.1.12.11.description: The glycine betaine uptake porter, GbpABCD ( Saum et al. , 2009 ).
3.A.1.12.11.name: The glycine betaine uptake porter, GbpABCD.

3.A.1.12.12.description: The CbcWV/CbcX (choline)/CaiX (carnitine)/BetX (betaine) transporter with 3 binding receptors for distinct quaternary ammonium compounds. Only the ligand-bound receptor binds to the transporter with high affinity ( Chen et al. , 2010 ; Thomas et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.12.12.name: The CbcWV/CbcX (choline)/CaiX (carnitine)/BetX (betaine) transporter with 3 binding receptors for distinct quaternary ammonium compounds.

3.A.1.12.13.description: High affinity (2mμM) choline uptake porter. The choline binding receptor exhibits a venus fly trap mechanism of substrate binding. (ChoX binds acetyl choline and betaine with low affinity (80μM and 470μM, respectively) ( Aktas et al. , 2011 ) (most similar to 3.A.1.12.7)
3.A.1.12.13.name: High affinity (2mμM) choline uptake porter.

3.A.1.12.14.description: OsmU (OsmVWXY) transporter for glycine betaine and choline-O-sulfate uptake. Induced by osmotic stress (0.3M NaCl) ( Frossard et al. , 2012 ). Also called OpuCA/CB1/CB2/CC.
3.A.1.12.14.name: OsmU (OsmVWXY) transporter for glycine betaine and choline-O-sulfate uptake.

3.A.1.12.15.description: Putative osmoprotectant (glycine/betaine/choline) uptake transporter, YehWXYZ. Induced by osmotic stress and growth into the stationary phase; under RpoS (σ S ) control ( Ibanez-Ruiz et al. 2000 ; Checroun and Gutierrez 2004 ). YehZ is also called OsmF.
3.A.1.12.15.name: Putative osmoprotectant (glycine/betaine/choline) uptake transporter, YehWXYZ.

3.A.1.12.16.description: Glycine betaine/carnitine/choline/proline transporter, OpuABC. It is not a dominant proline transporter which in S. aureus are, however, PutP and ProT ( Lehman et al. 2023 ). The sequence of OpuB, the membrane component of the system, is not included here. The 3-d structure of OpuC (or a part of it) has been solved (5IIP_A-D). .
3.A.1.12.16.name: Glycine betaine/carnitine/choline/proline transporter, OpuABC.

3.A.1.12.18.description: Osmoprotectant ABC transporter permease/substrate-binding subunit OpuFB (505 aas, 6 TMSs); The ABC-type ATPase is OpuFA, 318 aas, 0 TMSs). In OpuFB, the permease domain with 6 TMSs is N-terminal while the C-terminal hydrophilic half of the protein is the substrate binding domain.
3.A.1.12.18.name: Osmoprotectant ABC transporter permease/substrate-binding subunit OpuFB (505 aas, 6 TMSs); The ABC-type ATPase is OpuFA, 318 aas, 0 TMSs).

3.A.1.12.19.description: Ergothioheine uptake transporter (ABC-type), EgtUV, of 553 and 213 aas, respectively. While the first has 7 N-terminal TMSs and a binding protein domain C-terminally, EgtV is the ATPase subunit. The system transports human dietary antioxidants and 2-thioimidazole-containing low molecular weight thiol ergothioneine ( Legg et al. 2025 ). OseR, a bacterial redox sensor, regulates ergothioneine…
3.A.1.12.19.name: Ergothioheine uptake transporter (ABC-type), EgtUV, of 553 and 213 aas, respectively.

3.A.1.12.2.description: Glycine betaine OpuAA/AB/AC porter (also transports dimethylsulfonioacetate and dimethylsulfoniopropionate). The system has been reconstituted in nanodiscs and shows substrate-dependent ionic stringth-gated gating and energy coupling dependent on anionic lipids ( Karasawa et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.12.2.name: Glycine betaine OpuAA/AB/AC porter (also transports dimethylsulfonioacetate and dimethylsulfoniopropionate).

3.A.1.12.20.description: Thiol-containing reducing agent transporter, EgtUBC of two proteins, the transmembrane protein of 506 aas and 7 TMSs with a fused external C-terminal binding protein domain, and an ATPase of 242 aas. Ergothioneine (EGT) is a natural betaine amino acid found in various foods, particularly mushrooms ( Wen et al. 2025 ). A review of the antioxidant ergothioneine has appeared, focusing on its…
3.A.1.12.20.name: Thiol-containing reducing agent transporter, EgtUBC of two proteins, the transmembrane protein of 506 aas and 7 TMSs with a fused external C-terminal…

3.A.1.12.4.description: Uptake system for choline, L-carnitine, D-carnitine, glycine betaine, proline betaine, crotonobetaine, γ-butyrobetaine, dimethylsulfonioacetate, dimethylsulfoniopropionate, ectoine and choline-O-sulfate

3.A.1.135.10.description: Uncharacterized two component ABC transporter, both of M-C domain order with 6 N-terminal TMSs. The genes encoding these two proteins are adjacent to a putative ABC transporter of TC# 9.B.29.2.13.
3.A.1.135.10.name: Uncharacterized two component ABC transporter, both of M-C domain order with 6 N-terminal TMSs.

3.A.1.135.12.description: Two component ABC exporter, both subunits with 611 and 600 aas with 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 arrangement. The C-terminal domain is the ATPase
3.A.1.135.12.name: Two component ABC exporter, both subunits with 611 and 600 aas with 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 arrangement.

3.A.1.135.13.description: Two component netropsin resistance ABC netropsin exporter, NetP1/NetP2 ( Stumpp et al. 2005 ).
3.A.1.135.13.name: Two component netropsin resistance ABC netropsin exporter, NetP1/NetP2.

3.A.1.135.2.description: The heterodimeric putative multidrug exporter, RscA/RscB; probably orthologous to YdaG/YbdA (TC #3.A.1.117.4) [Transcription is activated by stress conditions (heat, acid) and repressed by a 2-component system, CovRS ( Dalton et al ., 2006 )]
3.A.1.135.2.name: The heterodimeric putative multidrug exporter, RscA/RscB; probably orthologous to YdaG/YbdA (TC #3.A.1.117.4) [Transcription is activated by stress…

3.A.1.135.3.description: Narrow spectrum fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin) efflux pump, SatAB ( Escudero et al. 2011 ). It is regulated by the two-component system, CiaRH ( Yang et al. 2022 ).
3.A.1.135.3.name: Narrow spectrum fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin) efflux pump, SatAB.

3.A.1.135.4.description: Multidrug resistance ABC exporter, PatAB (PatA, 564 aas; PatB, 588 aas) ( Bidossi et al. 2012 ). Drug-dependent inhibition of nucleotide hydrolysis by PatAB has been demonstrated ( Guffick et al. 2022 ). Ethidium-like inhibition was observed with propidium, novobiocin and coumermycin A1, which all inhibit nucleotide hydrolysis by a non-competitive mechanism. This fact casts light on potential…
3.A.1.135.4.name: Multidrug resistance ABC exporter, PatAB (PatA, 564 aas; PatB, 588 aas).

3.A.1.135.5.description: The hetrodimeric ABC transporter, TM287/TM288. The 2.9-Å crystal structure has been solved in the inward-facing state. The two nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) remain in contact through an interface involving conserved motifs that connect the two ATP hydrolysis sites. AMP-PNP binds to a degenerate catalytic site which deviates from the consensus sequence in the same positions as the eukaryotic…
3.A.1.135.5.name: The hetrodimeric ABC transporter, TM287/TM288.

3.A.1.135.6.description: Two component multidrug efflux pump with the 6 TMS membrane domain preceding the ATPase domain in both proteins. Confers resistance to erythromycin and tetracycline and catalyzes export of Hoechst 33342 ( Moodley et al. 2014 ). Expression is induced by the presence of erythromycin.
3.A.1.135.6.name: Two component multidrug efflux pump with the 6 TMS membrane domain preceding the ATPase domain in both proteins.

3.A.1.135.7.description: Multidrug exporter, EfrAB. Confers resistance to many structurally unrelated antimicrobial agents, such as norfloxacin, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, acriflavine, 4,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole, tetraphenylphosphonium chloride, daunorubicin, and doxorubicin ( Lee et al. 2003 ). Induced by half minimal inhibitory concentrations (MIC) of gentamicin, streptomycin and chloramphenicol which are also…
3.A.1.135.7.name: Multidrug exporter, EfrAB.

3.A.1.135.8.description: Multidrug efflux pump, EfrCD. Exports daunorubicin, doxorubicin, ethidium and Hoechst 33342. Mediates efflux of fluorescent substrates and confers resistance towards multiple dyes and drugs including fluoroquinolones ( Hürlimann et al. 2016 ).
3.A.1.135.8.name: Multidrug efflux pump, EfrCD.

3.A.1.135.9.description: Multidrug exporter, EfrEF. Mediates efflux of fluorescent substrates and confers resistance towards multiple dyes and drugs including fluoroquinolones ( Hürlimann et al. 2016 ).
3.A.1.135.9.name: Multidrug exporter, EfrEF.

3.A.1.136.2.description: ABC-type antimicrobial peptide transporter with a membrane protein of 421 aas and 4 TMSs (Q6MNW8) and an ATPase of encoded by a gene adjacent to the membrane protein (Q6MNW9). Adjacent to these two genes is one annotated as an iron-regluated protein, FrpA (Q6MNW7).
3.A.1.136.2.name: ABC-type antimicrobial peptide transporter with a membrane protein of 421 aas and 4 TMSs (Q6MNW8) and an ATPase of encoded by a gene adjacent to the…

3.A.1.137.2.description: ABC-type antimicrobial peptide transporter of 786 aas and 8 TMSs
3.A.1.137.2.name: ABC-type antimicrobial peptide transporter of 786 aas and 8 TMSs

3.A.1.139.1.description: UDP-glucose exporter, STAR1/STAR2 (sensitive to aluminum rhizotoxicity) (Probable Type I topology) ( Huang et al. 2009 ).
3.A.1.139.1.name: UDP-glucose exporter, STAR1/STAR2 (sensitive to aluminum rhizotoxicity) (Probable Type I topology).

3.A.1.139.2.description: The FetA (YbbL)/FetB (YbbM) iron exporter (SwissProt family UDF0014; 6 or 7 putative TMSs). Expression enhances resistance to oxidative stress ( Nicolaou et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.139.2.name: The FetA (YbbL)/FetB (YbbM) iron exporter (SwissProt family UDF0014; 6 or 7 putative TMSs).

3.A.1.139.4.description: Plasma membrane ABC exporter, sensitive to aluminum rhizotoxicity 1/2, STAR1/STAR2 ( Larsen et al. , 2005 ). Induced in response to aluminum exposure. The system is also called the ALS3/STAR1 ABC transporter that may transport an Al 3+ /Malate complex (). External and internal aluminum resistance by ALS3-dependent STAR1-mediated promotion of STOP1 degradation has been demonstrated ( Fan et al…
3.A.1.139.4.name: Plasma membrane ABC exporter, sensitive to aluminum rhizotoxicity 1/2, STAR1/STAR2.

3.A.1.139.5.description: Uncharacterized protein of 318 aas and 7 TMSs in a 5 + 2 TMS arrangement. An ATPase for this putative porter has not been identified.
3.A.1.139.5.name: Uncharacterized protein of 318 aas and 7 TMSs in a 5 + 2 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.14.name: The Iron Chelate Uptake Transporter (FeCT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.13 and 3.A.1.15)

3.A.1.14.1.description: Iron (Fe 3+ ) or ferric-dicitrate porter, FecBCDE ( Braun and Herrmann, 2007 ). The Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) ortholog has two substrate binding proteins, FecB and FecB2 ( de Miranda et al. 2023 ). The crystallographic structures of Mtb FecB and FecB2 were determined to 2.0 Å and 2.2 Å resolution, respectively, and they show distinct ligand binding pockets. In vitro ligand binding…
3.A.1.14.1.name: Iron (Fe 3+ ) or ferric-dicitrate porter, FecBCDE.

3.A.1.14.10.description: The heme porter, Shp/SiaABC (HtsABC). Shp is a cell surface heme binding protein that transfers the heme directly to HstA ( Nygaard et al ., 2006 ). The crystal structure of the heme binding domain of Shp has been solved ( Aranda et al ., 2007 ). HtsABC is required for the uptake of staphyloferrin A ( Beasley et al. 2009 ). The Shp cell surface heme receptor feeds iron-heme to the transporter in…
3.A.1.14.10.name: The heme porter, Shp/SiaABC (HtsABC).

3.A.1.14.11.description: The molybdate/tungstate ABC transporter, MolABC. For MolC; HI1470(C)/MolB; HI1471(M), the 3D structure is known at 2.4 Å resolution; Pinkett et al ., 2007 ). MolA binds to MolBC with low affinity (50 - 100μM), forming a transient complex that is stabilitzed by ligand binding ( Vigonsky et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.14.11.name: The molybdate/tungstate ABC transporter, MolABC.

3.A.1.14.12.description: Desferrioxamine B uptake porter, DesABC ( Barona-Gomez et al ., 2006 )
3.A.1.14.12.name: Desferrioxamine B uptake porter, DesABC

3.A.1.14.13.description: Ferric iron-coelichelin uptake porter, CchCDEF ( Barona-Gomez et al ., 2006 ).
3.A.1.14.13.name: Ferric iron-coelichelin uptake porter, CchCDEF.

3.A.1.14.14.description: The Fe 3+ /Fe3 + ferrichrome/Fe 3+ heme uptake porter; SiuABDG (FtsABCD) ( Montañez et al. , 2005 ; Hanks et al. 2005 ; Li et al. 2013 ). A similar system has been characterized in S. iniae ( Wang et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.14.14.name: The Fe 3+ /Fe3 + ferrichrome/Fe 3+ heme uptake porter; SiuABDG (FtsABCD).

3.A.1.14.15.description: Uptake transporter for the catecholic trilactone (2, 3-dihydroxybenzoate-glycine-threonine) 3 siderophore bacillibactin (for ferric iron scavenging), FeuABC ( Gaballa and Helmann, 2007 ; Miethke et al ., 2006 ).
3.A.1.14.15.name: Uptake transporter for the catecholic trilactone (2, 3-dihydroxybenzoate-glycine-threonine) 3 siderophore bacillibactin (for ferric iron scavenging)…

3.A.1.14.16.description: The heme-specific uptake porter, HemTUV ( Létoffé et al. , 2008 ).
3.A.1.14.16.name: The heme-specific uptake porter, HemTUV.

3.A.1.14.17.description: Heme acquisition ABC uptake transporter, IsdDEF ( Liu et al ., 2008 )
3.A.1.14.17.name: Heme acquisition ABC uptake transporter, IsdDEF

3.A.1.14.18.description: The heme uptake porter, ShuTUV ( Burkhard and Wilks, 2008 ). Transports a single heme per reaction cycle ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ). (3-d structure of ShuT is known (2RG7).
3.A.1.14.18.name: The heme uptake porter, ShuTUV.

3.A.1.14.19.description: Heme uptake porter, HugBCD ( Villarreal et al. , 2008 ); also called HmuTUV.
3.A.1.14.19.name: Heme uptake porter, HugBCD; also called HmuTUV.

3.A.1.14.20.description: Heme-iron (hemin) utilization transporter BhuTUV ( Brickman et al. , 2006 ; Vanderpool and Armstrong, 2004 ). The crystal structures of BhuUV with or without the periplasmic haem-binding protein BhuT have been solved ( Naoe et al. 2016 ). The TMSs show an inward-facing conformation, in which the cytoplasmic gate of the haem translocation pathway is completely open. Since this conformation is…
3.A.1.14.20.name: Heme-iron (hemin) utilization transporter BhuTUV.

3.A.1.14.21.description: The heme uptake porter, PhuTUV (transports one heme per reaction cycle) ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.14.21.name: The heme uptake porter, PhuTUV (transports one heme per reaction cycle).

3.A.1.14.22.description: The putative ferric iron-desferrioxamine E uptake porter, DesEFGH. The DesE binding receptor has been characterized ( Barona-Gómez et al. 2006 ). The remaining three ( desFGH ) genes cluster together without a gene encoding a receptor (R). They are believed to function with DesE based on sequence similarity and phylogenetic analyses (Getsin et al., 2013).
3.A.1.14.22.name: The putative ferric iron-desferrioxamine E uptake porter, DesEFGH.

3.A.1.14.23.description: Two components of a vitamin B12 (cobalamin) uptake porter, BtuCD. BtuAB must exist but have not been identified ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).
3.A.1.14.23.name: Two components of a vitamin B12 (cobalamin) uptake porter, BtuCD.

3.A.1.14.24.description: FecB1CDE iron siderophore uptake transporter. Transports iron chelated dihydroxamate xenosiderophores, either ferric schizokinen (FeSK) or a ferric siderophore of the filamentous cyanobacterium Anabaena variabilis ATCC 29413 (a schizokinen derivative, SAV), as the sole source of iron in a TonB-dependent manner ( Obando S et al. 2018 ). The gene schT encodes the TonB-dependent outer membrane…
3.A.1.14.24.name: FecB1CDE iron siderophore uptake transporter.

3.A.1.14.25.description: Heme uptake porter with three subunits ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.14.25.name: Heme uptake porter with three subunits.

3.A.1.14.26.description: Cyanocobalamin uptake porter with 3 components, R, M and C ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.14.26.name: Cyanocobalamin uptake porter with 3 components, R, M and C.

3.A.1.14.27.description: Heme transporter with three components, HmuU (M), HmuV (C) and HmuT (R). Chemo-mechanical coupling in the transport cycle has been proposed with outward open, inward open and occluded states ( Tamura et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.14.27.name: Heme transporter with three components, HmuU (M), HmuV (C) and HmuT (R).

3.A.1.14.3.description: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate (ferrichrome, coprogen, aerobactin, ferrioxamine B, schizakinen, rhodotorulic acid) porter, albomycin porter. A FtsZ inhibitor can utilize siderophore-ferric iron uptake transporter systems, FepA, CirA (outer membrane transporters) and FhuBC (inner membrane transporter) for activity against Gram-negative bacterial pathogens ( Bryan et al. 2024 ).
3.A.1.14.3.name: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate (ferrichrome, coprogen, aerobactin, ferrioxamine B, schizakinen, rhodotorulic acid) porter, albomycin porter.

3.A.1.14.5.description: Heme (hemin) uptake porter. The receptor, HmuT, binds two parallel stacked heme molecules, and two are transported per reaction cycle ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.14.5.name: Heme (hemin) uptake porter.

3.A.1.14.7.description: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate porter (transports Fe 3+ -ferrichrome and Fe 3+ -ferrioxamine B with FhuD1, and these compounds plus aerobactin and coprogen with FhuD2). FhuB may function with FhuG (A6QEV8) together with FhuD2 to form a ferrichrome transporter where FhuB and FhuG have conserved arginine residues (R71 and R61, respectively) that form essential salt bridges with FhuD2 ( Vinés et al. 2013…
3.A.1.14.7.name: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate porter

3.A.1.14.8.description: The iron-vibrioferrin uptake porter ( Tanabe et al ., 2003 )
3.A.1.14.8.name: The iron-vibrioferrin uptake porter

3.A.1.14.9.description: The Corrinoid porter, BtuCDE ( Woodson et al ., 2005 )
3.A.1.14.9.name: The Corrinoid porter, BtuCDE

3.A.1.140.1.description: The FtsX/FtsE ABC transporter ( Arends et al., 2009 ) (FtsX is of the type III topology). FtsEX directly recruits EnvC to the septum via an interaction between EnvC and a periplasmic loop of FtsX. FtsEX variants predicted to be ATPase defective still recruit EnvC to the septum but fail to promote cell separation. Amidase activation via EnvC in the periplasm is regulated by conformational changes…
3.A.1.140.1.name: The FtsX/FtsE ABC transporter (FtsX is of the type III topology).

3.A.1.140.2.description: The cell division ABC system, FtsX/FtsE
3.A.1.140.2.name: The cell division ABC system, FtsX/FtsE

3.A.1.140.4.description: Cell division ABC system, FtsXE of 300 aas and 4 TMSs, and 229 aas and 0 TMSs, respectively.
3.A.1.140.4.name: Cell division ABC system, FtsXE of 300 aas and 4 TMSs, and 229 aas and 0 TMSs, respectively.

3.A.1.140.6.description: Cell division system, FtsXE. The FtsEX:PcsB complex forms a molecular machine that carries out peptidoglycan (PG) hydrolysis during normal cell division. FtsEX transduces signals from the cell division apparatus to stimulate PG hydrolysis by PcsB, an amidase, which interacts with extracellular domains of FtsX ( Bajaj et al. 2016 ).
3.A.1.140.6.name: Cell division system, FtsXE.

3.A.1.140.8.description: FtsEX of Bacillus subtilis where FtsE is an ATPase of 228 aas (O34814) and FtsX is a dimeric membrane protein of 296 aas and 4 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS arrangement (O34876). It is an ABC transporter secondarily involved in sporulation. It was initially thought to act as an importer and/or exporter, possibly at the top of a hierarchical cascade leading to the correct temporal initiation of sporulation…
3.A.1.140.8.name: FtsEX of Bacillus subtilis where FtsE is an ATPase of 228 aas (O34814) and FtsX is a dimeric membrane protein of 296 aas and 4 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS…

3.A.1.141.name: The Ethyl Viologen Exporter (EVE) Family (DUF990 Family)

3.A.1.141.1.description: The ethyl (methyl; benzyl) viologen export pump, EvrABC (EvrB and EvrC of 6 TMSs are members of the large DUF990 superfamily ( Prosecka et al. , 2009 ); They appear to be of the ABC-2 topological type).
3.A.1.141.1.name: The ethyl (methyl; benzyl) viologen export pump, EvrABC

3.A.1.142.2.description: ABC exporter, YvfS/YvfR of 284 and 287 aas, respectively
3.A.1.142.2.name: ABC exporter, YvfS/YvfR of 284 and 287 aas, respectively

3.A.1.142.3.description: Uncharacterized ABC2 exporter consisting of a 6 TMS membrane protein of 254 aas and an ATPase, encoded by the gene adjacent to the 6 TMS membrane protein.
3.A.1.142.3.name: Uncharacterized ABC2 exporter consisting of a 6 TMS membrane protein of 254 aas and an ATPase, encoded by the gene adjacent to the 6 TMS membrane…

3.A.1.143.1.description: The exoprotein (including α-amylase) secretion system, EcsAB(C) ( Leskelä et al. , 1999 ). Also may play roles in sporulation, competence ( Leskelä et al. , 1996 ) and transformation using purified DNA ( Takeno et al. , 2011 ). An involvement of EcsC in transport is not established, but it is similar in sequence to the C-terminus of the P-type ATPase, 3.A.3.31.2.
3.A.1.143.1.name: The exoprotein (including α-amylase) secretion system, EcsAB(C).

3.A.1.144.1.description: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #1. This system is encoded by two genes that overlap and are therefore probably translationally coupled; they are in the same operon with the genes for 2.A.1.144.2.
3.A.1.144.1.name: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #1.

3.A.1.144.2.description: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #2. This system is encoded by two genes that overlap and are therefore probably translationally coupled; they are in the same operon with the genes for 2.A.1.144.1.
3.A.1.144.2.name: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #2.

3.A.1.146.1.name: The probable actinorhodin (ACT) and undecylprodigiosin (RED) exporter , AreABCD (Sco3956-9).

3.A.1.147.1.description: Putative two component ABC exporter with a membrane protein of 573 aas and 12 TMSs and an ATPase encoded adjacent to the membrane protein and also adjacent to a gene encoding an adenine glycosylase, probably within a single operon.
3.A.1.147.1.name: Putative two component ABC exporter with a membrane protein of 573 aas and 12 TMSs and an ATPase encoded adjacent to the membrane protein and also…

3.A.1.147.2.description: Putative 2-component sporulation-related ABC exporter. The genes encoding this system are adjacent to a spore germination receptor (TC# 2.A.3.9.5) and a putative signalling molecule transporter (2.A.86.1.11) .
3.A.1.147.2.name: Putative 2-component sporulation-related ABC exporter.

3.A.1.148.4.description: Uncharacterized ABC transporter, AbcYZ [Y (D2BBE4) = M with 6 TMSs; Z (D2BBE3)= C.]
3.A.1.148.4.name: Uncharacterized ABC transporter, AbcYZ [Y (D2BBE4) = M with 6 TMSs; Z (D2BBE3)= C.]

3.A.1.15.name: The Manganese/Zinc/Iron Chelate Uptake Transporter (MZT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.12, 3.A.1.14 and 3.A.1.16)

3.A.1.15.10.description: The Mn 2+ /Zn 2+ transporter MntABC (K B of Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ is 0.1μM which bind with equal affinity to the same site ( Lim et al ., 2008 )
3.A.1.15.10.name: The Mn 2+ /Zn 2+ transporter MntABC

3.A.1.15.11.description: The zinc uptake porter, YcdHI-YceA; AdcA/AdcC/AdcB ( Gaballa et al. , 2002 ).
3.A.1.15.11.name: The zinc uptake porter, YcdHI-YceA; AdcA/AdcC/AdcB.

3.A.1.15.12.description: Metal ion (probably iron) uptake permease , YtgABC-RD. The third gene in the ytg operon is fused, the N-terminal membrane domain being fused to the C-terminal transcriptional regulator homologous to the diphtheria toxin repressor, DtxR. These two domains may be proteolitically processed yielding the two active proteins ( Thompson et al. 2012 ).
3.A.1.15.12.name: Metal ion (probably iron) uptake permease , YtgABC-RD.

3.A.1.15.13.description: The ZnuA18/ZnuA08/ZnuB/ZnuC zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake system ( Hudek et al. 2013 ). ZnuB (M) and ZnuC (C) can function with either of two zinc ion receptors, ZnuA18 (R) which is encoded in the znuACB operon, and ZnuA08 (R) which is encoded elsewhere on the chromosome. ZnuA18 is more efficient that ZnuA08 in promoting uptake ( Hudek et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.15.13.name: The ZnuA18/ZnuA08/ZnuB/ZnuC zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake system.

3.A.1.15.14.description: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, PsaABC ( Lisher et al. 2013 ). The crystal structure of the manganese transporter PsaBC from Streptococcus pneumoniae has been solved in an open-inward conformation ( Neville et al. 2021 ). The type II transporter has a tightly closed transmembrane channel due to "extracellular gating" residues that prevent water permeation and ion reflux. Below these residues…
3.A.1.15.14.name: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, PsaABC.

3.A.1.15.15.description: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, MntABC. The 3-d structure of MntC has been solved to 2.2Å resolution ( Gribenko et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.15.15.name: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, MntABC.

3.A.1.15.18.description: ABC high affinity Zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake porter, ZnuABC. The similar system from Y. pestis has been characterized ( Bobrov et al. 2014 ; Neupane et al. 2018 ). ZnuA (R) of that systems can bind up to 5 zinc ions with high affinity.
3.A.1.15.18.name: ABC high affinity Zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake porter, ZnuABC.

3.A.1.15.19.description: Zinc ion ABC uptake system, AztABCD, where AztD is a periplasmic chaparone protein that feeds Zn 2+ into AztC, the periplasmic receptor/binding protein for the transporter ( Neupane et al. 2018 ).
3.A.1.15.19.name: Zinc ion ABC uptake system, AztABCD, where AztD is a periplasmic chaparone protein that feeds Zn 2+ into AztC, the periplasmic receptor/binding…

3.A.1.15.20.description: ABC uptake transporter specific for Mn 2+ and Fe 2+ , SloABC ( Paik et al. 2003 ). The system is repressed by Mn 2+ together with the SloR repressor, encoded by a gene downstream of sloABC .
3.A.1.15.20.name: ABC uptake transporter specific for Mn 2+ and Fe 2+ , SloABC.

3.A.1.15.21.description: Mn 2+ ABC uptake system, MntABC. Titratable transmembrane residues and a hydrophobic plug are essential for manganese import via the Bacillus anthracis ABC transporter MntBC-A ( Kuznetsova et al. 2021 ). Zinc is a high-affinity inhibitor. The transmembrane metal permeation pathway is lined with six titratable residues that can coordinate the positively charged metal, and mutagenesis studies…
3.A.1.15.21.name: Mn 2+ ABC uptake system, MntABC.

3.A.1.15.4.description: Iron, Manganese (and Zinc) (Fe 2+ , Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ ) porter, YfeABCD. The periplasmic receptor, YfeA binds Zn(II) ions as a preferred substrate, even though the YfeABCD system most likely does not transport zinc ( Orzel et al. 2026 ). YfeA possesses two metal-binding sites. Site 2 was shown to bind Zn(II) and Mn(II), but not Fe(II) ions. Orzel et al. 2026 investigated the metal-binding…
3.A.1.15.4.name: Iron, Manganese (and Zinc) (Fe 2+ , Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ ) porter, YfeABCD.

3.A.1.15.5.description: Zinc (Zn 2+ ) porter of E. coli , ZnuABC. Required for Zn 2+ homeostasis and virulence in the close E. coli relative, Salmonella enterica (Ammendola et al ., 2007 ).
3.A.1.15.5.name: Zinc (Zn 2+ ) porter of E. coli , ZnuABC.

3.A.1.15.7.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) (Km=0.1 μM) and iron (Fe 2+ ) (5 μM) porter (inhibited by Cd 2+ > Co 2+ > Ni 2+ , Cu 2+ ) (most similar to YfeABCD of Yersinia pestis (TC #3.A.1.15.4)). Important for virulence in Salmonella ( Karlinsey et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.15.7.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) (Km=0.1 μM) and iron (Fe 2+ ) (5 μM) porter (inhibited by Cd 2+ > Co 2+ > Ni 2+ , Cu 2+ )

3.A.1.15.8.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ), zinc (Zn 2+ ) and possibly iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake porter, TroABCD ( Hazlett et al ., 2003 ). Transcription of the operon is controlled by the Mn 2+ -activated (not Zn 2+ - or Fe 2+ -activated) repressor, TroR (153 aas, acc# F7IW50;) TroR contains a metal-binding domain homologous to the YtgC-R protein (3.A.1.15.12) which has the membrane domain of this ABC transporter…
3.A.1.15.8.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ), zinc (Zn 2+ ) and possibly iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake porter, TroABCD.

3.A.1.15.9.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) and Iron (Fe 2+ ) porter, SitABCD ( Davies and Walker, 2007 ). Both this system and the MntH system in Agrobacterium tumefaciens , both Mn 2+ transporters, are stronly inhibited by thymol and carvacrol, constituents of plant thyme white essential oils ( Jung et al. 2025 ). Other oil constituents are also inhibitory ( Jung et al. 2025 ).
3.A.1.15.9.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) and Iron (Fe 2+ ) porter, SitABCD.

3.A.1.152.1.description: LPS export system, LptF (M), LptG (M) and LptB (C). This system is also listed in TCDB under TC#1.B.42.1.2 as part of a multicomponent system. The entire system is described in detail there. LptB 2 FG extracts LPSs from the IM and transports them to the outer membrane. Luo et al. 2017 reported the crystal structure of nucleotide-free LptB2FG from P. aeruginosa . It shows that LPS transport…
3.A.1.152.1.name: LPS export system, LptF (M), LptG (M) and LptB (C).

3.A.1.152.10.description: Probable LptF/G or YjgP/Q membrane proteins of an ABC exporter, possibly specific for a lipopolysaccharide. Adjacent genes code for proteases/peptidases. Members of this family often work together with outer…
3.A.1.152.10.name: Probable LptF/G or YjgP/Q membrane proteins of an ABC exporter, possibly specific for a lipopolysaccharide.

3.A.1.152.2.description: Putative ABC exporter of the YjgP/Q (LptFG) family. The membrane protein has 772 aas and 12 TMSs in a (3 + 3) 2 duplicated topology. The gene adjacent to this membrane protein gene encodes an ABC1 ATPase of 583 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs with a C-terminal ATPase domain. Most ATPases of family 3.A.1.152 are of the ABC2-type. Thus, it is unlikely that this protein serves to energized the…
3.A.1.152.2.name: Putative ABC exporter of the YjgP/Q (LptFG) family.

3.A.1.152.3.description: Uncharacterized ABC system of the YjgP/Q family; the two membrane proteins are encoded by adjacent genes, but the gene for the ATPase was not found. However, a soluble OstA homologue (Q5SL97) of 824 aas is encoded adjacent to the two membrane protein-encoding genes.
3.A.1.152.3.name: Uncharacterized ABC system of the YjgP/Q family; the two membrane proteins are encoded by adjacent genes, but the gene for the ATPase was not found.

3.A.1.152.4.description: Uncharacterized YjgP/YjgQ family homologue of 441 aas and 6 TMSs. No other YjgP homologue and no ATPase is encoded adjacent to the gene encoding this protein.
3.A.1.152.4.name: Uncharacterized YjgP/YjgQ family homologue of 441 aas and 6 TMSs.

3.A.1.152.5.description: Uncharacterized YjgP/Q homologue of 266 aas and 6 TMSs. No ATPase or another YjgP homologue is encoded by a gene adjacent to this one.
3.A.1.152.5.name: Uncharacterized YjgP/Q homologue of 266 aas and 6 TMSs.

3.A.1.152.7.description: YjgP/Q family protein of 392 aas and 6 TMSs
3.A.1.152.7.name: YjgP/Q family protein of 392 aas and 6 TMSs

3.A.1.152.9.description: Lipopolysaccharide transporter that exports LPS from the external surface of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer membrane, LptB 2 FG. The 134-kDa protein complex is unique among ABC transporters because it extracts lipopolysaccharide from the external leaflet of the inner membrane and propels it along a filament that extends across the periplasm to directly deliver lipopolysaccharide into the…
3.A.1.152.9.name: Lipopolysaccharide transporter that exports LPS from the external surface of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer membrane, LptB 2 FG.

3.A.1.153.1.description: ABC transporter complex YtrBCD that may play a role in acetoin utilization during stationary phase and sporulation ( Yoshida et al. 2000 ). Expression is induced early in the stationary phase. The six ytr genes form a single operon, transcribed from a promoter present upstream of ytrA. YtrA, which possesses a helix-turn-helix motif of the GntR family, may be a repressor that regulates its own…
3.A.1.153.1.name: ABC transporter complex YtrBCD that may play a role in acetoin utilization during stationary phase and sporulation.

3.A.1.156.3.description: ABC2 transporter of unknown substrate specificity with two membrane constituents and one ATPase.
3.A.1.156.3.name: ABC2 transporter of unknown substrate specificity with two membrane constituents and one ATPase.

3.A.1.158.2.description: Putative ABC-type multidrug transport system with 3 protein components.
3.A.1.158.2.name: Putative ABC-type multidrug transport system with 3 protein components.

3.A.1.159.2.description: Putative 12 TMS ABC permease of 534 aas, HalU ( Besse et al. 2015 ). The gene adjacent to the membrane protein gene is the putative ATPase gene.
3.A.1.159.2.name: Putative 12 TMS ABC permease of 534 aas, HalU.

3.A.1.16.name: The Nitrate/Nitrite/Cyanate Uptake Transporter (NitT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.12 and 3.A.1.17)

3.A.1.16.1.description: Four component nitrate/nitrite porter ( Kikuchi et al. 1996 ). It's synthesis occurs in response to nitrite, not nitrate in a nitrate reductase mutant ( Kikuchi et al. 1996 ).
3.A.1.16.1.name: Four component nitrate/nitrite porter.

3.A.1.16.2.description: Bispecific cyanate/nitrite transporter (functions in both cyanate and nitrite assimilation; Maeda and Omata, 2009 ).
3.A.1.16.2.name: Bispecific cyanate/nitrite transporter.

3.A.1.16.4.name: Nitrate uptake system, NrtABCD.

3.A.1.160.1.description: ABC transporter probably with 2 subunits, PmtCD, an integral membrane protein with 6 TMSs and 251 aas, and an ATP binding and hydrolyzing subunit with 290 aas and 0 TMSs. It is a modulin exporter. This system shows…
