3.A.1.17.10.description: Aliphatic sulfonate (alkanesulfonate) import permease, SsuABC (YcbOEM) and is regluated by the transcriptional activator, Cbl ( van Der Ploeg et al. 1999 ; Eichhorn and Leisinger 2001 ).
3.A.1.17.10.name: Aliphatic sulfonate (alkanesulfonate) import permease, SsuABC (YcbOEM) and is regluated by the transcriptional activator, Cbl.

3.A.1.17.11.description: Putative ABC transporter specific for riboflavin, RibXYZ. RibY is called " NMT1/THI5 like domain protein" ( Anderson et al. 2015 ).
3.A.1.17.11.name: Putative ABC transporter specific for riboflavin, RibXYZ.

3.A.1.17.12.description: Sulfonate and sulfonate ester uptake transporter, SsuABC ( Koch et al. 2005 ).
3.A.1.17.12.name: Sulfonate and sulfonate ester uptake transporter, SsuABC.

3.A.1.17.13.description: Putative thiamine (vitamin B 1 )-specific transporter, ThiXYZ ( Rodionova et al. 2015 ).
3.A.1.17.13.name: Putative thiamine (vitamin B 1 )-specific transporter, ThiXYZ.

3.A.1.17.14.description: Riboflavin uptake porter, RibXY (RibX, 168 aas and 6 TMSs; RibY, 351 aas) ( Gutiérrez-Preciado et al. 2015 ).
3.A.1.17.14.name: Riboflavin uptake porter, RibXY (RibX, 168 aas and 6 TMSs; RibY, 351 aas).

3.A.1.17.3.description: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch. Potentially takes up a pyrimidine moiety of thiamin.
3.A.1.17.3.name: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ.

3.A.1.17.4.description: The taurine uptake system, TauABC ( Krejcík et al. , 2008 ).

3.A.1.17.5.description: The phthalate uptake system, OphFGH ( Chang et al. 2009 ).
3.A.1.17.5.name: The phthalate uptake system, OphFGH.

3.A.1.17.6.description: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch. Potentially takes up a pyrimidine moiety of thiamin. ThiY is homologous to the yeast THI5 HMP-P synthase (P43534) ( Bale et al. , 2010 ).
3.A.1.17.6.name: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ.

3.A.1.17.7.description: Putative riboflavin transport system, RibXY. Regulated by an FMN riboswitch ( Vitreschak et al. 2002 ).
3.A.1.17.7.name: Putative riboflavin transport system, RibXY.

3.A.1.17.8.description: Putative thiamine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch.
3.A.1.17.8.name: Putative thiamine transport system, ThiXYZ.

3.A.1.17.9.description: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 733 aas and 12 TMSs. The other constituents of the system have not been identified.
3.A.1.17.9.name: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 733 aas and 12 TMSs.

3.A.1.18.1.description: Putative ECF transporter, EcfSTA; regulated by a cobalamin riboswitch.
3.A.1.18.1.name: Putative ECF transporter, EcfSTA; regulated by a cobalamin riboswitch.

3.A.1.19.name: The Thiamin Uptake Transporter (ThiT) Family (Most similar to 3.A.1.10, 3.A.1.6 and 3.A.1.8 in that order)

3.A.1.19.1.description: Thiamin, thiamin monophosphate and thiamin pyrophosphate porter. The 2.25 Å structure of ThiB (TbpA) has been solved ( Soriano et al ., 2008 ).
3.A.1.19.1.name: Thiamin, thiamin monophosphate and thiamin pyrophosphate porter.

3.A.1.19.2.description: The thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) uptake porter ( Bian et al. , 2011 ).
3.A.1.19.2.name: The thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) uptake porter.

3.A.1.19.3.description: ABC transporter of unknown function. The three genes encoding this system are adjacent to a gene homologous to a mycothiol maleylpyruvate isomerase.
3.A.1.19.3.name: ABC transporter of unknown function.

3.A.1.19.4.description: The putative sulfate/thiosulfate transporter, YnjBCD. YnjB has 12 TMSs. The three genes encoding this system are adjacent to one encoding a thiosulfate:sulfur transferase or a rhodanese (B7L6N1). Also considered to be a thiamine transporter ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).
3.A.1.19.4.name: The putative sulfate/thiosulfate transporter, YnjBCD.

3.A.1.19.5.description: Putative ABC transporter, WtpB1/C1: molybdate/tungstate transport system.
3.A.1.19.5.name: Putative ABC transporter, WtpB1/C1: molybdate/tungstate transport system.

3.A.1.2.1.description: Ribose porter. RbsA has two ATPase domains fused together; RbsB is the substrate receptor; RbsC has 10 TMSs with N- and C-termini in the cytoplasm and forms a dimer ( Stewart and Hermodson, 2003 ). ABC importers can be divided into two classes. Type I importers follow an alternating access mechanism driven by the presence of the substrate. 3.A.1.2.10.description: The purine nucleoside permease (probably transports guanosine, adenosine, 2'-deoxyguanosine, inosine and xanthosine with decreasing affinity in this order) ( Deka et al ., 2006 )

3.A.1.2.11.name: The erythritol permease, EryEFG (probably orthologous to 3.A.1.2.16)

3.A.1.2.14.description: Putative L-arabinose porter ( Rodionov et al. 2010 ).

NupA is 506aas with two ABC (C) domains. NupB has 8 predicted TMSs, NupC has 9 or 10 predicted TMSs in a 4 + 1 (or 2) + 4 arrangement.
3.A.1.2.17.name: General nucleoside uptake porter, NupABC/BmpA (transports all common nucleosides as well as 5-fluorocytidine, inosine, deoxyuridine and xanthosine)…

3.A.1.2.18.description: Xylose porter ( Nanavati et al. 2006 ). Regulated by xylose-responsive regulator XylR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).
3.A.1.2.18.name: Xylose porter.

3.A.1.2.19.description: D-ribose porter ( Nanavati et al. , 2006 ). Induced by ribose ( Conners et al. , 2005 ).
3.A.1.2.19.name: D-ribose porter.

3.A.1.2.20.description: Glucose porter. Also bind xylose ( Boucher and Noll 2011 ). Induced by glucose ( Frock et al. 2012 ). Directly regulated by glucose-responsive regulator GluR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).
3.A.1.2.20.name: Glucose porter.

3.A.1.2.21.description: The myoinositol (high affinity)/ D-ribose (low affinity) transporter IatP/IatA/IbpA. The structure of IbpA with myoinositol bound has been solved ( Herrou and Crosson 2013 ).
3.A.1.2.21.name: The myoinositol (high affinity)/ D-ribose (low affinity) transporter IatP/IatA/IbpA.

3.A.1.2.22.description: ABC sugar transporter that plays a role in the probiotic benefits through acetate production ( Fukuda et al. 2012 ).
3.A.1.2.22.name: ABC sugar transporter that plays a role in the probiotic benefits through acetate production.

3.A.1.2.23.description: ABC sugar transporter, FruEFGK, important for the probiotic effect of Bifidobacterium longum and involved in producing acetate ( Fukuda et al. 2012 ). The system is specific for fructose (highest affinity) ribose and xylose. All three sugars induce the system ( Wei et al. 2012 ).
3.A.1.2.23.name: ABC sugar transporter, FruEFGK, important for the probiotic effect of Bifidobacterium longum and involved in producing acetate.

3.A.1.2.24.description: XylFGH downstream of characterized transcriptional regulator, ROK7B7 (Sco6008); XylF (Sco6009); XylG (Sco6010); XylH (Sco6011)) ( Świątek et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.2.24.name: XylFGH downstream of characterized transcriptional regulator, ROK7B7 (Sco6008); XylF (Sco6009); XylG (Sco6010); XylH (Sco6011)).

3.A.1.2.25.name: Putative sugar uptake porter, YtfQRT/YjfF.

3.A.1.2.26.description: Xylose transporter, XylFGH (XylF (R), 359 aas; XylG (C), 525 aas; XylH (M), 389 aas. Controlled by a 3 component sensor kinase/response regulator system (XylFII, sensor, A6LW07; LytS, SK, A6LW08; YesN, RR, A6LW09) ( Sun et al. 2015 ). The XylFII-LytS complex provides the molecular basis for D-xylose utilization and metabolic modification ( Li et al. 2017 ).
3.A.1.2.26.name: Xylose transporter, XylFGH

3.A.1.2.28.description: Riboflavin uptake ABC transporter, RfuABCD. The periplasmic binding protein (RfuA) has been crystallized at 1.3 Å resolution with riboflavin bound ( Deka et al. 2013 ). Similar systems are found in other spirochetes such as Treponema denticola , and Borrelia burgdorferi ( Deka et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.2.28.name: Riboflavin uptake ABC transporter, RfuABCD.

When FruR is eliminated, the cells become hypersensitive to fructose, and the level of fruABC expression is much higher than in the…
3.A.1.2.29.name: High affinity fructose uptake porter, FrtABC, Km (fructose) = ~100μM; expression of the frtABC operon is regulated by the product of the upstream…

3.A.1.2.31.description: Putative purine porter with 4 components ( Chandravanshi et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.2.31.name: Putative purine porter with 4 components.

3.A.1.2.32.description: ABC-type putative arabinose transport system, AraEGHP. The genes encoding this system are found within a large gene cluster including many arabinose/pentose metabolic enzymes, a sensor kinase/response regulator pair, and an ABC uptake system specific for araino-oligosaccharides of 2 to 8 sugar units (TC# 3.A.1.1.57) ( Lansky et al. 2020 ).
3.A.1.2.32.name: ABC-type putative arabinose transport system, AraEGHP.

3.A.1.2.33.description: XylFGH of T. ethanolicus ( Erbeznik et al. 2004 ).

3.A.1.2.6.description: D-allose porter. The structure of AlsB has been solved at 1.8 Å resolution ( Chaudhuri et al. 1999 ). Ten residues from both the domains form 14 hydrogen bonds with the sugar. 6-Deoxy-allose, 3-deoxy-glucose and ribose bind with reduced affinity so AlbP can function as a low affinity transporter for D-ribose ( Chaudhuri et al. 1999 ).
3.A.1.2.6.name: D-allose porter.

3.A.1.2.8.description: Autoinducer-2 (AI-2, a furanosyl borate diester: (3aS,6S,6aR)-2,2,6,6a-tetrahydroxy-3a-methyltetrahydrofuro[3,2-d][1,3,2]dioxaborolan-2-uide) uptake porter ( Taga et al ., 2001 , 2003 )

3.A.1.2.9.description: Rhamnose porter ( Richardson et al ., 2004 ) (Transport activity is dependent on rhamnokinase (RhaK; AAQ92412) activity ( Richardson and Oresnik, 2007 ) This could be an example of group translocation!)
3.A.1.2.9.name: Rhamnose porter (Transport activity is dependent on rhamnokinase (RhaK; AAQ92412) activity This could be an example of group translocation!)

3.A.1.20.1.description: The iron transporter, BitABCDEF ( Dugourd et al. 1999 ).
3.A.1.20.1.name: The iron transporter, BitABCDEF.

3.A.1.20.2.description: Hexose-phosphate transporter. Transports glucose-6-phosphate (Km = 0.3 υM) and fructose-6-phosphate (1.3 υM). Sugar phsophates can be used as both carbon and phosphate sources ( Moisi et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.20.2.name: Hexose-phosphate transporter.

3.A.1.20.3.description: Iron (Fe 3+ ) uptake porter, AfuABC (FbpABC) ( Chin et al. 1996 ). AfuA has been characterized ( Willemsen et al. 1997 ).
3.A.1.20.3.name: Iron (Fe 3+ ) uptake porter, AfuABC (FbpABC).

3.A.1.20.4.description: Putative glycerol phosphodiester uptake transporter. The three genes encoding this system are in an operon with a gene encoding a glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase, providing the evidence that this transporter might function to take up such substrates.
3.A.1.20.4.name: Putative glycerol phosphodiester uptake transporter.

3.A.1.20.5.description: A Mg 2+ -citrate uptake porter with three components, R, M and C, as suggested by Mandal et al. 2019 . This system alao be a ferric iron uptake system, based on sequence similarity studies (see other members of TC sub-family 3.A.1.20). The substrate binding protein, MctA, of the system, has been studied with and without Mg-citrate, and the 3-D structure at up to 1.63 Å resolution, indicating that…
3.A.1.20.5.name: A Mg 2+ -citrate uptake porter with three components, R, M and C, as suggested by Mandal et al. 2019.

3.A.1.201.1.description: Broad specificity multidrug resistance (MDR1; MDR-1; Pgp; P-gp; ABCB1; P-glycoprotein) efflux pump. It exports organic cations and amphiphilic compounds of unrelated chemical structure. These include: antibiotics, anti-viral agents, cancer chemotheraputic agents, hypertensives, depressants, histamines, emetics, and the protease inhibitor, lopinavir. 3.A.1.201.10.name: Mdr1; resistance to Cilofungin and other drugs

3.A.1.201.11.description: Mdr1 azole resistance efflux pump ( Lamping et al. , 2010 ). Antifungal activity of the repurposed drug disulfiram against Cryptococcus neoformans has been studied ( Peng et al. 2023 ).
3.A.1.201.11.name: Mdr1 azole resistance efflux pump.

3.A.1.201.12.description: California mussel ABCB/MDR multixenobiotic resistance efflux pump ( Luckenbach and Epel, 2008 ).
3.A.1.201.12.name: California mussel ABCB/MDR multixenobiotic resistance efflux pump.

3.A.1.201.14.description: P-glycoprotein-1 MDR exporter. Transports multiple drugs, cancer chemotherapy agents, cancer unrelated compounds and many xenobiotics including ivermectin ( Ardelli 2013 ). The crystal structure at 3.4 A resolution is available ( Jin et al. 2012 ). It has 4,000x higher affinity for actinomycin D in the membrane bilayers than in detergent. A "ball and socket joint" and salt bridges similar to ABC…
3.A.1.201.14.name: P-glycoprotein-1 MDR exporter.

3.A.1.211.3.description: Multidrug resistance pump, ABCA2 (ABC2). Mediates trafficking of LDL-derived free cholesterol ( Voloshyna and Reiss, 2011 ). Transports endogenous lipids such as myelin ( Soichi et al. 2007 ). It transports liipids ( Wang et al. 2026 ).
3.A.1.211.3.name: Multidrug resistance pump, ABCA2 (ABC2).

3.A.1.211.4.description: The aced cell death 7 (ced-7) protein (translocates molecules that mediate adhesion between dying and engulfing embryonic cells during programmed death).
3.A.1.211.4.name: The aced cell death 7 (ced-7) protein

3.A.1.211.5.description: The surfactant-secreting porter, ABCA3 (exports lipids and proteins into lamellar bodies). Fatal surfactant deficiency (FSD) can result from mutations in ABCA3, causing abnormal intracellular localization (type I) or decreased ATP hydrolysis (type II). Other mutations cause pediatric interstitial lung disease (pILD) ( Matsumura et al. 2008 ). ABCA3 is found in lamellar bodies of lung alveolar…
3.A.1.211.5.name: The surfactant-secreting porter, ABCA3 (exports lipids and proteins into lamellar bodies).

3.A.1.211.6.description: Xenobiotic transporter, ABCA8. It transports estradiol-β-glucuronide, taurocholate, LTC4, para-amino-hippurate, ochratoxin-A and hydrophilic drugs ( Tsuruoka et al ., 2002 ), ( Sakamoto et al. 2019 ). A novel pathway in ABCA8-regulated inhibition of human hepatocellular carcinoma tumorigenesis and metastasis has been identified ( Cui et al. 2020 ).
3.A.1.211.6.name: Xenobiotic transporter, ABCA8.

3.A.1.211.8.description: AbcA12 Keratinocyte lipid transporter. Transports lipids in lamellar granules to the apical surface of granular layer keratinocytes. Extracellular lipids, including ceramide, are thought to be essential for skin barrier function. ABCA12 mutations underlie the three main types of autosomal recessive congenital ichthyoses: harlequin ichthyosis, lamellar ichthyosis and congenital ichthyosiform…
3.A.1.211.8.name: AbcA12 Keratinocyte lipid transporter.

3.A.1.211.9.description: ABCA5 of 1642 aas and 12 TMSs. It is related to lysosomal diseases and plays important roles, especially in cardiomyocytes and follicular cells ( Kubo et al. 2005 ). It mediates cholesterol efflux to HDL3 ( Voloshyna and Reiss, 2011 ) and functions in autolysosomes ( Sakamoto et al. 2019 ).
3.A.1.211.9.name: ABCA5 of 1642 aas and 12 TMSs.

3.A.1.212.1.description: The mitochondrial peptide exporter, Mdl1p (exports peptides of 6-21 amino acyl residues from the mitochondrial matrix as well as degradation products of misassembled respiratory chain complexes) ( Janas et al ., 2003 ; van der Does et al ., 2006 ; Gompf et al ., 2007 ). A leaderless Mdl1p targets to the ER membrane instead of to the mitochondria ( Gompf et al ., 2007 ).
3.A.1.212.1.name: The mitochondrial peptide exporter, Mdl1p

3.A.1.212.2.description: ABC mitochondrial peptide/MDR half transporter, MdlB. High copy number suppressor of ATM1 [iron-sulfur cluster transporter (3.A.1.210.1)]
3.A.1.212.2.name: ABC mitochondrial peptide/MDR half transporter, MdlB.

3.A.1.212.4.description: Mitochondrial inner membrane ABC transporter of 805 aas and 6 TMSs near the N-terminus of the protein, MDL1. Mdl1 is involved in conidial germination, virulence, and resistance to anilinopyrimidine fungicides in Botrytis cinerea ( Fan et al. 2023 ).
3.A.1.212.4.name: Mitochondrial inner membrane ABC transporter of 805 aas and 6 TMSs near the N-terminus of the protein, MDL1.

3.A.1.22.1.description: Putative nickel (Ni 2+ ) and/or Cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter with 4 components, CbiKMQO. CbiM and CbiQ probably have 6 TMSs, but TMSs 3 and 4 are close together.
3.A.1.22.1.name: Putative nickel (Ni 2+ ) and/or Cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter with 4 components, CbiKMQO.

3.A.1.22.2.description: The ABC exporter, CbiMNQ 1 O 1. CbiM and CbiQ1 both have 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.
3.A.1.22.2.name: The ABC exporter, CbiMNQ 1 O 1.

3.A.1.23.2.description: Putative cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter ( Chen and Burne, 2003 )
3.A.1.23.2.name: Putative cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter

It possesses an additional TMS at its N-terminal region not present on other ECF transporter of known structure, resulting in an extracellular N-terminus. The highly conserved N-terminal loop inserts into the center of NikM2 and occludes a…
3.A.1.23.4.name: The NikM2 (230 aas; 5 TMSs)/NikN2 (110 aas; 2 TMSs) pair is part or all of a nickel transporter.

3.A.1.23.5.description: Putative Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, NikMNOQ ( Yu et al. 2013 ).
3.A.1.23.5.name: Putative Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, NikMNOQ.

Substrate binding (S) components rotate within the membrane to expose their binding pockets alternately to the exterior and the cytoplasm. In contrast to vitamin transporters…
3.A.1.23.6.name: Cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter.

3.A.1.23.7.description: Ni 2+ , Co 2+ uptake transporter, NikMNOQ (subunit sizes: NikMN, 347 aas, 9 TMSs; NikQ, 284 aas, 4 TMSs; NikO, 254 aas, 0 TMS. NikMN can take up Ni 2+ without NikQ or NikO ( Kirsch and Eitinger 2014 ).

3.A.1.24.5.name: L-Histidine uptake porter, MetIQN

However the similarity with the methionine transporter of Streptococcus mutans (TC# 3.A.1.24.3) suggests that this porter may also be a methionine uptake porter.
3.A.1.24.6.name: Putative peptide transporter, PepABC.

3.A.1.25.1.description: The biotin uptake porter (binding receptor lacking) (see also the VUT or ECF family; BioY; 2.A.88.1.1) ( Rodionov et al ., 2006 ; Hebbeln et al ., 2007 ). 3.A.1.25.1.name: The biotin uptake porter (binding receptor lacking) (see also the VUT or ECF family; BioY; 2.A.88.1.1).

BioY alone binds biotin but doesn''t transport it ( Berntsson et al. , 2012 ). Ala-Arg-Ser and…
3.A.1.25.4.name: The biotin uptake system, BioMNY.

3.A.1.25.5.description: Biotin/Riboflavin ECF transport system, EcfAA'T/RibU/BioY ( Karpowich and Wang 2013 ). RibU binds riboflavin with high affinity, and the protein-substrate complex is exceptionally stable in solution. The crystal structure of riboflavin-bound RibU reveals an electronegative binding pocket at the extracellular surface in which the substrate is completely buried ( Karpowich et al. 2016 ).

BioM, EtcA, ATPase, 234 aas; BioN, EtcT, 190 aas, 5 TMSs; BioY, EtcS, 210 aas, 5 TMSs BioY can also function as a secondary carrier and is therefore listed separately under TC# 2.A.88.1.3. ATP-dependent conformational changes drive substrate capture and release when BioMNY are together in a complex ( Finkenwirth et al. 2015 ).
3.A.1.25.7.name: The riboflavin uptake system, BioMNY.

The membrane-intrinsic protein ABCI12 may be the interaction partner for…

In the crystal…

3.A.1.3.13.name: Uptake system for L-cystine (Km=2.5 μM), L-cystathionine, L-djenkolate

3.A.1.3.15.name: Putative uptake system for arginine, YqiXYZ

3.A.1.3.16.name: Uptake system for glutamate and aspartate.

3.A.1.3.18.name: Acidic and neutral amino acid uptake transporter NatFGH/BgtA.

3.A.1.3.22.name: Amino acid transporter, AatJMQP.

3.A.1.3.28.name: Putative amino acid uptake porter, YckIJK; deletion of YckK (substrate binding protein) increases sensitivity to the antimicrobial peptide, cecropin.

3.A.1.4.3.description: General L- (and D-)amino acid uptake porter (transports acidic, basic, polar, semipolar and hydrophobic amino acids). 3.D.5.1.1.description: Na + -translocating NADH-quinone oxidoreductase, NqrABCDEF ( Steuber et al. 2014 ). Evolution of the Na + -NQR complex may have involved functional divergence from its RNF homologue (3.D.6) following duplication of the rnf operon, loss of the rnfB gene and the recruitment of the reductase subunit of an aromatic monooxygenase. Two additional proteins, ApbE and NqrM (DUF539), are essential for…

3.D.6.1.2.description: The Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RnfABCDEG ( Imkamp et al ., 2007 ). Note: RnfD may be truncated as almost all homologues have 300-330aas with 6-7 TMSs. This system has been shown to pump Na + out of the cell when reducing NAD + with reduced ferredoxin, and dependent on the smf for reduction of ferredoxin with NADH 2 ( Hess et al. 2013 ).
3.D.6.1.2.name: The Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RnfABCDEG.

3.D.6.1.3.description: The Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RnfABCDEG/MA0658 ( Welte and Deppenmeier 2013 ). RnfB and RnfC are on the cytoplasmic side of the membrane. Both have 4Fe4S centers (5 and 2, repectively), and RnfB oxidizes reduced ferredoxin ( Suharti et al. 2014 ). The integral membrane proteins are RnfA, D and E, while RnfG and MA0658 are on the outside. RnfE reduces oxidized Mph ( Welte and Deppenmeier 2013 ).
3.D.6.1.3.name: The Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RnfABCDEG/MA0658.

3.D.6.1.4.description: Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RsxA, RsxD, RsxE, RsxG, RsxB, RsxC of 6, 10, 5, 1, 1 and 1 TMSs, respectively.
3.D.6.1.4.name: Rnf-type NADH dehydrogenase, RsxA, RsxD, RsxE, RsxG, RsxB, RsxC of 6, 10, 5, 1, 1 and 1 TMSs, respectively.

3.D.6.1.5.description: Na + -translocating ferredoxin:NAD + reductase (RnfABCDEG) complex. The 6 subunits have 191, 274, 435, 310, 201 and 189 aas, respectively ( Vitt et al. 2022 ). Microbial metabolism often uses H + /Na + -translocating ferredoxin:NAD + reductase (Rnf), either to exergonically oxidize reduced ferredoxin by NAD + for generating a transmembrane electrochemical potential, or reversely to exploit the…
3.D.6.1.5.name: Na + -translocating ferredoxin:NAD + reductase (RnfABCDEG) complex.

3.D.7.1.1.description: H 2 :heterodisulfide oxidoreductase, HHO. Two protons are consumed in the cytoplasm while two protons are released in the periplasm, contributing to the pmf ( Simon et al. , 2008 ; Welte and Deppenmeier 2013 ). The HdrD/E-type heterodisulfide reductase probably can function independently of the other subunits.
3.D.7.1.1.name: H 2 :heterodisulfide oxidoreductase, HHO.

3.D.7.1.2.name: Putative heterodisulfide oxidoreductase, HdrDE.

3.D.7.1.3.name: Putative heterodisulfide reductase, HdrDE.

3.D.7.1.7.name: The Hdr or Vho complex with 5 constituent proteins, HdrA - E: Dihydromethanophenazine:CoB--CoM heterodisulfide reductase.

Only the following constituents were found in the NCBI protein database: (1) CoB-CoM heterodisulfide reductase and its iron-sulfur subunit: subunit A2 and subunit B, and the 5,10-methylene THF reductase (NADPH) with acc#s SCM80793.1, SCM80794.1 and SSCM80790.1.
3.D.7.1.8.name: The H 2 -methylene THF reductase electron transfer chain.

3.D.7.2.1.description: Membrane-bound H 2 oxidizing hydrogenase, HydAB ( Guiral et al ., 2005 ). HydC has not been identified, but adjacent to hydB is an open reading frame (ORF; AAC07057; 226aas) showing similarity to cytochromes that could be HydC.
3.D.7.2.1.name: Membrane-bound H 2 oxidizing hydrogenase, HydAB.

Two protons are consumed in the cytoplasm while two protons are released in the periplasm, contributing to the pmf ( Simon et al. , 2008 ).
3.D.7.2.2.name: Membrane-bound Ni/Fe-hydrogenase complex, HydABC.

3.D.7.2.3.description: Hydrogenase HyaABCDEF, important for H 2 oxidation during fermentation ( Zbell and Maier 2009 ).
3.D.7.2.3.name: Hydrogenase HyaABCDEF, important for H 2 oxidation during fermentation.

3.D.7.2.4.name: F420-non reducing hydrogenase subunits A, D and G of 472, 141, and 308 aas, respectively, with 0, 0 and 3-5 TMSs, respectively.

3.D.7.2.5.description: Hydrogenase-2, HybABCDEFG including the subunits of the hydrogenase as well as three maturation proteins (HybD, HybF and HybG).
3.D.7.2.5.name: Hydrogenase-2, HybABCDEFG including the subunits of the hydrogenase as well as three maturation proteins (HybD, HybF and HybG).

Proton efflux occurs via a transient linear water-molecule chain in a hydrophobic section of the Brho channel between Asp96 and Asp85 ( Freier et al. , 2011 ). Local-global conformational coupling in brho has been proposed as a transport mechanism from crystal structures of the nine states in the bacteriorhodopsin photocycle ( Lanyi and Schobert 2004 ). The protein can be…
3.E.1.1.1.name: Bacteriorhodopsin.

3.E.1.1.10.description: Schizorhodopsin of 202 aas and 7 TMSs. The crystal structure reveals the mechanism of inward proton pumping ( Higuchi et al. 2021 ). Schizorhodopsins (SzRs), a new rhodopsin family identified in Asgard archaea, are phylogenetically located at an intermediate position between type-1 microbial rhodopsins and heliorhodopsins. SzRs work as light-driven inward H + pumps ( Higuchi et al. 2021 )…
3.E.1.1.10.name: Schizorhodopsin of 202 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.11.description: Mastigocladopsis repens rhodopsin chloride pump (inward pumping). The 3-d structure is known to 3.3 Å resolution ( Besaw et al. 2020 ). It may transport both Cl - and Br - ( Kikukawa 2021 ).
3.E.1.1.11.name: Mastigocladopsis repens rhodopsin chloride pump (inward pumping).

3.E.1.1.13.description: Xenorhodopsinof 229 aas and 7 TMSs. The structures have been determined for all intermediates of the photocycle; 7ZNB, C, D, E, G, H and I, all A - C. Thus, a comprehensive function-structure study of the light-driven bacterial inward proton pump, xenorhodopsin from Bacillus coahuilensis, in all major proton-conducting states was carried out ( Kovalev et al. 2023 ). The structures revealed that…
3.E.1.1.13.name: Xenorhodopsinof 229 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.14.description: Synechocystis halorhodopsin of 234 aas and 7 TMSs. The 3-D structure is known ( Astashkin et al. 2022 ). MRs can pump various monovalent ions like Na + , K + , Cl -, I-, and NO 3 -. The only characterized MR proposed to pump sulfate in addition to halides belongs to the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 7509 and is named Synechocystis halorhodopsin (SyHR). Astashkin et al. 2022 presented the…
3.E.1.1.14.name: Synechocystis halorhodopsin of 234 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.15.description: Schizorhodopsin 4 of 110 aas and 7 TMSs. The protein pumps H + into the cytoplasm of the cell. Cis-trans reisomerization preceding reprotonation of the retinal chromophore Is common to the schizorhodopsin family. A simple and rational mechanism for inward proton pumping has been proosed ( Urui et al. 2024 ), and the 3-D structure is known ( Higuchi et al. 2021 ).
3.E.1.1.15.name: Schizorhodopsin 4 of 110 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.17.description: Cyanorhodopsin, CyR, of 254 aas and 7 TMSs. These proteins are found in non-marine cyanobacterial strains. They catalyze light-driven outward H+ pumping ( Hasegawa et al. 2020 ).
3.E.1.1.17.name: Cyanorhodopsin, CyR, of 254 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.18.description: Glycy lhalorhodopsin is an anion pumping microbial rhodopsin. It is 260 aas long with 7 TMSs. It takes up anions including chloride and sulfate. The function of many microbial rhodopsins is determined by three residues in the third transmembrane helix called motif residues. Ishizuka et al. 2024 reported a group of microbial rhodopsins with a novel Thr–Thr–Gly (TTG) motif. They function as…
3.E.1.1.18.name: Glycy lhalorhodopsin is an anion pumping microbial rhodopsin.

3.E.1.1.19.description: Glycylhalorhodopsins (GHR) of Salinarimonas soli of 263 aas and 7 TMSs ( Ishizuka et al. 2024 ). See 3.E.1.1.18 for details. This system transports anions including chloride and sulfate in the inward direction. X-ray crystallographic analysis found large cavities on the cytoplasmic side, which are produced by the small side-chain volume of the glycine residue in the TTG motif in TMS3. The opened…
3.E.1.1.19.name: Glycylhalorhodopsins (GHR) of Salinarimonas soli of 263 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.20.description: A light-driven Li + /Na + -pumping rhodopsin with a DTG motifhas been characterized. It is of 250 aas and has 7 TMSs. The MpR E33Q mutant transported H + in place of Li + /Na + , suggesting that Glu33 is a Li + /Na + binding site on the cytoplasmic side. Gly93 in MpR was replaced by Asp to convert it from the Li + /Na + pump to an H + pump ( Cho et al. 2021 ).
3.E.1.1.20.name: A light-driven Li + /Na + -pumping rhodopsin with a DTG motifhas been characterized.

3.E.1.1.3.description: "Middle" rhodopsin or bacteriorhodopsin 1 (Brhol); it has 11-cis-retinal and shows intermediate properties between Brho and sensory rhodopsin II ( Sudo et al. , 2011 ). Its structure is known to 2.0 Å resolution following crystalization using polymer-bounded lipid nanodiscs ( Broecker et al. 2017 ). It may pump Cl - and Br - into the cell ( Kikukawa 2021 ). See also Ko et al. 2022 .
3.E.1.1.3.name: "Middle" rhodopsin or bacteriorhodopsin 1 (Brhol); it has 11-cis-retinal and shows intermediate properties between Brho and sensory rhodopsin II.

3.E.1.1.5.description: Bacteriorhodopsin I (HmBRI) of 250 aas and 7 TMSs. The structure is known to 2.5 Å resolution, revealing the usual BRI fold but with several modifications ( Shevchenko et al. 2014 ). Expression in E. coli membranes does not affect the overall structure.
3.E.1.1.5.name: Bacteriorhodopsin I (HmBRI) of 250 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.6.description: Sensory rhodopsin (green-light-activated photoreceptor; does not transport ions) ( Jung et al ., 2003 ). Has all- trans -retinal when dark adapted, but 11- cis -retinal when light adapted due to reversible interconversion ( Sineshchekov et al ., 2005 ). Anabaena sensory rhodopsin, a photochromic sensor that interacts with a soluble 14-kDa cytoplasmic transducer that is encoded on the same operon…
3.E.1.1.6.name: Sensory rhodopsin (green-light-activated photoreceptor; does not transport ions).

3.E.1.1.7.description: H + -pumping electrogenic bacteriorhodopsin of 250 aas and 7 TMSs ( Kamo et al. 2006 ). The delta rhodopsin (dR), a microbial light-driven proton-pumping rhodopsin from Haloterrigena turkmenica , was expressed and localized in the vacuolar membrane of Saccharomyces cerevisiae by conjugation with a vacuolar membrane-localized protein. Vacuoles with dR were isolated from S. cerevisiae , and the…
3.E.1.1.7.name: H + -pumping electrogenic bacteriorhodopsin of 250 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.8.description: Inward H + pumping xenorhodopsin (bacteriorhodopsin) of 228 aas and 7 TMSs.
3.E.1.1.8.name: Inward H + pumping xenorhodopsin (bacteriorhodopsin) of 228 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.1.9.description: Rhodopsin, RxR, of 239 aas and 7 TMSs. This rhodopsin is from the thermophilic eubacterium Rubrobacter xylanophilus DSM 9941(T) and was isolated from thermally polluted water. Although R. xylanophilus rhodopsin (RxR) is from an Actinobacterium, it is located between eukaryotic and archaeal rhodopsins in the phylogenetic tree ( Kanehara et al. 2017 ). Helix movement is required to create the Cl - entrance path on the…
3.E.1.2.2.name: Chloride-pumping halorhodopsin.

3.E.1.3.2.name: Sensory rhodopsin II or photoreceptor phoborhodopsin (ppR).

3.E.1.3.3.description: Sensory rhodopsin II, SR2 (Sop2; ppR), also called Pharaonis phoborhodopsin. The NMR solution structure of the detergent solubilized protein is in good agreement with the x-ray structure ( Gautier et al. 2010 ). 3.E.1.3.3.name: Sensory rhodopsin II, SR2 (Sop2; ppR), also called Pharaonis phoborhodopsin.

3.E.1.4.3.name: H + pumping rhodopsin (opsin; Ops), of 313 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.4.4.description: Acetaularia rhodopsin I, ARI or c102333 of 246 aas. It exhibits outward H + pumping activity, and D89 and D100 are essential for pumping activity ( Lee et al. 2015 ). Blue-light causes a shunt of the photocycle under H + reuptake from the extracellular side ( Tsunoda et al. 2006 ). Similarities and differences of AR with BR have been revealed by detailed electrophysiological studies, revealing…
3.E.1.4.4.name: Acetaularia rhodopsin I, ARI or c102333 of 246 aas.

3.E.1.4.6.description: Possible chaperone membrane protein related to Hsp30, Mrh1 (320 aas; 33% identical to Hsp30p). This protein and its two paralogues, Hsp30 and YR02, are induced by heat shock and are present primarily in the plasma membrane ( Wu et al. 2000 ). It plays a role in acetic acid tolerance and may be an acetic acid exporter ( Takabatake et al. 2015 ).
3.E.1.4.6.name: Possible chaperone membrane protein related to Hsp30, Mrh1 (320 aas; 33% identical to Hsp30p).

3.E.1.4.7.description: Cyanorhodopsin of 334 aas and 7 TMSs, Ops1 ( Frassanito et al. 2010 ).

3.E.1.4.8.description: Yro2 of 344 aas and 7 TMSs. Plays a role in acetic acid tolereance and is induced by acetic acid stress and by entry into the stationary phase. It is 72% identical to Mrh1 (TC# 3.E.1.4.6) which is also believed to be involved in the acetic acid stress response ( Takabatake et al. 2015 ).
3.E.1.4.8.name: Yro2 of 344 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.5.1.description: Bacterio-rhodopsin/guanylyl cyclase 1 fusion protein of 626 aas; light-activated enzyme, RhCG, Gc1 or Cyc1Op. The central bacteriorhodopsin domain with 7 TMSs is linked via an additional TMS to the C-terminal adenylate/guanylate cyclase catalytic domain. CyclOp enables precise and rapid optogenetic manipulation of cGMP levels in cells and animals ( Gao et al. 2015 ).
3.E.1.5.1.name: Bacterio-rhodopsin/guanylyl cyclase 1 fusion protein of 626 aas; light-activated enzyme, RhCG, Gc1 or Cyc1Op.

3.E.1.6.12.name: Blue-light absorbing proteorhodopsin (BPR) of 251 aas and 8 TMSs including a cleavable N-terminal TMS.

3.E.1.6.13.name: Viral rhodopsin II (RhoII) of 211 aas and 7 TMSs, OLPVRII, a VirChR1, a Na + /K + channel that does not transport Ca 2+.

3.E.1.6.14.description: Chloride (Cl - ) pumping rhodopsin of 272 aas and 7 TMSs. It may pump Cl - , Br - , I - , and NO3 - ( Kikukawa 2021 ).
3.E.1.6.14.name: Chloride (Cl - ) pumping rhodopsin of 272 aas and 7 TMSs.

3.E.1.6.15.description: Bellilinea Na + -pumping rhodopsin, BeNaR, of 269 aas and 7 TMSs. Kurihara et al. 2023 identified and characterized a rhodopsin from a thermophilic bacterium, Bellilinea sp. 3.E.1.6.2.name: Xanthorhodopsin, a proton pump with a carotenoid antenna, salinixanthin.

3.E.1.6.3.name: Gloeobacter rhodopsin (GT) of 298 aas and 7 TMSs (associates with salinixanthin, the light-harvesting carotenoid antenna of xanthorhodopsin).

3.E.1.6.6.description: Proton pumping proteorhodopsin of 253 aas ( Kimura et al. 2011 ).
